News.title: Myanmar releases rare images of Aung San Suu Kyi after King Charles’s dramatic intervention
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

King Charles III has made an extraordinary and personal intervention in the case of Myanmar’s detained leader Aung San Suu Kyi, reaching out with diplomatic correspondence to her undisclosed location under house arrest in the capital Naypyitaw.

The Myanmar regime released rare photographs of Ms Suu Kyi on Monday as she received the King’s correspondence, which included a sealed letter and two books on environmental matters.

It marks an exceptionally rare insight into the conditions of Ms Suu Kyi’s detention, with only a couple of other images released by the military-backed government in the five years since she was ousted in a coup.

The new photographs, which were released by the junta on social media, show the 81-year-old former state counsellor wearing a traditional blouse and skirt, seated across a small table from two officials in a wood-panelled room.

According to Myanmar’s presidential press and information bureau, home ministry officials delivered the books to Ms Suu Kyi in a 10-minute meeting, along with a sealed envelope with correspondence from the King.

open image in gallery Myanmar's former leader Aung San Suu Kyi receives books and a letter from Britain's King Charles from a Myanmar official in Naypyitaw, Myanmar ( Reuters )

The books were The Land Gardeners: Soil to Table, by British authors Bridget Elworthy and Henrietta Courtauld, which explores how healthy soil helps produce healthy food. The second, Soil: The World at Our Feet, is a catalogue from an exhibition at London’s Somerset House about the importance of soil to life on Earth.

No further information on the letter has not been disclosed, and authorities have not explained how the books were sent.

Ms Suu Kyi, who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1991 for her campaign for democracy, was arrested in February 2021 when Myanmar’s military seized power from her elected government in a coup. She was subsequently convicted of multiple offences, including corruption, incitement, and election fraud, in trials that have been criticised by her supporters and human rights groups as politically motivated.

open image in gallery Then-Prince Charles and Camilla met Aung San Suu Kyi at Clarence House in London in May 2017 ( PA )

Ms Suu Kyi has denied wrongdoing and dismissed the charges as “absurd”.

The Independent released its award-winning documentary Cancelled: The Rise and Fall of Aung San Suu Kyi in December 2024, examining the controversial former Myanmar leader’s political career and legacy. The film is being screened this week at 6.30pm on Tuesday 20 October at the Institute of Contemporary Arts in London.

In April 2026, the regime reduced her sentence through a series of amnesties, bringing the remaining term to 18 years, and transferred her from prison to house arrest. Her exact location has not been disclosed, and concerns about her health persist.

open image in gallery The books were The Land Gardeners: Soil to Table , by British authors Bridget Elworthy and Henrietta Courtauld, and Soil: The World at Our Feet ( Reuters )

In August, Ms Suu Kyi met a representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross, her first known contact with an independent international humanitarian organisation since her detention.

Ms Suu Kyi’s younger son Kim Aris welcomed Charles’s “thoughtful gesture” but said it should not distract from his mother’s continued detention. “I take comfort in knowing that my mother remains in the thoughts of His Majesty King Charles III, and I sincerely appreciate his kind gesture in sending her books,” he told Radio Free Asia on Monday.

He continued: “However, we must not allow the military regime to use such selective disclosures to create an illusion of normality or gain international legitimacy. A gesture of kindness should never be used to distract from the continued violation of my mother’s fundamental human rights.”

Mr Aris said that the family still has “no direct communication with her or credible, independently verified information about her health and wellbeing”.

He urged governments engaging with Myanmar’s military chief-turned-president Min Aung Hlaing to press for regular contact between Ms Suu Kyi and her family, independent medical access, and her “immediate and unconditional release, together with all political prisoners”.

open image in gallery Kim Aris, son of Aung San Suu Kyi, speaks to supporters before taking part in a run on his mother's 80th birthday, to raise awareness of her ongoing incarceration, in Hyde Park in London ( AFP/Getty )

Myanmar’s government has been trying to end its international isolation since the 2021 coup, which brought the country’s top general to power.

Min Aung Hlaing named himself president in April 2026 following a sham election in which any genuine political opponents, including Ms Suu Kyi and her party, were barred from taking part.

He has since aggressively pursued the normalisation of diplomatic ties with other countries, carrying out visits to neighbours including Laos, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia and Malaysia.

Myanmar’s military leaders have been excluded from high-level Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summits since the coup, however, after failing to implement a regional peace plan intended to end the violence and encourage dialogue. Its regime remains largely isolated on the world stage.

Min Aung Hlaing also remains under US sanctions for human rights abuses, including for his role in the coup and crushing a subsequent popular uprising, and the 2016-2017 mass killings and expulsions of Rohingya Muslims that Washington declared a genocide.

open image in gallery Myanmar’s government has been trying to end its international isolation since the 2021 coup, which brought the country’s then military chief Min Aung Hlaing to power ( AP )

In September, Mr Aris hand-delivered a letter to the Myanmar embassy in London appealing for her freedom.

“She symbolises freedom and democracy in a country taken over by and run by the rule of military law. The world cannot allow democracy to be snuffed out and for my mother not to be freed,” Mr Aris told The Independent at the time. “At her age it is the equivalent of execution to keep her hidden and locked up.”

News.title: Andrew Lloyd Webber songs ‘ditched’ from show with Tim Rice after fallout
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Andrew Lloyd Webber and Tim Rice, one of the UK’s most successful creative duos, appear to have fallen out over a new project.

The pair have worked together on some of the biggest hits in musical theatre, from Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat to Evita and Jesus Christ Superstar, picking up multiple awards including dual “EGOT” status, with Joseph, Superstar, and Evita collectively winning Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, and Tony Awards.

So it will come as a shock to fans that Lloyd Webber has apparently withdrawn his music from a production of Sherlock Holmes and the 12 Days of Christmas, which premiered at the Birmingham Rep theatre last year to positive reviews.

The project, a murder mystery about a serial killer bumping off the cast of West End shows in the run-up to the festive season, marked Lloyd Webber and Rice’s first collaboration in 40 years.

Rice told the Times on Wednesday (21 October) that his former partner’s songs had been “ditched” after Lloyd Webber allegedly withdrew his score.

“Andrew really didn’t want to continue with the show,” he said. “He basically withdrew his score. He really did not feel it was the sort of thing he wanted to do. Andrew is more concerned with much bigger productions.”

open image in gallery Rice (left) and Lloyd Webber form one of the UK’s most successful creative partnerships ( Getty )

However, in his own statement to the publication, Lloyd Webber disputed this account and said the show’s producers, Donald and Eva Rice – the children of Tim Rice – had “decided not to use the music I composed for the Birmingham production for two reasons”.

He claimed that he was told further work was needed on the project, which would have been “impossible” with his schedule.

Lloyd Webber also alleged that he was asked to “sign away” his rights in advance for five years “without any right of approval over its use in a production I hadn’t seen and with a team I had never worked with before!”

He said that the two issues meant that he felt he was not being granted “basic approval which even a rookie writer would expect”.

The Independent has contacted Rice’s representatives for further comment.

Lloyd Webber had previously warned that he and Rice were unlikely to team up for a full musical again: “I mean,” he told the Times, “Tim doesn’t need to. He’s written The Lion King.”

open image in gallery Lloyd Webber claimed he was asked to ‘sign his rights away’ for five years ( PA )

His own website describes Rice as one of his “great collaborators”. They first met in 1965 when Rice, then an aspiring lyricist, wrote to Lloyd Webber who was seeking a writing partner.

“I was told you were looking for a ‘with it’ writer of lyrics,” he wrote. “I wondered if you consider it worth your while meeting me. I may fall far short of your requirements, but anyway, it would be interesting to meet up – I hope!”

The pair’s first production was inspired by the biblical story of Joseph, to which they applied their smart blend of rock, pop and calypso to a full-length production that opened at the Edinburgh International Festival in 1972.

Joseph… opened later that year in London’s West End at the Roundhouse, starring Gary Bond as Joseph, and has since gone on to become one of the most successful musicals, with a long-running Broadway production and a 1999 film adaptation starring Donny Osmond.

Separately, Lloyd Webber is also known as the mastermind behind hit musicals including The Phantom of the Opera, Cats, Sunset Boulevard, Starlight Express and School of Rock, while Rice is renowned as the lyricist to the Lion King songs “Circle of Life” and “Can You Feel the Love Tonight”, the latter winning him and Elton John an Oscar for Best Original Song in 1995.

News.title: Country music legend John Anderson dies aged 71
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

John Anderson, the country music star behind hits including “Swingin’,” “Seminole Wind” and “Straight Tequila Night,” has died aged 71.

The singer died peacefully in his sleep on Wednesday, October 21, his family confirmed in a statement shared on social media. No cause of death has been announced.

The highly influential musician had only recently attended the 2026 Country Music Hall of Fame induction ceremony on October 18.

A statement on the musician’s Instagram page read: “It is with the heaviest of hearts that we share the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and best friend.

“To the world, he was a gifted country music singer whose voice and songs touched countless lives. To us, he was so much more. He was the heart of our family, the one who made us laugh, loved us fiercely, and made every ordinary moment feel special.

“We are completely heartbroken.

open image in gallery John Anderson attended the 2026 Country Music Hall of Fame induction ceremony on October 18, just three days before his death ( Getty )

“His music will live on, but for us, his greatest legacy will always be the love he gave his family and the memories we will carry with us forever.

“Please keep our family in your thoughts and prayers as we grieve this unimaginable loss.”

Tributes have flooded in for the beloved star from across generations.

Tim McGraw, who only caught up with John at the ceremony in Nashville at the weekend, shared: “I was talking with John Sunday night at the HOF ceremony.

Alongside a picture of the pair at the event, he shared to Instagram: “He was in such good spirits. We talked, we laughed, we sang his songs that I loved so much together, just goofing off.”

The 59-year-old star continued: “I am completely heartbroken by his passing.

“There will never be a stylist in music, any music, that was so defining as his. It’s just devastating. All of our love goes out to his family and the country music community. He was and is one of the defining voices in country music. So great. I am completely shook.”

No Doubt frontwoman Gwen Stefani, 57, commented underneath the family's official statement: “We loved him!! His music is part of our family's hearts forever!! Gx.”

Country veteran Reba McEntire, 71, wrote: “One of my favorite people in this business. I sure will miss you, John. Love you and your music always.”

Jason Aldean, 49, said: “One of my all time favorites. I Grew up listening and learning to play guitar on all my dad’s old John Anderson albums. I was Lucky enough to have met and performed with him a few times over the years. Sending Thoughts and prayers to the family. He was a great one. You’ll be missed bud.”

Luke Combs, 36, wrote: “Damn. Rest easy John. Thanks for the songs.”

John began his recording career in 1976 when Warner Bros. Records brought him onto its roster. Within a few years he was on major national tours, joining Merle Haggard and Willie Nelson in the early 1980s.

During his starry career, the musician earned five number-one singles, including 1983’s “Swingin’” - which spent one week at the top of the Hot Country Songs charts. The hit went gold and received a Single of the Year award from the Country Music Association.

In the Nineties, he scored hits with Straight Tequila Night and Seminole Wind.

John was inducted into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2014 and the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2024.

News.title: Tour de France 2027 routes unveiled as Britain hosts Grand Depart and Montmartre returns
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The full route for the 2027 Tour de France and Tour de France Femmes have been unveiled, with a double-header of the Col du Tourmalet and Col du Portet featuring on a brutal queen stage for the men’s race, while the women tackle the iconic Puy de Dome.

Race organisers ASO revealed the course design at a presentation at the Palais des Congres in Paris on Thursday.

The men’s race runs from Friday 2 July to Sunday 25 July, with three race days rather than the customary two and a three-day opening week. The women’s race begins on Friday 30 July 30 and runs until Saturday 7 August.

The Grand Depart for both editions is to take place in Britain and had already been announced, with 2027 marking the first time that both races will begin in the same country outside France.

Stage one of the Tour travels from Edinburgh to Carlisle, with stage two from Keswick to Liverpool and stage three from Welshpool to Cardiff, before the extra rest day on the first Monday of the race to allow for the transfer to France.

Once on the mainland the race continues in Cherbourg, heading out of Normandy through well-known host towns Plumelec and Vannes before the first of two individual time trials in Chambord. The mountain stages begin on stage nine’s ride to Grand Colombier, with a rest day in Haute-Savoie leading to another two days in the Alps including the climbs of the Cote de Dormancy and Les Saisies.

open image in gallery Tour de France 2027 route map ( ASO )

The final week begins with a 33km ITT in Toulouse before moving south into the final mountainous battleground, the Pyrenees. Jumping off from Pau, stage 18 is the most brutal, taking in the Col du Portet and the infamous Col du Torumalet, which feature on the same stage for the first time, with Le Soulor and the Hourquette d’Ancizan adding to an already gruelling queen stage.

The climbing continues in the Basque Country before a long transfer back up north to Paris. The final stage begins in Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines, home of the Paris Olympics velodrome, and once again visits the hugely popular Montmartre, with three circuits of the punchy climb before a 10km run to the traditional finish line on the Champs-Elysees.

As well as two ITTs totalling 71km - the longest time against the clock of any edition since 2012 - there are seven flat stages, six hilly stages, and six days in the mountains including three summit finishes - on the Grand Colombier, Les Saisies and Saint-Lary-Soulan Col du Portet - on the parcours.

open image in gallery Tour de France 2027 stage 18 profile ( ASO )

In total the riders will tackle 53,450m of climbing across the Massif Central, Jura, Alps and Pyrenees, traversing 3,479km in total.

Overall this route has followed the trend of recent Tours: another mountainous challenge tailor-made for five-time champion Tadej Pogacar, who will resume hostilities with Jonas Vingegaard as he targets a sixth title. The amount of time-trialling on the route will also appeal to Olympic and world champion Remco Evenepoel, who finished second this year.

The Tour de France Femmes will begin in Leeds - harking back to the Grand Depart of the 2014 men’s race - with a flat stage to Manchester before a tough day out in the Peak District and a first-ever team time trial in central London, featuring landmarks including Westminster, St Paul’s Cathedral and Trafalgar Square before finishing on The Mall.

The sixth edition of the women’s race has stuck with the nine-day schedule from last year but with an additional rest day to allow for the transfer to France.

open image in gallery Tour de France Femmes 2027 map ( ASO )

The peloton will then head to France with a flat stage from Le Touquet to Calais, with the race visiting Orleans and Clermont-Ferrand as it travels southwards, with the queen stage coming on its last day and finishing atop Puy de Dome, which makes its debut, in the Massif Central.

There are only two mountain stages on the agenda, both summit finishes, the first on stage seven at La Loge des Gardes, and no individual time trial.

The queen stage features 3,840m of elevation gain but while there are two ‘hilly’ stages which promise general classification action, overall this is a less dramatic route on paper compared to previous years’ - in particular the 2026 edition, which featured more than 1,000m more climbing and a spectacular queen stage to the summit of Mont Ventoux.

open image in gallery Tour de France Femmes 2027 - stage nine profile ( ASO )

In total the race covers 1,156km, with the longest day coming on stage nine at 170km from Clermont-Ferrand to Puy de Dome, an 11.3km climb averaging 7.8%.

The layout of this race, with the toughest stage on the final day, means the battle for the yellow jersey is highly likely to be decided at its very end - setting up a grandstand finish.

The last three stages are the toughest, with chances for breakaway specialists and Classics-style riders on the Ardennes-style stage five and two chances for the pure sprinters before the backloaded finale.

This year’s champion Demi Vollering of FDJ United-Suez is set to renew her rivalry with 2024 winner Kasia Niewiadoma, who is moving to Lidl-Trek in the off-season, as the Dutchwoman seeks a third title at the sport’s biggest race.

News.title: Questions grow after Saudi Arabia executes two Bangladeshis for ‘immoral act’ in Mecca mosque
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Two Bangladeshi nationals were executed in Saudi Arabia on 14 October for allegedly committing an “immoral act” inside a mosque.

The Bangladesh consulate in Jeddah reportedly received a list of about 2,500 prisoners from Saudi authorities in September, which included the two Bangladeshis but did not disclose their death sentences.

A confidential memo from Bangladesh’s consulate – that Dhaka’s The Daily Star gained access to – revealed that the records it received listed entirely different allegations against them, without mentioning the death sentences.

There were allegations of adultery against Suety Akhter, 24, and an offence under the cybercrime law against Nazrul Islam Abdul Basir, 22, reportedly leaving the consular officials unable to link the entries to the executions, the outlet revealed.

Dhaka learnt of the executions only after they were carried out on 14 October.

The prisoners’ list reportedly sent to the consulate on 30 September showed that Basir had been detained on 1 August 2023 under Saudi Arabia’s cybercrime law, while Akhter was arrested a day later over allegations of adultery.

The memo said Basir was held at the Jeddah correctional facility and Akhter at Jeddah’s women’s prison. Both had worked as cleaners for a company named Al Majal.

After the executions were carried out, Bangladesh subsequently summoned the Saudi ambassador to seek details.

open image in gallery File. Muslims walk at the Grand Mosque in the holy city of Mecca, Saudi Arabia ( Reuters )

The Bangladesh consulate also requested copies of the court judgments and information about the proceedings.

Saudi authorities classified the Bangladeshis’ death sentences as ta’zir, a form of punishment left to judicial discretion, and said the executions followed a judicial review and a royal order. However, their public statement did not specify what the alleged “immoral act” involved, name of the mosque where it took place, or state when the pair were arrested.

Earlier, Saudi Arabia’s interior ministry said the two were executed after being convicted of an “immoral act” inside a mosque in Mecca.

The Saudi interior ministry reportedly said the government remained committed to safeguarding and enforcing Islamic law against those found to have violated the sanctity of mosques.

It also warned that anyone committing similar offences would be punished under Saudi law, Gulf News reported.

The memo reportedly said that 306 Bangladeshis were in prison across Saudi Arabia’s western region, with 147 serving sentences of between one month and 15 years. It also listed three cybercrime cases in which the prisoners had received jail terms of six months to five years.

Akhter, originally a resident of Nagar Chhawali village in Mirzapur, was arrested in August 2023 but only informed her family about her detention a year later. Initially, she had reportedly told them she had been held following a physical altercation.

“She sent money home for the first five months. One day, she called and told us she had been sent to jail,” her father Fazal Mia told The Daily Star.

“The family later learned that she had been arrested in connection with a relationship with a young man there,” a local police official in her hometown was quoted as saying by The Telegraph.

Her last conversation with her family was on 13 October, a day before her execution.

“She told them she would return home within the next two and a half months. She was unaware of her execution,” the official allegedly said.

Her father told the local media that she was falsely accused and jailed after a dispute with other female workers in Saudi Arabia. The family then heard nothing from her for about a year.

She later resumed contact, calling home roughly once a month, but never mentioned her trial or the sentence she received.

Akhter’s mother, Johura, has said that her daughter was divorced and had a four-year-old daughter. When Akhter moved to Saudi Arabia, her daughter was taken care of by her Akhter’s sister.

open image in gallery A man looks at a screen displaying the flight schedule at the Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka on 12 October 2026 as Saudi Arabia-bound flights remain cancelled a day after a Houthi strike at Riyadh's international airport ( AFP/Getty )

The family has allegedly not received any official confirmation from the Bangladesh government.

The 22-year-old man, Basir, moved to Saudi Arabia in November 2022 and was the eldest of four siblings. He came from Birampur village in Bangladesh’s Brahmanbaria district. His family has alleged that he contacted them six months after he was arrested, saying he had been arrested and falsely accused, but offered no further details.

His father Abdul Basir told The Daily Star: “If my son was executed without just cause, I want justice.”

The Bangladesh government has yet to officially confirm the identities of the two people executed in Saudi Arabia and has reportedly sought an explanation from Riyadh over the alleged failure to share information. Over 3.5 million Bangladeshis work in Saudi Arabia.

The Independent has reached out to Saudi Arabia’s foreign affairs ministry for comment.

State minister for foreign affairs Humaiun Kobir said the government was seeking further details.

The Independent has reached out to the Bangladesh mission in Riyadh for comment.

The Human Rights Support Society (HRSS) has called for an impartial investigation and accountability over the executions. The organisation raised concerns over reports that Bangladesh’s foreign ministry and diplomatic missions were not informed before the executions.

According to The Dhaka Tribune, HRSS has demanded the disclosure of the charges, trial records and sentences, along with details of the legal assistance the pair received.

It also called on the government to investigate possible negligence by the relevant ministries, take action against those responsible if wrongdoing is established, improve coordination between diplomatic missions and ensure access to qualified lawyers for Bangladeshis facing serious charges abroad.

“The responsibilities of the relevant ministries in protecting the rights of expatriate citizens cannot be limited to mere formalities,” HRSS executive director Ejazul Islam said in a statement.

“If there has been any negligence or failure in this matter, accountability must be established, and those responsible must be held answerable.”

News.title: ‘Cockroach’ party leaders released after seven days in custody over Delhi protests
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The leaders of India’s “cockroach” movement were released on Wednesday after spending over a week in preventive custody after they waved the Indian flag at a newly de-notified protest site.

A special executive magistrate in Delhi ordered the release of Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka on the condition that they would not call for further protests at Jantar Mantar while the site remains de-notified.

The two leaders of the youth-led movement under Cockroach Janta Party had been detained after allegedly climbing over a locked gate and entering the barricaded protest site on 13 October, carrying the Indian national flag, and raising slogans against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

They were subsequently remanded to judicial custody on 14 October, with their detention extended by two days on 19 October.

Their release came after they submitted written undertakings.

open image in gallery Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokespersons Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka walk out from a police station as they seek approval for a protest demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar ( AFP/Getty )

“We will not make any calls for protest at Jantar Mantar till such a time that it is de-notified in accordance with law. That we further reiterate that any protest undertaken would be done within the four corners of the Constitution,” the undertaking stated.

The magistrate also directed the two men to furnish personal bonds and surety bonds of Rs 50,000 each. They are due to appear before the court again on 23 October, when the police are expected to submit a verification report on their sureties.

The release followed a hearing at the Delhi High Court earlier on Wednesday, where Mr Das and Mr Ranka withdrew their challenge to the extension of their custody after the bench pointed out that they had an alternative legal remedy available.

Justice Subramonium Prasad questioned the activists’ decision to approach the High Court, noting that they had signed a peace bond on 11 October but allegedly breached it later.

He also asked whether the authorities were justified in demanding stricter assurances after the pair allegedly crossed barricades and entered the protest site.

“The two petitioners are out there at the forefront. Now when you go there (Jantar Mantar) and break a barricade – the barricade is meant for a particular purpose – chances of 10-20 more people violating are very bright… There can be persons who might not be in your control and who do things… We have seen it outside the country… You could start with something which is peaceful but then you cannot control… police permission is just not to stop you, it is also to prevent unwanted elements from joining your group and spoiling the name.”

The judge also questioned the evolution of the movement’s demands, asking about the ages of the two activists and observing that the initial protests had involved students and young people.

open image in gallery ( Reuters )

“So you are not Gen Z?” he asked after their lawyer, Abhik Chimni, told the court that Das was 27 and Ranka 31.

“Why I am asking (about their ages) is… the first protest (in July, triggered by the paper leak of undergraduate medical exam) was a student protest, children were there… Now cause is changing, people are remaining the same… Suddenly they are talking about ‘regime change’, about ‘ballot’… What is your purpose, what do you do in your life otherwise… We will have to go into all these questions then,” Justice Prasad said.

The High Court did not rule on the merits of their challenge to the custody order. It said they could pursue the appropriate appellate remedy if they remained aggrieved by the magistrate’s decision.

The CJP emerged in May after a social media post by its founder Abhijeet Dipke turned an online joke into a youth-led protest movement.

The name was inspired by remarks from chief justice of India Surya Kant comparing unemployed young people to cockroaches, which sparked outrage among sections of the youth.

The group gained prominence during protests over alleged examination irregularities and paper leaks, with demonstrations in July demanding education reforms.

Its campaign subsequently shifted towards India’s electoral system, with the group demanding Kumar’s resignation over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

The exercise, intended by the Election Commission to remove dead, duplicate and ineligible voters, has drawn criticism from opposition parties and activists who allege that eligible voters risk being excluded. The commission and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) have rejected allegations that the revision is intended to benefit the governing party.

The dispute over Jantar Mantar has added another dimension to the confrontation.

The site, long associated with demonstrations by political parties, trade unions, and civil society groups, was denotified as an authorised protest venue on 11 October. The decision has been challenged separately in the Supreme Court and the Delhi High Court.

The CJP had sought to demonstrate there despite the restrictions, prompting a police response and the detention of its activists. Mr Das and Mr Ranka's custody was extended on 19 October after the magistrate rejected their sureties, citing concerns about their suitability and discrepancies in identity documents.

The magistrate had also expressed doubts about the pair's willingness to comply with the law, citing what the order described as repeated calls for protests at a de-notified site.

Mr Dipke had a message for his fellow activists after two of the movement’s leaders walked free following seven days in custody: “Saurav and Ashu are not just better but much, much bigger leaders than me. Happy to follow your orders, my leaders. Jaan hazir hai. Lekin iske baad mere bina garden mein koi akela nahi ghumega!!! (After this, don’t walk in the garden without me).”

Welcoming the release, CJP legal head Ratna Singh said the decision should have come earlier.

“We welcome the decision. I think this decision should have been taken long ago, but it is not too late,” Ms Singh said.

News.title: Second storm to hit UK this weekend as Storm Boelo forecast to bring wind and rain after Austen
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The Met Office has declared a second named storm in a matter of days, with fresh weather warnings issued for this weekend.

Storm Boelo is due to hit the UK on Saturday, bringing strong winds and heavy rain to large parts of the country, the forecaster said.

The storm will impact Northern Ireland, Scotland and parts of northern England over the weekend, the Met Office said.

It comes as an amber wind warning has been issued for parts of southwest England, where heavy rain and severe gusts of up to 80mph are forecast.

Met Office Deputy Chief Forecaster Chris Bulmer, said: “Storm Boelo will bring strong winds and heavy rain to Northern Ireland, Scotland and parts of northern England over the weekend, impacting the opposite end of the country to Storm Austen.

“Gusts of 70-80mph in exposed coastal areas and high ground are possible, with 50-60mph gusts more widely. The strong winds will be accompanied by heavy rain, making for an impactful weekend of weather.

“Severe weather warnings and forecast detail will continue to develop, so people should keep up to date with the forecast over the next few days.”

More follows...

News.title: What happens when you get malaria during pregnancy?
News.content:
Huge strides have been made in recent years in combating malaria but one group is more at risk than ever before: pregnant women.

They are uniquely vulnerable to the disease and because sub-Saharan Africa shoulders the burden of global cases the continent’s rapidly growing population means far more women are exposed today than at the turn of the millennium.

According to a recent study, 52 million pregnant women in Africa face the threat of malaria each year, up from 37 million in 2000.

And the toll is heavy: malaria in pregnancy kills at least 10,000 mothers and 210,000 infants every year.

Malaria in pregnancy is uniquely dangerous, and the disease acts very differently to how it does in someone who is not pregnant.

“Pregnant women are one of the most vulnerable groups to malaria, it can lead to severe anaemia, immune suppression, and in the worst cases, mortality,” Lottie Renwick, global campaign director at Malaria No More UK told The Telegraph.

Malaria parasites infect and feed on red blood cells, dividing and multiplying in the bloodstream. This makes them easily detectable through a simple blood test, which allows life-saving treatment to be administered quickly.

But in pregnancy, the parasites are notoriously evasive.

Instead of floating in the bloodstream, they colonise in the placenta – the organ that feeds and sustains the baby.

News.title: Harry Kane proves there is only one Ballon d’Or winner
News.content:
After Arsenal were beaten by Bayern Munich in a Champions League quarter-final two years ago, Mikel Arteta bemoaned a lack of “magic moments” in attack.

Arsenal have since progressed to a Champions League semi-final and final, while ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

The upward trajectory has translated to tangible success, but Arsenal are still searching the level-raising attacker they lacked on their last visit to the Allianz Arena in 2024.

Back then, Arsenal’s offensive game revolved around Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard and that remains the case, which makes one wonder if Arsenal’s forward options have been adequately renewed.

A pair of stodgy performances (in victory) against Leeds United and Nottingham Forest have amplified those questions, though some of Arsenal’s slicker football in the season’s early weeks has been forgotten a little hastily.

They have made another strong start to another European campaign with six points from six, but this is undoubtedly their hardest fixture of the league phase.

Their chances of matching last season’s eight wins from eight could well hinge on the outcome of tonight’s game, but there are worse times to face Bayern.

Vincent Kompany’s team looks as formidable as ever, having scored 22 goals from six Bundesliga games so far this season. Their rotational approach is hard to track, with runners from deep breaking beyond Harry Kane who wanders into deep midfield positions.

However, they are without Michael Olise (suspension) and Jamal Musiala (injury) while Joshua Kimmich will miss the game on compassionate grounds following the death of his father.

With the exception of William Saliba, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincacpie, Arsenal have a pretty clean bill of health and the strength of their bench was crucial against Leeds, Lille and Forest last week.

For Arteta, there are some interesting selection calls to make. It is anticipated that Jurrien Timber will replace Ben White at right-back, and first-choice left-back Riccardo Calafiori has been rested for the Champions League games so far. Should Arteta continue that policy, Myles Lewis-Skelly will fill the position, which will likely mean a midfield start for Bruno Guimarães or Mikel Merino.

Arsenal’s manager must also decide between Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze on the left, and Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front. Havertz is Arteta’s preference, but he also has to consider a relatively short turnaround before Saturday’s league game against Everton.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Aston Villa 2.0 are making mockery of the early-season doom merchants
News.content:
In this comfortable victory over Viking, Villa became the second fastest team to win 20 matches at this level from 30 matches, only behind Real Madrid (who won 20 of their first 29). They have also won 12 home games in Europe in a row.

Much tougher assignments are to come, with powerhouses Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Borussia Dortmund still to come in the league phase.

Yet Villa are currently level on points with Paris St-Germain, Liverpool and Real Madrid, and Emery remains determined to make an impact in this competition.

He said: “We are delighted with how we are responding and improving things. The Champions League is very difficult, but we have nine points and you can feel confidence. We are comfortable for the next challenge.”

What a difference a few months make. Over the course of the summer, many observers wondered if the Emery fairy tale was in danger of ending.

With six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final victory moving on, it could have been a difficult period of transition. We have all learnt, however, that Emery can never be written off or doubted.

Just a week after their biggest European win, the 6-0 destruction of Fenerbahce, expectations were understandably high. Before kick-off a huge tifo was unfurled in the Holte End with the words: “We’ve conquered before. We’re prepared for more.”

News.title: Carrick apology to United fans ominously similar to Solskjaer’s final match
News.content:
There have been some dark days in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era but this was up there with the very worst of them: the kind of performance that gets a manager sacked, the kind of display that points to a fundamental disconnect, the kind of occasion that leaves you thinking Manchester United are as far away as they have ever been.

When players seem so averse to doing the very basics, such as running, and the club habitually have such trouble attracting the right profiles and personalities, it is hard to escape the feeling that saying goodbye to another manager is going to do little more than paper over the many cracks at Old Trafford.

But, watching this, you had to think Michael Carrick will do well to limp on as far as Sunday, when United face Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

And that was before we had heard the United captain, Bruno Fernandes, appearing to call out the manager’s tactics just a week on from the last show of public dissent from a player, when Lisandro Martínez attacked the Old Trafford board. If only these players were as good at talking on the pitch.

At the final whistle, Carrick walked over to the 700-strong group of United supporters, held up both hands in apology on no fewer than seven occasions and then walked off down the tunnel without looking in the direction of any of his players.

There were shades of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer at Watford in November 2021, when he also held up his hands in apology before being sacked 24 hours later.

News.title: Ebola case confirmed in Nigeria as outbreak spreads through Africa
News.content:
African ministers have been called to an urgent health summit after Nigeria confirmed its first case in the outbreak of the deadly Ebola fever tearing through eastern Congo.

Confirmation of a case in Africa’s most populous nation came days after a cluster was detected in Kenya and has heightened questions about border screening checks designed to stop the virus spreading from its epicentre in Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

With cases now found in West Africa, Central Africa and East Africa, the epidemic “has already become the most geographically widespread Ebola outbreak in history,” said Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of the continent’s main public health body.

DRC has recorded close to 10,000 cases since an outbreak began in mid-May, with around half of them dying of the haemorrhagic fever.

The Nigeria case meant “Ebola is now affecting three regions of Africa,” warned Dr Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention.

“The situation demands urgent action and political leadership at the highest level,” he said, convening an online summit for next week.

News.title: One billion children at risk from heatwaves, WHO warns
News.content:
More than one billion children are exposed to increasingly severe heat waves, the World Health Organization (WHO) has warned.

1.5 billion children under one experienced a fivefold increase in the number of heat wave days in 2024 compared with the 1986 to 2005 baseline period, jumping from roughly four days per year to a high of over 20, says the health agency. And these periods of high temperature are becoming longer, more frequent and more severe, the WHO warns.

According to the Met Office, this summer was the hottest on record in the UK, with five widespread heatwaves and 40 days where the temperature was above 30 degrees celsius. Europe also saw record-breaking temperatures, and Asia and Africa both experienced their warmest July on record, according to the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).

Four UN agencies, including the WHO, the WMO, Unicef and the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), have urged countries to monitor how extreme heat affects pregnant women, newborns and children.

The new framework tracks preterm birth, stillbirths, low birthweight, pregnancy hypertension, child deaths and health facility visits.

“Heat is already affecting our most vulnerable populations, including pregnant women, newborns and children. But what health systems do not count, they cannot respond to,” said Dr Pascale Allotey, director of WHO’s department of maternal and child health.

“By tracking outcomes such as preterm birth, child deaths and illnesses, and health-facility visits alongside heat exposure, countries can identify potential impacts and take action to protect women and children,” she said.

High temperatures are particularly dangerous for pregnant women because the body has to work much harder to cool both the mother and the baby.

Intense heat can cause surface-level blood vessels to dilate, which in pregnant women can restrict blood flow to the placenta and reduce the amount of oxygen and nutrients that reach the foetus. Heat can also put strain on the cardiovascular system, increasing the risk of gestational diabetes, dangerously high blood pressure, and pre-eclampsia.

The odds of a preterm birth also increase by 26 per cent during heatwaves: for every one degree rise in heat exposure, the likelihood of giving birth early rise by roughly 4 per cent, according to a systematic review published in Nature Medicine.

The WHO has also urged countries to develop and implement tailored heat-health action plans that account for the needs of pregnant women, newborns and children, as well as strengthening early-warning systems to ensure timely action to heat risks, such as alert systems and personalised public messaging.

“As our world continues to heat up, it creates new risks for health, and older people, pregnant women, newborns and children are among those least able to escape them,” said Bruce Gordon, director of environment and climate change at the WHO.

“Our health systems need the data to recognise this reality and take action – from protecting people during heatwaves to embedding climate risk consideration into everyday health services,” he said.

News.title: Rio Ngumoha dazzles on coming-of-age night in Europe
News.content:
Iraola made major changes at half-time, substituting Araújo and playing without a conventional right-back for the second half. It was brave and changed the momentum of the game, pushing his team higher up the pitch in what looked like a man-to-man marking arrangement. It enabled Iraola’s players to deny Villarreal the space and possession they had enjoyed in the first half when they had taken a two-goal lead – chiefly because of the mistakes of the home team. However much that was destabilising for Liverpool, by half-time they were level.

“They are so good on the ball,” Iraola said of Villarreal afterwards. Indeed, Villarreal’s manager Iñigo Pérez, a former Athletic team-mate of the Liverpool manager, was a coach whom Iraola sought to appoint at Bournemouth. “People probably don’t rate them [Villarreal],” Iraola said, “but after Barça they are probably the best in La Liga. They have 61 per cent of possession. Probably they have not had the results they deserve. If you are not really aggressive, you are not going to get the ball.

“We didn’t take as much risk. We were struggling because it is not a team that you can just press a bit. Either you go all the way or you will struggle without the ball.” Once Liverpool had done so, he said, his team had “won a lot of duels”. He was right in that respect. With the space squeezed, it was the power of Liverpool’s midfield that was telling.

Virgil van Dijk gave the first goal to Villarreal’s small No 9 Georges Mikautadze who had looked up to that point like he was hopelessly mismatched against the Liverpool captain and Jérémy Jacquet. Van Dijk’s misjudged header back to Alisson let in the striker, who did well to gather the ball and then hit it early. The second Villarreal goal at the midpoint of the first half was a mistake from Kostas Tsimikas, who failed to step up and played both Mikautadze and Cardona onside from Nathan Saliba’s ball. Either might have tucked it in but it was the left-back Cardona who took it on.

News.title: Inflation jumps in run-up to Healey’s maiden Budget
News.content:
Inflation has jumped to its highest level in almost a year, underlining the challenges facing John Healey, the Chancellor, ahead of his first Budget next week.

The consumer prices index climbed from 3.1pc in August to 3.5pc in September, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS).

Inflation was ahead of the 3.4pc predicted by economists and is now at its highest level since October 2025.

The sharp rise was driven by soaring fuel costs as a result of the Iran war. The ONS said average petrol prices rose by 8.2p a litre in September and diesel by 10.7p. Both reached levels not seen since 2022, in the wake of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

Suren Thiru, chief economist at the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales, said: “Rising inflation is turning the Budget into a perilous high-wire act for the Chancellor, increasing pressure for cost-of-living support while pushing up government borrowing costs, which is shrinking fiscal headroom and narrowing his policy options.”

Britain spent more money on debt interest last month than in any September on record, official figures show.

The UK’s debt servicing costs rose to £10.9bn in September, the highest total for the month since at least 1997, according to the ONS.

This burden helped to push national debt above £3 trillion for the first time.

Andrew Griffith, the shadow chancellor, said the unhappy milestone and the rise in inflation “show Labour has lost control of the economy”.

Public sector net debt has soared by 50pc since it first exceeded £2tn in June 2020.

Mr Healey insisted the British economy still had “momentum” and pointed to Wednesday morning’s approval of new drilling for gas in the North Sea as evidence of this.

He said: “We know that price rises from conflicts in the Middle East and Europe are hitting Britain and countries worldwide. Last week, the IMF said our UK fiscal discipline stands out with the lowest forecast deficit in the G7 by 2029.

“And today we’ve given the green light to getting North Sea gas from the Jackdaw field, investing the revenues in our clean energy future and supporting British workers.

“In my Budget next week, I will keep up this momentum. Maintaining our fiscal discipline and drive for growth in every postcode, while giving businesses and families some breathing space.”

September’s inflation figure is used for the annual uprating of welfare payments, with the state pension now in line to rise by almost £500 next year.

The figure is also used to calculate increases in business rates in England, with pubs, shops, offices and other hospitality businesses now facing a £1.1bn increase in the collective bill from April, according to tax firm Ryan.

Sports.title: ‘Could never be recreated’ – Lionel Messi’s World Cup trophy he paraded on pitch going up for sale with ‘endless’ value
Sports.content:
Next

WHEN Lionel Messi shared the picture of himself lifting the World Cup trophy for Argentina, it was quite literally internet breaking.

The picture became – and to this day still is – the most-liked Instagram post of all time with 74.4 million likes on the platform, while it was also the pinnacle of the career of arguably football‘s greatest ever player.



But no one at the time stopped to consider that Messi was actually parading around a replica trophy, rather than the genuine Jules Rimet.

And fast forward four years, a poignant moment considering the little magician’s recent retirement from international football, the replica trophy Messi and Co held that day is going up for auction.



The trophy itself was down on the pitch of the Lusail Stadium in Qatar after Argentina‘s penalty shootout victory over France for 45 minutes of the jubilant celebrations.

It was later signed by eight members of the World Cup winning team, including Lautaro Martínez, Leandro Paredes, Guido Rodríguez, Ángel Di María, and Gonzalo Montiel – the man who scored the winning goal in the final.



Following the final it was put on display at the National Historical Museum of Buenos Aires, but will now headline the inaugural sports memorabilia auction by Richmond Auctions.

The trophy is going up on Saturday, November 7, alongside a Mint 9 Panini Trading Card with the picture on and a series of more than 350 other lots featuring classic and iconic trading cards.

But the magnum opus of the auction is the replica trophy, which the Founder of Richmond Auctions, Jordan Richmond, reckons could go for a record-breaking fee.

Speaking exclusively to SunSport, Richmond said: “I’ve never been a big advocate of putting a ceiling or a floor on a collectible item.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“I can just say that it’s a collectible that really is based in three different kind of bullet points: one would be the story, the provenance, and then the rarity of opportunity.

“The story is incredible, and in any collectible market, the story is what drives value. And so, you know, we’ve got all kinds of documentation. There’s notarized letters, there’s photos, there’s videos.

“The provenance is locked tight, which is important with something like this.

“And then the rarity of the opportunity, right? This replica trophy, the story could never be recreated.

“Messi is retired. Just the possibility this would end up on the pitch, celebrated with, and there are hundreds of photos of it if you just Google replica trophy and 2022.



“So, those three things, I think really the opportunities are endless as far as the value is concerned.”

He continued: “It’s such a unique item. There are comps for game-worn jerseys or other clothing articles.

“There’s really nothing that has a story like this. A replica trophy that made it to the championship in Qatar.

“Never was meant to be on the field, ended up on the field, was carried by all the players, Messi himself. So it’s really hard to say.



“In my opinion, it’s one of the coolest, most unique stories of a collectible that I have ever seen, and we’re really honoured to bring it to market.”

Talking about the story of how the replica even made it on to the pitch, Richmond explained: “The consignor of the item brought it all the way from Argentina to Qatar in 2022, really was meant just to be a photo prop for him and his family and friends.

“They got it into the stadium. There’s a ton of photos of them and their family taking photos and selfies with the pitch behind them.

“After the game-winning goal, one of the players saw the replica trophy up in the stands and thought it would be neat to have on the pitch with the rest of the players.

“He goes up and asks if he can borrow it, and the consignor let him borrow the trophy. Ended up on the pitch for 45 minutes or so, and was held by a ton of different players, Messi himself.

“Most of the on-field celebration photos you see with Messi and other players are with this replica trophy.

“There’s even a trading card that we just found in the last few weeks of the exact moment with this trophy, and it will be sold with it as well. It’s a cool piece to commemorate the moment.

“Signed by eight players and then returned back to the customer. It’s really pretty remarkable how it happened, and we’re really excited to bring it to market.”

It is estimated the sports memorabilia industry could reach £202billion in value by 2034, and assets such as this will only serve to accelerate its growth.



Previously, much of the market has been dominated by US stars and trading cards such as Michael Jordan, Kobe Bryant, Tom Brady, Shohei Ohtani, but football – the world’s most watched sport – is catching up.

Richmond continued: “I think with any collectible, it’s the people that are collecting it, and my generation, your generation and younger, it’s what we grew up doing, right?

“I was a huge sports card collector, the Michael Jordan era, that’s what we did growing up.

“And so as our generation, the younger generation starts to come into their own money, you tend to resonate back to what you collected as a kid or what you were a part of, and that’s why we’re seeing such a huge influx in not just the value of this stuff, but also the people collecting it.



“So yeah, I think it’s got a long runway. The sports collecting and sports memorabilia market, I think is going to be around for a very long time.”

As well as the replica trophy, Richmond highlights a Jordan NBA rookie card and a Babe Ruth baseball card.

He even reveals one of the other lots in the auction, of which there are over 350, already has interest to the tune of £105,000 ($140,000) despite being three weeks away from the final sale day.

Asked whether Messi’s replica trophy could eclipse Jordan – putting one sport’s GOAT against another – Richmond said: “I think for football collectors, Messi is number one.

Real Madrid discovered ahead of time that Vinicius Junior had lost out to Rodri and boycotted the event.



Kane is in the dark, however, as to whether he has scooped the award to become the first English winner since Michael Owen in 2001.

He said: “I think my wife would prefer to know and my family, it’s very stressful for everyone.



“I can see why they don’t tell people. They want everyone to go, all the big names there and there will be more people watching it if they don’t know, so I can understand why.

“From my point of view, of course I’d love to know to just kind of see and not have to wait throughout the whole night.

“But it is their decision, I can’t control that. We’ll have to just enjoy it and try not to stress out too much.”

Kane did not appear to let the uncertainty impact him on Wednesday night.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The striker scored a penalty and assisted Bayern Munich’s opening goal as they drew 2-2 with Arsenal in the Champions League.

The Three Lions skipper has already scored 10 goals for the German champions this season in 11 games.

It carries on Kane’s fine performances from last season, when he scored an incredible 73 goals for club and country.

That form has made the 33-year-old the favourite to win the Ballon d’Or, but he faces strong competition.

Lamine Yamal and his Spain team-mate Rodri are rivals for the award, as are Kylian Mbappe and Lionel Messi.



Kane said: “I try not to think about it. Obviously it is hard not to.

“There are always rumours and stuff flying around so you try to stay away from it.

“We have important games to play and I know we have another important one on Sunday before the event on Monday so that’s where my focus is.

“Of course I am going to try and enjoy Monday night as much as possible. It is a big occasion, a big event so we will have to wait and see.”

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Second investigation confirmed as Pep Guardiola questioned on legacy
Sports.content:
As the saga around Manchester City's 115 charges continues to rumble on, Mirror Football will be here with all of the latest updates and news

Welcome to Mirror Sport's live blog about Manchester City's 114 guilty charges.

The football world is still reeling from last month's announcement which confirmed the Cityzens had been found guilty on all charges relating to breaches of its financial regulations between 2009/10 and 2017/18.

It was deemed that the club artificially inflated revenue by more than £900million through the use of supposed 'sham' sponsorship deals. City continue to insist they are innocent and launched an appeal against the verdict on October 1.

They also maintain there is a "a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence" that exonerates them, but this is yet to be communicated to the public. In and amongst the saga, the legitimacy of their achievements over the last 20 years have been brought into question.

One of Pep Guardiola's former players has recently questioned his legacy at the club, given the fact many of his achievements took place in between 2009/10 and 2017-18.

All of this will be covered and more in today's Mirror Live blog!

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp admits he still hasn't come to terms with Diogo Jota's tragic death
Sports.content:
Jurgen Klopp admits he still hasn't come to terms with Diogo Jota's tragic death

In a new biography of Diogo Jota, the tragic former Liverpool star, his ex-boss Jurgen Klopp reveals he still has not come to terms with the player's death, aged just 28

View 2 Images Klopp has spoken about the tragic death of Jota (Image: Getty Images)

Jurgen Klopp has spoken about the death of former Liverpool star Diogo Jota for a new biography into the tragic footballer's life.

‌



‌



Jota died aged just 28 along with his brother Andre Silva in a car crash in the summer of 2025 just weeks after becoming a Premier League champion for the Reds udner Klopp.

‌



Klopp has now recalled how he knew he had to sign Jota after watching him in action for Wolves, and how he has struggled to come to terms with the death of one of the most popular members of his Liverpool squad.

‌



"I was watching a Wolves match," recalls Klopp in Diogo Jota: Forever In Our Hearts from Reach Sport, which is available now. "When Diogo drifted to the left, using his physicality, showing refined technique and tremendous power. I immediately thought: ‘I want this player’.

"It was a gut feeling, the sort that you can usually rely on.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"Over the years, I’ve learnt that if you see certain things in a footballer – certain actions – they can tell you a great deal about the person. And there have only been very rare cases where I’ve been disappointed or come to realise, later on, that they were actually completely different.

‌



"Normally when I sign a player, the process is different. I work closely with the scouts and sporting directors, I tell them which position I need to strengthen, and they come back to me with some options. In Diogo’s case, it was me who took the initiative. I asked them to put together some material about him. I told them I wanted to take a closer look at him, and that I was excited about his attributes.

"We needed versatile players, and Diogo could play in several positions. And he had the right attitude and mentality for a club like Liverpool."

‌



View 2 Images Jota was one of the most popular members of Liverpool's squad (Image: PA)

Klopp says he is still coming to terms with the death of Jota at 28, and finds it difficult to speak about the loss of the husband and father of three.

‌



“I’m 58 years old. I know that people die, that this is part of life," he said. "Once you reach a certain age, we have to accept that these things happen. But when I heard about Diogo’s accident, I was in shock and I couldn’t even speak. I didn’t ask how, I didn’t ask where; I just stopped what I was doing and tried to come to terms with it. To this day, I must admit, I still haven’t really managed to do that.

“When my assistant Danielle asked me if I was available to have this conversation – to contribute to this book – I said yes, that I wanted to talk about Diogo, to think about him. However, now that we’re talking, I can see that I’m not ready for it.

‌



"I’ve spent most of my life talking, but now I’m just hanging by a thread, lost for words – which is not at all normal. It’s crazy…”

Diogo Jota: Forever In Our Hearts (Reach Sport, £22) is on sale now.

Sports.title: Cesc Fabregas admits he told Como stars to 'slow down' after going 4-0 up against Man Utd
Sports.content:
Cesc Fabregas admits he told Como stars to 'slow down' after going 4-0 up against Man Utd

Italian side Como ran riot against Manchester United but it could have been worse for the Red Devils after boss Cesc Fabregas made a post-match admission

View 2 Images Fabregas admits he told his stars to slow down against Man Utd (Image: Xinhua/Shutterstock)

Cesc Fabregas admits he told his Como side to 'slow down' after they romped into a 4-0 lead against Manchester United in the Champions League.

‌



‌



The former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder is manager of the Italian club and they enjoyed one of the most famous nights in their history as they swatted aside the Red Devils on Wednesday night.

‌



Joshua Zirkzee scored a late consolation for United but it is a result that leaves Michael Carrick's job hanging by a thread. United have won just two of 11 games in all competitions so far this season.

‌



And it could have been even worse for Carrick's side after Fabregas admitted he told his players to take the foot off the gas after going 4-0 up in order to preserve their energy levels for their games ahead.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"I regret the last ten minutes because I was the one who told the team to slow down the tempo because there's another match and at 4-0 we could manage things a little," said the Spaniard.

“I told the players to stop running and stay in the middle and that is something I regret because I'm the first to always push them to fight until the end.

‌



“Their goal hurt me because we dropped our intensity and dropped our defensive block, but it was my fault.”

Carrick is now facing a battle to remain as United manager despite only penning a two-year deal in the summer after an impressive spell as caretaker boss.

‌



View 2 Images Carrick gave a damning assessment of his players in his post-match press conference (Image: UEFA via Getty Images)

He took aim at his players in his post-match press conference, saying: "We might win, we might lose, but the way we went about it tonight, I wouldn't say everyone, but the way we went about it in some ways tonight wasn't acceptable. And I just wanted to let the fans know that I feel for them, for sure.

‌



"It wasn't just the goals, if I'm totally honest. It was the manner and the way we played at times, in the way we went about it, that was the difficult thing to watch for me.

"It's not about playing for me, it's about playing for this football club. It's the responsibility that comes with being in the position; I'm responsible for the football club and the supporters.

‌



"I'm giving my best, absolute best all the time, I care about it. My whole life's wrapped around it. I genuinely give everything that I possibly can."

Sports.title: Kyle Walker admits Man City's 114 charges 'don't look great' and fears he'll lose his medals
Sports.content:
Kyle Walker admits Man City's 114 charges 'don't look great' and fears he'll lose his medals

The former Manchester City defender spent eight seasons at the Etihad Stadium between 2017 and 2025, winning 15 major trophies including six Premier League titles

View Image Kyle Walker has spoken about Man City's charges

Kyle Walker has insisted he and his former Manchester City teammates simply focused on giving their all on the pitch while the club's financial charges case unfolded. The current Premier League leaders have appealed after an independent panel found them guilty of 114 breaches of the league’s financial rules.

‌



‌



The case included accusations that City artificially inflated their income through ‘sham’ sponsorship deals. The club have consistently denied any wrongdoing. Potential punishments include a substantial fine and a points deduction severe enough to send City into the Championship.

‌



The Mail has reported that a further deduction could follow, potentially leaving them facing a second season in the second tier. While the EFL would not be obliged to enforce that punishment, reports suggest it would do so.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Man City win in front 20,000 empty seats at the Etihad as Enzo Maresca speaks out READ MORE :

Other potential sanctions include a transfer embargo and stripping City of the titles they won during the period covered by the financial charges.

Walker spent eight seasons at the Etihad, winning 17 major trophies, including six Premier League titles. The uncertainty over City's honours also puts an awkward spotlight on the Burnley defender's tattoo.

‌



He has the words 'four in a row' inked on his leg to mark the club's four consecutive Premier League titles.

"[I've got] 'four in a row' tattooed," he confirmed on talkSPORT.

‌



Presenter Andy Goldstein then probed: "If they take the medals away have you got a tattoo removal firm ready to take that one?"

Walker then replied: Well I'm probably going to have to do that bit! I'll try and keep it on, but hopefully we don't get things taken away."

‌



Asked about the charges, Walked added: "It's the big elephant in the room we're probably all going to be asked when doing interviews or whatever. It doesn't look great.

"Let's not hide from the fact they've been found guilty but they're going through an appeal. As a player all I can say is all we did is go out and play our best as a team and I'll defend the players for the rest of my life, because I feel what we did and achieved in that time was incredible and probably won't be done ever again.

‌



"But from the outside looking in, it doesn't look great and we have to address that."

That said, it is unlikely that any punishment will be handed down to City until the appeals process has been navigated.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher calls Bruno Fernandes a DISGRACE for 'throwing Michael Carrick under the bus'
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher calls Bruno Fernandes a DISGRACE for 'throwing Michael Carrick under the bus'

Jamie Carragher has launched a scathing attack on Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes, branding the Portuguese a 'disgrace' for his post-match comments following the club's 4-1 defeat to Como

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher criticised Bruno Fernandes after his post-match remarks

Jamie Carragher has unleashed scathing criticism of Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes - labelling the Portuguese midfielder a 'disgrace.' The former Liverpool defender defended embattled head coach Michael Carrick and commended the 45-year-old for responding to the skipper following their 4-1 hammering at the hands of Como.

‌



‌



Carragher suggested that Fernandes' explosive remarks came after he was left 'embarrassed' by his 66th-minute substitution during their humiliation in Northern Italy. Nico Paz shone brightest as his double inspired Cesc Fabregas' side to a memorable victory and intensified the scrutiny on the Premier League-winning midfielder.

‌



The United skipper joined Lisandro Martinez in delivering a shock statement during post-match media appearances. Fernandes directed criticism towards Carrick, pinning responsibility for the loss on Ruben Amorim's successor.

‌



Man Utd news: Lewis Hall transfer twist as Antonio Conte conditions emerge READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

In an impassioned outburst, the footballer-turned-pundit speaking on CBS Sports accused Fernandes of 'killing' his teammates and being the reason for United's inability to press collectively. He said: "No (not a good look). We said Lisandro Martinez was bang out of order last week for calling out the hierarchy and for Bruno Fernandes to do that is a disgrace really.

"When you think about last season he got Player of the Season, that was off the back of Michael Carrick becoming manager, he wouldn't have got that without Michael Carrick because he got put back in his rightful position and went on to have a fantastic season because he's a talented footballer."

‌



"But in terms of attitude, the way he goes about things, is not right at all. He's reacted like that because he's been brought off and he's been embarrassed by the manager because he's been brought off. When he talks about pressing, man-to-man or zonal, for years, Bruno Fernandes has meant Manchester United can't press.

"Because he does things for the crowd, I commentate on games and he runs all over and plays like a kid in the schoolyard, he plays for the supporters, it looks like he's working hard, he's not, he's killing the team doing it. He's not playing in a successful era for Manchester United.

‌



Carragher continued: "Years ago, there was a captain called Bryan Robson, one of the greatest players to ever play for Man United because he played for the club, he didn't throw the manager or the players under the bus.

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes questioned Man United's coaching staff's decision

‌



"He kept fighting for Manchester United and watching him throw his arms up every week in a game is an absolute disgrace, calling the manager out considering how he's performed this season on the pitch.

"Awful attitude and not what a Manchester United captain should do."

‌



Carragher acknowledged that a change in the dugout is required at Old Trafford following the loss, which extended their winless run to seven matches. During his post-match media briefing, Carrick hit back at Fernandes by suggesting that 'if you don't run forward and back, you aren't going to win.'

The response earned praise for Carrick, with Carragher emerging as an unexpected supporter as he confessed to feeling sympathy for the manager.

‌



"Isn't it funny, how many managers has Bruno Fernandes had? So every single manager doesn't have a philosophy? How many managers are we on now? Five?" said the former Liverpool man.

‌



"It's an easy thing to say, Fabregas is the best new thing in managerial teams but Man United is rotten from top to bottom. Not just the manager, the whole club, who has got the answers?

"We comment on it all the time. Are we ever right really? No one else seems to. There's no doubt the manager needs to be changed now, this can't go on for a club of this stature but I'm glad Michael Carrick come out and said that about Michael Carrick. They don't run.

‌



"What he did last season, no one proclaims Michael Carrick is one of the greatest managers in Europe but what he did was come in and helped his own football club, he was out of work, come in and done amazing, the only reason they're in the Champions League is because of Carrick.

"He got them in there, the reason they got another £100m to £150m, no one thought they'd be there. I feel sorry for him a little bit. It's not working out and it needs to be changed.

"I'm delighted he brought him off and a pop back because that what they need some of them players."

Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Lewis Hall transfer twist as Antonio Conte conditions emerge

Manchester United are in crisis again with Michael Carrick in the firing line and Antonio Conte waiting in the wings

View 3 Images Antonio Conte is a contender for the Manchester United job (Image: Getty Images)

Michael Carrick is clinging to his job following Manchester United's shambolic defeat to Como in the Champions League. The 4-1 loss to Cesc Fabregas's side made it seven games without a win in all competitions.

‌



‌



Carrick now appears to be facing the same fate as every other manager since Sir Alex Ferguson. The 45-year-old walked over to apologise to the travelling support following a chastening defeat that saw skipper Bruno Fernandes publicly question the manager's approach.

‌



Carrick hit back by suggesting the players didn't work hard enough. The obvious discontent in the camp, coupled with an alarming display, raises serious questions about Carrick's future ahead of Sunday's Premier League home game against Bournemouth.

‌



Away from the Como debacle, here's a round-up of other United news lines...

Man Utd in-fighting erupts as Matheus Cunha and Michael Carrick row off camera READ MORE :

United back in for Hall

United are reportedly ready to revive their interest in Newcastle's Lewis Hall. There was disappointment in the summer when the club failed to land a replacement - or at least an alternative - to Luke Shaw.

United wanted Hall but Newcastle were unwilling to sell and then tied the full-back to a new long-term contract, which appeared to make him unattainable. However, according to The i Paper, United will make a fresh bid to sign the 22-year-old, who, it is claimed, is open to moving to Old Trafford.

‌



The same report says United are interested in another left-back, Adrien Truffert, who is expected to leave Bournemouth next summer amid significant interest in the French defender.

View 3 Images Lewis Hall is a long-term target of Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Conte conditions

Antonio Conte, a contender to replace Carrick if United decide to make a change, has reportedly set out his conditions amid interest from Juventus. The Italians are the other club being linked with Conte, who is a free agent after leaving Napoli in the summer.

‌



However, according to TMW Radio in Italy, Conte wants specific guarantees 'for the next few seasons' from Juve before returning to the Turin giants, whom he managed between 2011 and 2014. The report adds that if those assurances, which it hints are about rebuilding the squad, aren't met then he is likely to opt for United instead.

Conte recently gave an interview in which he said he can see his next job being with a fallen giant, with United and Juve both falling into that category. He told The Athletic: "There are many clubs that have somewhat lost sight of their history.

‌



View 3 Images Antonio Conte is ready for his next big job (Image: Getty Images)

"I'd like to go to one of these clubs to dust off that history and make it shine once more. Clubs where there's pressure, where, ultimately, you know full well that you're not going there just to take part, but to compete."

‌



Juve are currently managed by Luciano Spalletti, who, like Carrick, is under mounting pressure following Sunday's 3-0 home defeat to Lazio, which left them eighth in Serie A.
