Sports.title: Arsenal news: David Raya makes exit admission as Mikel Arteta eyes new signing
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: David Raya makes exit admission as Mikel Arteta eyes new signing

Arsenal have been linked with a transfer target as David Raya discusses his future with the Gunners

View 2 Images Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya has made an admission about his plans for the future (Image: Maynard Manyowa/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Arsenal have made a strong start to the new season but will be aware that there is still room for improvement in the transfer window. Mikel Arteta is aiming to build on last season’s success by retaining the Premier League title and lifting the Champions League trophy for the first time in the club’s history.

‌



‌



The Gunners bolstered their ranks through the arrivals of Ezri Konsa, Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis in the summer. However, Arsenal’s unsuccessful pursuits of Real Madrid's Vinicius Junior and Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez show that Arteta was willing to strengthen his attacking options.

‌



Club Brugge striker Nicolo Tresoldi has reportedly emerged as a target for Arsenal ahead of the January transfer window. The 22-year-old has scored nine goals in 12 games for the Belgian side so far this term, including a Champions League hat-trick against Inter Milan.

‌



Elsewhere, the Gunners’ recent success has been built on their resolute backline, but goalkeeper David Raya has suggested he could exit Arsenal in the future. Here, Mirror Football looks at some of the biggest stories surrounding Arteta’s side.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources .

‌



David Raya makes exit admission

Spain international Raya has hinted that he may choose to leave Arsenal in the future, as he wishes to play in La Liga. The 31-year-old shot-stopper, who is under contract until 2028, has been integral to the team since initially arriving on loan from Brentford in 2023.

Raya has since established himself as one of the world’s best goalkeepers, winning three consecutive Premier League golden gloves, as well as helping the Gunners finally clinch the title last season. The former Blackburn Rovers star was also part of Spain’s World Cup-winning squad this summer and has admitted he would relish the opportunity to test himself in his home country, having spent his professional career in English football.

‌



When asked if he would like to play in Spain, Raya told Marca: “Yes, I would love to, I would love to try La Liga. For now, I'm very happy here, but I would like to try the Spanish league.

“I think it's a very competitive league. Maybe, in the future, I could play for a Spanish club. I'm Spanish and I would love to play there, that's for sure.”

‌



View 2 Images Arsenal have been linked with Club Brugge striker Nicolo Tresoldi (Image: Nicolò Campo/LightRocket via Getty Images)

Arsenal eye new signing

Arsenal are reportedly eyeing a move for Club Brugge star Tresoldi. The Germany U21 international has been a standout for the Belgian side, who sold Christos Tzolis to the Gunners in the summer.

‌



Arteta has relied on Kai Havertz to start up front in every league game so far, with Viktor Gyokeres struggling to impress when called upon. The Sun reports that the situation has led Arsenal to become interested in Tresoldi, with the club exploring a possible move in January.

Tresoldi’s value is claimed to have risen to around £42million following Brugge previously rejecting a £30m offer from Roma. However, Arsenal would face competition from AC Milan for the 22-year-old, who is a boyhood fan of the Italian giants.

Sports.title: Man Utd in-fighting erupts as Matheus Cunha and Michael Carrick row off camera
Sports.content:
Man Utd in-fighting erupts as Matheus Cunha and Michael Carrick row off camera

Michael Carrick is seemingly starting to lose the dressing room, with a number of key players clashing with the head coach during Wednesday's Champions League loss to Como

View 2 Images Matheus Cunha reportedly clashed with Michael Carrick (Image: Image Photo Agency, Getty Images)

Manchester United's Matheus Cunha was reportedly embroiled in a fiery exchange with Michael Carrick during Wednesday's Champions League loss to Como. The rift at the Red Devils appears to be widening, with Bruno Fernandes also questioning his head coach before the 45-year-old responded during his post-match press conference.

‌



‌



Como humbled the Premier League side as Cesc Fabregas delivered a statement performance in the Champions League. The visitors stormed to a 4-1 victory with Nico Paz bagging a memorable brace in the emphatic triumph.

‌



The setback adds to a torrid spell for Carrick, prolonging their search for a win to seven fixtures. The Sun's Samuel Luckhurst, meanwhile, claimed that Carrick had a 'relatively robust' confrontation with Cunha during an exchange that wasn't captured by television cameras.

‌



Michael Carrick's reaction says it all as Como hammering leaves job hanging by a thread READ MORE :

Some United supporters also expressed alarm over the "altercation" between the Brazilian and his boss. Cunha was withdrawn at the interval, with Amad introduced, as Carlos Baleba also came on at the beginning of the second half in an attempt to salvage the contest.

However, it proved futile as United were outclassed in every area. United's aspirations of a crucial victory were effectively dashed inside two minutes when Paz bent home a stunning opener, leaving United instantly deflated.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Carrick's team were made to pay for their slack defending as they allowed the former Real Madrid talent too much space. The visitors were also lucky not to trail by a greater margin at half-time.

But just four minutes after the restart, Anastasios Douvikas found the net in what became an eight-minute onslaught from Como, with Paz taking advantage of a United error. A week after Lisandro Martinez's explosive remarks, in which he criticised the shortage of reinforcements in the squad and the Old Trafford hierarchy, Fernandes decided to air his own grievances.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



In doing so, he called out Carrick over his tactical approach in a revealing confession. He said: "It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence.

"It's not the first time, we started on the wrong foot, and they scored very early. Not much pressure on the ball, not many good movements with the ball, not many things going our way.

‌



"Conceding early makes us go into game with a mood of defeat, it's difficult to get out of that, trying to be brave, to have the ball and make something happen. If we are not able to do that, it is going to be very difficult to get out of this situation."

The consequences from Wednesday's match will rumble on, just as they did following last week's 2-0 loss to Atletico Madrid after Martinez's comments. United have found themselves in the spotlight and under scrutiny for all the wrong reasons as their promising season begins to fall apart just two months in.

‌



View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes called out Michael Carrick's tactics (Image: PIERO CRUCIATTI, AFP via Getty Images)

Carrick responded to Fernandes and raised concerns about his squad's commitment, with the club edging towards turmoil both on and off the field. He said: "We might win, we might lose, but the way we went about it tonight, I wouldn't say everyone, but the way we went about it in some ways tonight wasn't acceptable.

‌



"And I just wanted to let the fans know that I feel for them, for sure. It wasn't just the goals, if I'm totally honest. It was the manner and the way we played at times, in the way we went about it, that was the difficult thing to watch for me.

"We actually half-pressed man-to-man the second half and then conceded a goal from that. And there's a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you ain't going to win."

Sports.title: Humphries withdraws from European Championship
Sports.content:
Luke Humphries has withdrawn from the 2026 European Championship after being diagnosed with gastroenteritis.

The world No 2 was set to make his sixth appearance in Dortmund, having finished as runner-up last year.

Under PDC rules, Humphries will be directly replaced in the field by Kim Huybrechts, the highest-ranked non-qualified player in the 2026 European Tour rankings.

Belgium's Huybrechts will now take on Ryan Searle on Thursday evening, with the winner set to face Danny Noppert or Stephen Bunting on Saturday.

World No 1 Luke Littler will face William O'Connor in his European Championship opener, while Gian van Veen will start his title defence against Andrew Gilding.

After first round contests on Thursday and Friday, Saturday's action will see eight round-two ties played across the afternoon and evening sessions, before the quarter-finals take place on Sunday afternoon ahead of the semi-finals and final on Sunday evening.

The action gets under way at Dortmund's Westfalenhallen on Thursday, with a top prize of £150,000 up for grabs on Sunday October 25.

2026 Machineseeker European Championship

Sports.title: Jarvis leads at Genesis Championship to pressure McIlroy in Race to Dubai
Sports.content:
Casey Jarvis made a strong start to his late bid for Race to Dubai glory by grabbing the early lead at the Genesis Championship, where Ryan Fox also impressed.

Fourth on the Race to Dubai ranking, Jarvis birdied the final hole at Woo Jeong Hills Country Club to regain the outright lead from nearest challenger Sanghun Shin on day one of the final event of the regular season.

Already a two-time winner this season, the 23-year-old is projected to overtake Rory McIlroy and Patrick Reed and enter the DP World Tour Play-Offs in second place behind leader Eugenio Chacarra.

"Felt really good out there," Jarvis said.

"Hit a lot of good-quality iron shots and made some good putts. Been working really hard on the greens and to see it finally paying off a bit is really nice. So yeah, super happy.

"I definitely think the putting has improved a lot. I went through a bit of a dip, so I worked hard with the putter and took some time in the middle of the season to start finding the stroke again. I started with a new putting coach and it seems to be working really well."

The South African made three birdies in a row at the third, fourth and fifth holes before another at the eighth took him to four under alongside early leaders Antoine Rozner and Mikael Lindberg.

A dropped shot at the ninth saw him turn in 33, but after two pars, a brilliant approach from the rough at the 12th helped him regain a share of the lead. He then moved clear with a 32-footer for birdie to reach five under.

Close behind on the other side of the course, Frederic Lacroix converted from two feet for birdie at the sixth, his 15th, to briefly join Jarvis at the top. The Frenchman then gave the shot straight back after missing the green at the par-three seventh before closing with two pars for an opening 67.

Sanghun Shin, who had been part of a four-way tie one shot back, was the next to join Jarvis as the Korean Tour (KPGA) Order of Merit leader birdied his final hole.

After Shin signed for a 66, Jarvis regained the outright lead by holing from seven feet for a closing birdie of his own.

It has been a breakout year for Jarvis, who recorded two top tens before claiming his maiden DP World Tour title in February with a birdie-eagle finish at the Magical Kenya Open presented by absa.

A week later, he won his second DP World Tour title on home soil at the Investec South African Open Championship, securing qualification for both the Masters Tournament and The Open Championship in 2026, where he finished tied sixth.

He almost made it three wins in a row with a tie for second at the Joburg Open, and although he has not maintained that momentum throughout the season, he recently returned to form by finishing tied second at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship.

Sports.title: Carra: Fernandes comments 'disgraceful', but Carrick's time may be up
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher has criticised Bruno Fernandes for questioning Man Utd's tactics following their 4-1 defeat to Como, but believes that it could be the end of the line for Michael Carrick.

Fernandes questioned the decision to not press Como man-to-man post-match, while Carrick responded in his press conference by saying "if you don't run back, you ain't going to win".

Fernandes' claims come just over a week after Lisandro Martinez called out the club's hierarchy following the 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid. Carragher was critical of the Argentine's comments, and shared a similar stance when it came to the Manchester United captain's verdict.

"We said Lisandro Martinez was bang out of order for calling out the hierarchy," Carragher said on CBS Sports.

"For Bruno Fernandes to do that, it is a disgrace. Last season he was Player of the Year. That was due to Michael Carrick coming in as manager. He wouldn't have got that award without Carrick. He put him back in his right position.

"His attitude and the way he goes about things, it is not right at all. He has reacted like that because he was brought off and he has been embarrassed tonight by the manager.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manchester United boss Michael Carrick admitted his team's performance was 'not acceptable' in their 4-1 loss at Como in the Champions League

"When he talks about pressing, whether it is man-to-man or zonal, for years, Bruno Fernandes has meant Man Utd can't press.

"He runs all over the place like a kid in the school yard for the supporters. They all think he's working hard, he is not. He is killing the rest of the team by doing it.

"He is not playing in a successful era at Manchester United but years ago there was a captain called Brian Robson, one of the greatest players to ever play for Man Utd.

"He didn't play for teams that won leagues or European cups every year. He is still seen as one of the greatest players to play for the club. He never threw a manager or the players under the bus. He kept fighting for Man Utd.

"Watching him [Bruno] play every week, throwing his arms up at players constantly, it is a disgrace that he has called out the manager considering how he has performed this season on the pitch. Awful attitude and not what a Manchester United captain should be.

"How many managers has he had? Every single manager at Man Utd has not had an identity?

"[Como boss] Cesc Fabregas, I think he is the best young thing in managerial terms, but Man Utd is rotten from top to bottom. Everything about the club.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On Paper Talk, Henry Winter disagrees with Bruno Fernandes for publicly criticising Michael Carrick's tactics after Manchester United lost 4-1 at Como

"This can't go on for a club of this stature. I am glad Michael Carrick came out and said that about Bruno Fernandes. That they don't run, because they don't run.

"I am delighted he brought him off and delighted he had a pop back at him."

'Looks like another Man Utd manager is going to bite the dust'

While Carragher may have been pleased with Carrick's response to Fernandes, he admitted that it might be the final straw for the former midfielder as Man Utd manager.

"It's embarrassing. But the worst thing about it I that I don't think there were many people who thought Manchester United could win tonight," Carragher added.

"So, in some ways it doesn't feel like a shock result. I think the manner of it is the shocking part of it.

"I think it's such a bad result and a bad performance that it could have serious repercussions for the manager, unfortunately for him.

"Good lad, good player for Man Utd, did really well last season, but again It looks like another Man Utd manager is going to bite the dust."

Merse: United should stick with Carrick

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Paul Merson reflects on Manchester United's poor form but believes Michael Carrick should remain as United boss, following their heavy 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League.

While Carragher thinks Carrick's time might be coming to an end, Paul Merson has suggested that changing the manager will change nothing and that the club should stick with their man.

"It's a bad result. It's a bit like snakes and ladders. They get to the top of the ladder and then get to the snake and go back down again. It's got to get steadied out," Merson said.

"To steady the ship, I think you've got to keep with the same manager. He's proven that he did get results last year. This is what I wanted to see from Michael Carrick last season. When it was going well and people were saying give him the job, it's easy when you're winning every week.

"It's when you're not doing well how the manager reacts. Now is the time to see how you are going to react.

"What do you change the manager for? You could bring in [Carlo] Ancelotti and tell him to win the league but he will fail miserably. But, if you want to come in and start learning how to walk first and go from there...

"It's just bringing managers in and it's the same thing. It's Man Utd, you've got to win the league. You're entitled to get top four. That's not Man Utd any more."

'Carrick's change in tune startling'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Danyal Khan provides insight on three things we learned from Manchester United's embarrassing Champions League loss at Como

Sky Sports News' Danyal Khan:

"I'm still processing what we saw last night and even more incredibly, how Michael Carrick handled that situation.

"After the final whistle blows you see him going to the away fans, really ignoring a lot of the players, hands up apologising to the 100 of the 700 away stand left.

"A completely dejected Michael Carrick. There will be comparisons to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in 2021 when United were pretty comprehensively beaten by Watford. Carrick was part of that coaching staff and Solskjaer was sacked.

"Then you see Michael Carrick in his post-match press conference. He has defended this team so much after the last few months when they have been targeted with their running, their intensity and their aggression. He couldn't defend any of that.

"His captain, Bruno Fernandes, comes out questioning the tactics and Carrick bit back. The fact that he hasn't broken ranks and turned on the team, but accepted criticism that for the majority of the season has been targeted at his side, was quite startling."

Sports.title: Where is it going wrong for Carrick's Man Utd?
Sports.content:
Thursday marks five months exactly since Man Utd announced Michael Carrick would be staying on as head coach. There will be little mood for celebrating anniversaries the morning after his worst night in the role.

The 4-1 thumping in Como left Carrick, in his own words, "angry". It also ruptured open divisions in the camp, with club captain Bruno Fernandes criticising the tactical plan.

United have made their worst-ever start to a Premier League season and that European humbling means they are now seven without a win across all competitions.

It's a shocking collapse in form from the brilliant run at the back end of last season which convinced United to sign Carrick up until 2028. So what's gone wrong?

Seeds sown in the summer

This week, it was Fernandes. Last week, it was Lisandro Martinez hitting out at the hierarchy. The centre-back had technical director Jason Wilcox in his sights when he criticised the club for not strengthening the squad further in the summer transfer window.

United spent £163m - less than promoted pair Hull City and Ipswich Town, as well as seven other Premier League clubs. Midfield was the focus but left-back and centre-forward areas weren't bolstered.

Reasons for the scale of United's summer outlay are multi-layered - stretching right back to the Glazer takeover - but crucially Carrick was not able to significantly upgrade this group to go from playing just 40 games last season to taking on Champions League football and trying to improve on a third-place Premier League finish this term.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rob Dorsett explains why Manchester United can't compete to sign the best players in response to Lisandro Martinez comments

Fitness fears

The World Cup made it a draining summer for many players at elite clubs. But when concerns about this season's increased workload for United were combined with Youri Tielemans suggesting there had been a lighter load of pre-season running, alarm bells began to ring.

United's intensity - or lack of - has proven to be a standout problem.

They have been out-run in six of their seven Premier League games. The only exception was when Man City played over an hour with a man less. On Wednesday, their out-of-possession failings were again exposed.

"If you don't run back, you ain't going to win," was how Carrick put it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On Paper Talk, Henry Winter disagrees with Bruno Fernandes for publicly criticising Michael Carrick's tactics after Manchester United lost 4-1 at Como

Fernandes' form

Fernandes may have issues with the pressing plan deployed by Carrick and his coaching staff in Como but with just one goal involvement in his past nine games for United, the drop-off from the team's talisman has clearly been extremely damaging.

All four of his goal involvements in the Premier League came against Ipswich Town (three goals, one assist).

After breaking the assists record last season, his chance creation figures have halved this season.

Sesko and a misfiring attack

Fernandes' figures reflect a wider problem to United's attack.

Since that Ipswich game, he has had 12 shots - but just two on target.

No team has had more shots than United this season - but they rank joint-worst for xG per shot.

Too often it's speculative rather than substantial from United's forwards.

They were the top scorers during the final 17 games of last season, when Carrick was in charge and harnessing the powers of his Portuguese playmaker.

But the continued absence of Benjamin Sesko due to injury and the lack of an alternative out-and-out striker has left United without a focal point to target. Fernandes took on the role of false-nine on Wednesday and it didn't work.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Danyal Khan provides insight on three things we learned from Manchester United's embarrassing Champions League loss at Como

No clean sheets

If you're struggling to score, you need security at the back to give you a chance - but United haven't kept a clean sheet this season.

In Italy, the full-backs Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui had games to forget, while Matthijs de Ligt was understandably, laboured on his first appearance in 11 months.

Image: Diogo Dalot during Man Utd's Champions League match with Como

Injuries to Martinez and Luke Shaw, illness for Ayden Heaven, and suspension for Leny Yoro didn't help. But whether it's a personnel problem, an issue with United's structure without the ball, or simply their intensity and fitness to shutdown their opponents, they are being too often opened up.

Different midfield pairings have been tried in front of the backline but the right combination - which likely includes Carlos Baleba, who is working back to fitness - is still something Carrick is searching for.

Manchester United

Bournemouth Sunday 25th October 12:30pm Kick off 2:00pm

What's the fix?

Many problems mean there is no easy answer.

United could have four of the nine players unavailable on Wednesday back for Bournemouth on Sunday, which will help. Yoro, Martinez and Heaven would refresh the defence, Marcus Rashford could add a spark to the attack.

But Fernandes suggested United must win a mental battle as much as a physical one this weekend.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Paul Merson criticised Manchester United after they were thrashed 4-1 in the Champions League by Como

On the impact of Como's opener after two minutes, he said: "Conceding the goal very early makes us feeling, going into the game, already in a mood of a defeat.

"It's very difficult to get out of that at the moment, without being ourselves and trying to push and trying to be brave, trying to have the ball, trying to make something happen.

"If we're not able to do that it's going to be very difficult to get out of this situation."

At Old Trafford, United are going to have to step up and show that bravery on and off the ball to deliver a performance and result to shift the narrative and put what has gone wrong so far this season behind them.

But quickly recapturing the magic of that run of form under Carrick in the second half of last season from this position would be some trick.

Sports.title: Sage must show willingness to adapt with pressure mounting at Palace
Sports.content:
If Crystal Palace had made the start they have this season under Oliver Glasner, they wouldn’t be a story.

Apart from the defeat to Ipswich at home - for which they had ten men for over an hour - results have largely gone as expected.

But it’s the performances, even in victories, that leaves Pierre Sage’s future in doubt. Steve Parish is giving Sage the opportunity this week to improve the team, especially from a defensive standpoint, but if that does not improve against Besiktas and Newcastle - live on Sky Sports - it’s likely a change will be made.

There have been spells in games where Crystal Palace have played very well and this is without Jean-Philippe Mateta and Ismaila Sarr at full speed.

But Sage’s team have been too easy to play against. They rarely control the match and the 17 goals conceded in seven Premier League games this season is the most in the league.

Sage has cut a jolly figure with the media since his appointment, but in recent press conferences, his frustration and pain has been clear.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Brighton and Crystal Palace.

And the Frenchman has another problem. Certain managers that are out of work currently.

There were contrasting views in the summer from the Crystal Palace hierarchy about what type of head coach was best to replace Glasner.

They were admirers of Thomas Frank, Gareth Southgate and Domenico Tedesco - all currently available - before hiring Sage. There was strong interest in Frank Lampard and Kieran McKenna too. However, the former Ipswich boss will cost any club who wants to hire him £8m if appointed before June next year.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on the Amol Rajan Connection, Gareth Southgate has revealed he has hardly watched football since leaving the England job,

It’s my understanding, that alongside Lens’ second-place finish in Ligue 1, the French Cup win led by Sage was seen as a huge positive given the success Crystal Palace have had in cup competitions of late.

And there is a feeling among the fans that Sage has been dealt a tough hand. Maxence Lacroix and Marc Guehi haven’t been replaced adequately.

Axel Disasi was brought in as the new leader of the defence and his suspension has hurt Palace. Injuries to Chadi Riad and Takehiro Tomiyasu have meant Sage has only named an unchanged back three in all competitions once.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Crystal Palace and Nottingham Forest, where Axel Disasi was sent off

Adam Wharton has not been at his best, especially struggling against Brighton. Daichi Kamada has been used further up the field while Ismaila Sarr returns to full fitness. That midfield combination needs to be addressed urgently, with Quinten Timber making a lively start to his time in south London, but perhaps needing to play in a more disciplined fashion while Palace leak goals.

A hamstring injury to Timber may force Kamada to drop deeper and could be a blessing in disguise.

But nevertheless, you play the hand you are dealt, and if Palace continue to play in the same fashion defensively, the fans will lose patience.

Crystal Palace

Newcastle United Sunday 25th October 12:30pm Kick off 2:00pm

Speaking to Timber on Tuesday, he expressed his belief that the manager can turn things around. While there have been reports suggesting that some players are unhappy with Sage's communication, I understand that the majority of the squad remain firmly behind him.

Sage gave up Champions League football to work in the Premier League, but he now finds himself with two games to turn things around.

It isn’t just results that’ll save him. Sage needs to show he’s willing to adapt himself and his team.

Sports.title: Blues buoyant & Hammers make statement - Championship Catch-up
Sports.content:
Welcome to The Championship Catch-up, a new Sky Sports column in which Andy Hinchcliffe rounds up some of the key stories from the second tier. This week:

Birmingham City's incredible recent form under Chris Davies

West Ham asserting their title credentials by winning at Swansea

Preston's lack of improvement under Graham Alexander

Davies deserves huge credit for Birmingham form

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Birmingham City and Queens Park Rangers.

You have to give Chris Davies a huge amount of credit for the transformation he's overseen. Last season, Birmingham were a possession-dominant side, but they struggled to turn that control into goals on the road. Their away form was particularly poor, and they ultimately finished well outside the play-off places.

I saw the potential there, but what Chris has done over the summer is clear. He's made them a bit more progressive. They're ranked 10th now for possession, which shows they still want the ball and want to control games, but they're playing forward a little bit more and being a bit more direct.

They've got August Priske leading the line, who's not just scoring goals but is also a big focal point they can play to. They're a team now that can play through you, over you or around you.

Liam Millar has to be in the top three best Championship players since he arrived. Davies has always said he was a player he wanted to sign, but he hadn't been able to get it done until now. You can see why, because Millar is fitting in perfectly.

I heard an interview with Millar about his own form and how well he was doing individually, but he also spoke about the team and the attacking mix they've got now. They're not predictable anymore. Last season, you could work out who was going to play, how they were going to play, and you could deal with it. Teams did that last season.

This season, with the development in their style and the signings they've made hitting the ground running, things are different. It's all about Davies.

He had to develop the style because he couldn't just say, "We'll go with Plan A again and hope it works better this season." He needed a Plan B, and that's what he's done. The players seem to really enjoy playing this new style, which is a bit more direct at times, and it's paying dividends.

Lots of people I've spoken to believe Birmingham are the best team to watch in the league and one of the most dangerous sides going forward. It really highlights the transformation Chris Davies has overseen from last season to this.

West Ham make statement with win at leaders Swansea

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Sky Bet Championship match between Swansea and West Ham.

That was the biggest standalone game of the season so far and the biggest test for both teams. Swansea weren't that far off, but I think West Ham have again shown they've got huge attacking talent.

Looking at the numbers, they've had 11 different scorers in their last five games. If you've got that attacking variety, you're going to cause teams a huge amount of problems. They've got a great balance, with the top scorers and the fourth-best defence.

Everything we've seen from West Ham so far has been right. They've only lost one game and have won six of their last eight, so they're starting to go through the gears.

The signings they've made, with Joel Piroe and Manor Solomon coming in, have gone straight into the team and are scoring goals, doing what they were brought in to do.

That win at Swansea was only 1-0, but it was a massive 1-0 away from home. You might have expected them to win at home, but to go to Swansea, given their form and the way they've played at the start of the season, was a huge test. Swansea aren't an easy team to play, so that was a massive statement win.

There haven't been many games this season where West Ham have looked vulnerable. Perhaps for half a game against Millwall, when Millwall swarmed all over them and took a 2-0 lead, but they couldn't see it out.

I haven't seen anything from West Ham so far that leads me to believe the wheels are suddenly going to come off. They've got depth, quality and creativity. Most importantly, they've got application and a desire to enjoy playing in the Championship.

Lots of players coming down from the Premier League think they don't want to be in this league. It looks like the West Ham players have embraced it, and their fans are travelling in such numbers that they've embraced it too. They've effectively said they might as well enjoy this season rather than endure it.

Everything has fallen into place for West Ham so far, but they've also made their own luck through the way they've approached each game.

I probably would have said West Ham would be favourites even if they'd been eighth or ninth in the league. With what they've got, I still would have backed them.

They're further down the line now and have embraced the league much more than I thought they would in the opening 11 games. I think you'd have to say West Ham are title favourites.

Preston looking doomed as Alexander struggles to make impression

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Wrexham against Preston North End in the Sky Bet Championship.

To me, it doesn't look like anything tactical because, if you remember what happened previously, they're virtually playing the same way with roughly the same personnel that Paul Heckingbottom had.

I think it shows how much Paul overachieved last season. They finished 14th with a team whose numbers were really down in the bottom three or four. He coached the life out of that team to enable them to get results and finish around mid-table. It showed what an incredible job he did.

Graham Alexander talks about going home, and I can completely understand why he wanted to go back to the club. But he probably knew what he was taking on in terms of the squad he had. There hasn't been a huge amount of investment in players.

It was a question of whether he could do what Paul had done, coaching the life out of those players and getting them to pick up results that Paul, for some reason, wasn't able to get.

But when you look at the games and the goals they're conceding, that's the major problem. Your defensive foundations are all-important in any team, particularly in the Championship.

Under Graham, they've conceded around nine goals and scored only one. Confidence is being seriously knocked as well. When a new coach comes in, there's usually a bit of a lift, but that hasn't really taken off.

They're really struggling. They've lost nine games out of 11 and aren't even drawing matches. They're not picking up a point here or there when they manage to find a way to get a draw. That's not happening either.

If things don't change drastically, they're going to be in real trouble.

Sports.title: Can McLaren 'up their game' to respond to Red Bull threat?
Sports.content:
McLaren will introduce further upgrades at the United States Grand Prix as they bid to improve their car's performance and stave off a resurgent Red Bull in the standings over the remainder of the season.

The reigning world champions continue to sit third in the Constructors' Championship with six rounds to go but fell into the clutches of fourth-placed Red Bull over the first of the end-of-season triple headers.

While McLaren failed to score a podium across that run of races, Red Bull claimed four top-three finishes - including two wins for Max Verstappen - to cut what had been a 76-point deficit to their rivals to just seven points.

McLaren's official pre-Austin preview described the team's results over the last three events as falling "significantly short of expectations" and that their 33-point haul in that run was "significantly lower than anticipated".

McLaren now head to a Circuit of the Americas track in Austin this weekend that they are hoping will be more suited to the strengths of their car, which will be boosted by some further revisions.

Rob Marshall, McLaren's chief technical officer, said: "We're bringing a modest selection of upgrades for this event, aimed at improving some braking reliability and performance issues. We also have some small floor changes to test.

"We have all seen how difficult it is to predict the relative performance of the top teams over the last five or six races.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fascinating insight into McLaren's communication between pit wall in Baku and McLaren's Technology Centre in Woking.

"Obviously, there are many factors in play here: cars being upgraded, cars suiting and drivers liking certain circuits among other factors. The last few races have not been great for us, but I think we're getting stronger again and Austin is probably a better circuit for our car.

"Practice will be important for correlating what we've seen in our development tools with the track.

"We are still learning how best to extract performance from this car. We have the full range of corner types here so getting the best balance for the whole lap will be our main focus."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McLaren team principal Andrea Stella reacts to the Sprint collision between Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri at the Singapore Grand Prix.

'They need to up their game'

McLaren's cause in Singapore was not helped by them losing eight points on the final lap of the Sprint when their cars collided after Lando Norris attempted an overtake on Oscar Piastri. Norris later apologised for the accident, admitting it was ill-advised move on his team-mate at such a late stage of the short-form race.

The world champion said in the team's Austin preview that "I take responsibility for my mistakes, and I learn from them".

McLaren now return to the scene of a previous high-profile incident in Austin from 2025, when both their drivers crashed out on the first lap of the Sprint in a chain reaction set off by Piastri colliding with Nico Hulkenberg, and have little room for any similar missed opportunities 12 months on.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris collide on the first corner after dramatic multi-car contact which forces both McLarens to retire at the US Grand Prix Sprint race!

Speaking on the post-Singapore GP edition of The F1 Show podcast, Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins said: "McLaren have had a few incidents through the year where they have not maximised their points.

"[In Singapore] Max Verstappen maximised the result, McLaren did not and there have been several weekends where McLaren did not maximise the result. This accident [in the Sprint] was a silly example of it.

"Arguably, I think if Hadjar hadn't missed three races when Liam Lawson was in that car Red Bull would be ahead of McLaren. And that's what McLaren know, that they have been saved I think, at this stage, because Hadjar wasn't in that car for three races and [Red Bull] weren't scoring the points that they could have done.

Image: McLaren have won the Constructors' Championship in each of the past two seasons but are in danger of finishing fourth this year

"But now Red Bull are on the up and they need to up their game if they are going to survive in that P3 position because it doesn't look like it at the moment."

Karun Chandhok added: "I think they probably know they now have the fourth-fastest car, which is a bit of a concern, and Red Bull are probably now the fastest if not second-fastest car for most tracks."

Sports.title: ‘Angry’ Carrick on the brink as Fernandes hits out at Manchester United tactics
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick’s future as Manchester United manager is in the balance after a humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como on Wednesday night.

Before Bournemouth’s visit to Old Trafford on Sunday his future may be discussed by Jason Wilcox, the director of football, Omar Berrada, the chief executive, and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the co-owner who controls sporting policy.

On a torrid night an “angry” ­Carrick insisted afterwards that he had not given his position any thought and was forced to defend himself against Bruno Fernandes after his captain questioned the manager’s tactics of not pressing against Cesc Fàbregas’s team. Carrick also criticised his side for not running. The defeat by Como in the third Champions League group game leaves United with only two wins all season from 11 games. ­Carrick’s side are in 13th place in the Premier League and were eliminated from the Carabao Cup last month.

The 45-year-old was asked if he fears for his job. “Listen, I’ve not given my own position any thought,” he said. “[My thoughts are] for the supporters – I was one of them watching that and I wasn’t happy at all.”

Carrick was then asked if he could walk away following the latest defeat in Europe. “No. It’s not about me right now and my feelings in that regard,” the manager said. “It’s more of as a team and as a football club, what we want to look like, what we should look like. And as I said, the results can come and go at times, but you got to do it in a certain way. And that wasn’t it.”

700 United sup­porters travelled. At the end around 200 remained and Carrick went to ­apologise to them, noticeably ­ignoring his players. After United conceded Nico Paz’s second-minute goal, Carrick’s men were unable to mount any resistance. By 57 minutes Como led 3-0, due to Tasos Douvikas’s strike and Paz’s second, before Jacobo Ramón completed the scoring for the Italian side on 76 minutes. Joshua Zirkzee netted in added time for the visitors.

Fernandes openly challenged ­Carrick’s strategy during the match. “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said.

The captain was asked if Carrick’s tactics were wrong. “That’s on the manager and staff to see, not me,” he said. “Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable. As you saw with them, the centre-back was coming to mark me in my own half. We need to do that as a team but we were unable to.”

View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes and his United teammates were second-best throughout. Photograph: Alessandro Garofalo/Reuters

Fernandes’s criticism was put to his manager after the match. “We actually half-pressed man-to-man the second half and then conceded a goal from that,” Carrick said.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don’t run, and you don’t run forward, and you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win.”

Carrick was asked how he can raise the mood before Bournemouth’s visit. “I’m bitterly disappointed, I’m frustrated; more than frustrated, I’m really angry. But you’ve got to move on. You got to deal with what’s next and see what that looks like.

“At this moment in time, there’s a lot to do before that next game to get the team ready because that was a difficult night for everyone. I have to apologise to the supporters.”

Sports.title: Harry Kane admits wait to learn if he has won Ballon d’Or is ‘very stressful’ for family
Sports.content:
Harry Kane would love to know now whether he has won the Ballon d’Or because the uncertainty and constant questions are driving his family to distraction. But the Bayern Munich and England striker accepts the suspense before the big reveal at the London Palladium on Monday night is part of the show.

Kane is the odds-on favourite to win the prestigious individual honour after a prolific run of form. The 33-year-old scored 61 goals for Bayern last season and 12 for England. This time out, he has 10 for Bayern and six for England. He scored from the penalty spot in Wednesday night’s 2-2 Champions League draw against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena, although his stand-out moment was the inch-perfect through ball that set up Alphonso Davies to make it 1-1.

Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal is the second-favourite for the Ballon d’Or and Kylian Mbappé of Real Madrid is next in the betting.

“I think my wife would prefer to know and my family … it’s very stressful for everyone,” Kane said, when asked whether he would prefer to be told in advance of the ceremony. “I can see why they don’t tell people. They want everyone to go, all the big names, and there will be more people watching it if they don’t know so I can understand why.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“From my point of view, of course I’d love to know to just kind of see and not have to wait throughout the whole night. But it is their decision, I can’t control that. We’ll have to just enjoy it and try not to stress out too much. I try not to think about it. Obviously it is hard not to. There are always rumours and stuff flying around so you try to stay away from it.”

Sports.title: ‘It doesn’t look good’: Arteta concerned as Saka limps off against Bayern Munich
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta made no attempt to conceal his concern over the quad injury that forced Bukayo Saka out of Arsenal’s 2-2 Champions League draw at Bayern Munich, saying it did not “look good at all”.

The manager was delighted with the fight that his players showed, Declan Rice earning a deserved point with an 82nd-minute equaliser. Arsenal had led through Eberechi Eze, who came on in the 10th minute for the stricken Saka, before Harry Kane took centre stage. The Bayern striker set up Alphonso Davies for 1-1 before giving his team the lead from the penalty spot.

It was Saka’s setback that provided the sour note for Arsenal. He collapsed to the turf after a routine battle with Davies and walked off slowly after treatment. Saka was still moving in a very limited way as he left the stadium.

“It doesn’t look good at all but we have to wait and see,” Arteta said. “They [the medics] are a bit concerned. A player who has to come off with a really sharp pain is never good news. Bukayo did not start the game against Lille last Tuesday, then he started at Nottingham Forest on Sunday and it happened very early in this game. The level of intensity that this game requires, as well, is something incredible.

“You could see it on Tuesday night, the PSG-Barcelona game, what happened [with players getting injured]. This is man-to-man for 96 minutes in every action. There’s no breathing. The stress, the quality, the intensity, the level that you need … it’s unbelievable. It’s the highest level. And those things happen, unfortunately.”

Arteta insisted that he wanted more than the draw. “We take it, although that doesn’t mean we are really happy about it as we prepared to win,” he said. “You could see that right from the beginning – the mindset, the purpose and the intention that the team has, to be very dominant, to come here and cause problems to Bayern. To press them and attack them. That’s certainly what we’ve done. We were the better team in the first 25 minutes, we got the goal … unfortunately we also got the injury of Bukayo, which was a big setback.

“The team showed incredible composure, the spirit to keep going, to attack them. The finishers came in and made an impact, as well. After scoring the goal [for 2-2], you see the reaction of the team. We wanted to take the ball and go and attack them again to come and win the game.”

Sports.title: Paris Saint-Germain sparkle on the pitch while the city of light burns around them | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
PASSION!

GOOOOAL!

MVP!

The security deployment will be massive.

Those who sought to bring down the Republic will have to answer for it.

Tell you who would have loved this? Who would have been utterly engrossed scrolling the hashtag #Paris on Tuesday night as two things happened simultaneously, the harrowing of the Barcelona defence at the Parc des Princes, and the harrowing of Paris itself via tales of city-centre thuggery and end-of-days political doom‑mongering.

The big man, Guy Debord himself. The Society of the Spectacle, you say? Actually, I think we’re past that now. Hold the society bit. We’ll just take the spectacle.

The great Parisian Situationist philosopher wasn’t really one for managed fun. But it was impossible not to be bowled over by the extraordinary pre-match show for Paris Saint‑Germain versus Barcelona, Champions League Matchday Three.

The wild pyrotechnics, the plumes of smoke, the full-wrap light show, the lime-green robo‑text spelling out every player’s name on the pitch. Although not the Barcelona names, sadly, for anyone with an unrealised desire to see the words “ANTHONY GORDON” projected in vast letters for the delight of a shrieking crowd.

Admittedly, the Halloween‑themed tifo banner showing a masked Paris Saint-Germain serial killer-type literally butchering the Barcelona badge to death with his bloodied chainsaw was perhaps a bit much. As were the Barça Puta signs, which are now reportedly the subject of a complaint to Uefa.

But it was a wild and all‑consuming spectacle, annihilating every other impulse in your head to a green thought in a green shade. And in the process capturing the profound sense of cognitive dissonance in the city.

View image in fullscreen PSG fans light flares after their team took the lead against Barcelona. Photograph: Julien de Rosa/AFP/Getty Images

Just walking around the streets of central Paris earlier in the day generated its own mild whiplash. On the face of it this was still the same city of flâneurs and tourists and everyday bistro business, and not, repeat not, a civil war drama or some kind of emergent military caliphate.

But the sense of dread was also tangible. You still got the occasional crunch of glass underfoot. Here and there charred bikes and scooters had been politely piled to one side. Even close to the Parc, away from the main hotspots, shopkeepers could be seen emerging warily into their doorways at the sound of a police siren.

By Tuesday night, a total of 2,513 people had been taken into police custody after the events of the weekend. At least 420 rental bikes had been destroyed or maimed. Liberated high-value retail goods were already being sold on Vinted, a commendable show of entrepreneurial energy from the maligned younger generation.

Not that you’d suspect these two worlds had any kind of overlap, lost in the booming triumphalism around PSG’s 4–2 win, one of the most beautifully luminous football matches you’re ever likely to see. Or indeed reading the coverage of an event that seems to have been treated in France like its own clear, clean space, floating above the flames, all the chat about the brilliance of Monsieur Dynamite, Désiré Doué, the wonderful television audiences on Canal+ TV, the whole of European football “kneeling before the machine” (are we sure this isn’t to do with anarchic rejection of social control?). “Paris est insubmersible!” was the headline in Le Parisien. But is it?

Remember when football used to reflect the world? Or just provide clues, a commentary, some kind of metaphor? This is no longer the case. At a time when even the most thunderous of commentators is struggling to summarise all this in suitably trite and damning terms, it was hard to avoid the feeling Paris Saint-Germain, the pet power football project of the state of Qatar, expresses this dualism perfectly.

Sometimes you just have to let football tell you things. “People who want to cause trouble in the city centres next Saturday will be prevented,” Emmanuel Macron announced on Tuesday evening, speaking, as it happens, from Doha, where he met Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad al-Thani, ultimate owner of PSG.

View image in fullscreen Désiré Doué (left) with João Neves after scoring PSG’s first goal against Barcelona. Photograph: David Ramos/Uefa/Getty Images

Macron is said to be considering deploying the French military to keep the peace on the streets before the next planned protests, although even here he may have to ask Qatar’s permission if he wants to deploy any of the French troops currently deployed working its missile systems, or embedded in the Doha security services.

The key event Macron is tooling up for is this Saturday night, 24 October, the date the gilets jaunes social media feed has set for an even greater swell of disorder. And again this will be football adjacent, with PSG playing Lyon at home on Sunday, a top‑of‑the-table capital‑city clash played out against whatever wreckage is left, however many thousands of Dot bikes are savaged, whatever guerrilla skirmishes are still playing out in the Marais.

What does this really have to do with football and the Ici C’est Paris brand appropriated by a state outreach project? Well, what are these demonstrations anyway? There have been many theories put forward as to what exactly is happening here, what is the spark, the kindling, the fire behind this disorder. School protests were the original line. Others have now roped in some kind of nebulous omni-cause, Instagram-activism, perhaps even a barbarian takeover, the decline of the west, savagery at the gates, of the type Donald Trump pretends to see.

Do you need a single reason? Take a look around. Modern life is pretty alarming on a minute‑to‑minute basis. Disaffection, alienation, a sense of being transformed in real time into a passive economic consumer unit, a set of eyeballs, an avatar of consumption. French youth unemployment is close to 20%. Robots nobody wants are being lined up to take jobs that don’t exist. Why don’t these young people want to join a youth club? Why don’t they 

On the other hand, what is PSG in Paris, other than the perfect expression of this? It often seems to surprise people that celebrations of PSG victories end up with riots and burnt-out cars. But Paris is both a beautiful and deeply dysfunctional city, a place of make‑believe and deprivation, where the centre is a perfect, performative relic, the suburbs shunted out to the ring roads, a life lived inside a box, noses pressed up against the glass, peering through your binoculars at the city of someone else’s love.

Paris is the divide between overclass and churn expressed in a single city. It’s everything you might have had but never will. And PSG represent this like no other entity, a football club owned as an act of outreach by a staggeringly rich inherited monarchy, weaponised passion, borrowed culture, engineered spectacle, deeply cynical but also deeply seductive.

View image in fullscreen Damage after the riots in Place de la République. Photograph: Telmo Pinto/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

Why are the Qataris splurging hundreds of millions into this project? Because they just really like high-pressing positional football? Qatar is the indentured labour state that employs Colin Kaepernick to promote its outreach projects. It will hymn its connections to the footballers of the banlieue, which is true and real and valuable, but not because of anything this political project wants or needs other than public relations.

It is in its own way a perfect human lab experiment, synthesised beauty, collectivism, with a cold, cold hand at its heart. And this is why there weren’t two versions of Paris in evidence on Tuesday night, just the same one, the dark side and the shiny side, an engine of the same divisions, the same kind of violence, right down to the sight of kids in PSG training gear dodging the police or taunting the barricades at the Place de la République.

And now we have Sunday night to come, more Ici C’est Paris, more PASSION. What kind of background will it be played out against? Does it matter under the lights? Will anyone notice?

Le Monde has described these events as a very basic test of the republic, its ability to bend, to remain essentially itself, the state’s willingness to pit itself against its own people. Football, as ever, holds these answers already. PSG’s Qatari owners have spent the past 15 years flaunting this city like a global luxury brand, extending its reach, creating its own ideal of conspicuous consumption, spectacle, triumph, son et lumière, bread and roses. As ever, if you want to know how and why, football has the answers.

Sports.title: Shola Ameobi: ‘I thought: how can I be most useful to Newcastle? Then the cog started turning’
Sports.content:
“There were times where I feared for my life as a kid, being harassed and chased by different groups of people,” Shola Ameobi says. “There were situations where I had to sprint to get away from groups of lads who didn’t like me because of what I looked like.”

Ameobi is recalling growing up in Newcastle during the late 1980s and 1990s, having moved from Nigeria aged six. There were, he says, “lots of moments” like that. “It was almost as if I had to hide myself to be able to do what I love to do. It wasn’t a very nice feeling, having to worry about getting from A to B. It was just part of my world. I had to be more aware of my surroundings and what I was doing.”

Ameobi’s “A” was often the family home, situated within a few pitch lengths of Newcastle’s St James’ Park, and “B” was frequently the club’s then Benwell base, where he would head for academy training.

“It built incredible resilience in me,” Ameobi says. “That really helped me in a sporting context in my career but also as a person, understanding that, irrespective of what people thought of me, what really mattered was the value I put on myself.”

That young boy running in fear became the scorer of 79 goals in 397 appearances for Newcastle including seven against their local rivals, Sunderland. The likelihood is that some of those he fled from while wearing a club tracksuit subsequently cheered him.

Since July, Ameobi has been Newcastle’s head of corporate affairs, after seven years as the loans coordinator. His role is to lead on “strategic external engagement” to ensure “we’re doing things that are valuable not only to us as a football club but to the region. We want to make this club the heartbeat of this city. But by being the heartbeat of the city, I think it’s making sure that we integrate well into everything the city is about, whether that’s civically, whether that’s through our sport or through our community engagement.”

Ameobi’s job switch followed the 100-day review conducted by the CEO, David Hopkinson. At the end of a preliminary discussion, Hopkinson told Ameobi to take the weekend to consider things. But Ameobi, while grateful for the “level of trust and commitment”, pushed back, wanting to consider what the role would look like in practice. Six months and plentiful discussions later, he accepted.

View image in fullscreen An overjoyed Shola Ameobi wheels away after scoring against Newcastle’s derby rivals, Sunderland, in October 2010. Photograph: Michael Mayhew/Sportsphoto/Allstar

For Ameobi the leap to an executive position was not as huge as it might appear. He started his previous role in the Mike Ashley days and built that department “from nothing”, he says. “That’s really helped me understand how to business-plan and build a team.”

Ameobi has been part of the Premier League’s Black participants advisory group since it formed in 2019. Its successes include implementing the No Room for Racism action plan in 2021 – this weekend marks the second of two match rounds this month dedicated to the initiative – and the pilot launch of the player to executive pathways scheme in 2022. The scheme is designed to help those from underrepresented groups into executive roles and Ameobi was part of the initial seven-strong cohort.

“It gave me a really good framework,” he says. “It took us through, at a very high level, what the different streams of executive work look like, whether that’s finance, brand, the future of working, how organisations work. That gave me a little bit of confidence, if I’m honest, more than anything, to go: ‘Actually, a lot of the things I’m already doing actually translate into that world.’

View image in fullscreen Shola Ameobi at an event celebrating the supporters’ group The Black Geordie Club. Photograph: NUFC

“One of the biggest things was working in a pressurised environment, which is what I’ve done for 20 years, and learning how that can really help you in those moments when things get a little squirrelly, when they aren’t going as planned.”

Completing the programme fuelled a fire in Ameobi that had flickered for two decades. In November 2006, having struggled with a hip injury for several years, he had career-saving surgery. The resulting time out was “the start of my thought process beyond the football pitch”. Whether he would return to playing at his previous level, or at all, was uncertain. So, Ameobi’s thoughts turned to: “How can I best be useful to my teammates and this football club? That’s when the cog started turning.

“Football wasn’t always going to be there so who am I outside of the footballer? There were some really hard questions I had to answer during a very, very difficult time. There were some dark moments.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Ameobi navigated those moments with the help of a psychologist and by leaning on his family. “I’ve always been fascinated with leadership, right from an early age,” he says. “My father was a leader of a church, and he’s been the biggest influence of my life when it comes to leadership and how to lead well.”

He cites the late Sir Bobby Robson, who gave him a professional debut aged 18, and Alan Pardew, who managed him at Newcastle and Crystal Palace, as footballing influences. The former “still to this day has such an impact on the way I think about the game, the way I think about the person more than what you’re doing”, while the latter “used me to channel my leadership within the dressing room and wider squad to help him deal with some of the issues we were going through”.

View image in fullscreen Ameobi has gone from academy graduate to first-team mainstay to an executive position within the club. Photograph: Graeme Robertson/The Guardian

Ameobi also holds a master’s in strategic leadership, and it is obvious from observing him at an event to celebrate the supporters’ group The Black Geordie Club that he is a natural with people. There is a presence to him, a warmth, that puts others at ease.

Ameobi is unrelenting in wanting to use his position to improve society. He grew up watching Andy Cole at Newcastle, and memories of Tino Asprilla’s 1997 Champions League hat-trick against Barcelona bring the broadest of smiles. “That was the moment where time stood still. It was almost like I said to myself: ‘What’s wrong with you, Shola? You should be giving everything to be there.’

Allow Instagram content? This article includes content provided by Instagram . We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content, click 'Allow and continue'. Allow and continue

“You need to feel like you belong, you need to see yourself there, and I think that is so important when it comes to inspiration, and people who aspire to be great in whatever sphere.

“I think it’s so important that those who are in those positions give back and share their experience, and share what helped them get to where they’re at. Being a young Black kid who has walked the walk throughout the club, from youth team to first team and now into this executive role, I want to show that anything’s possible for anybody.

“Part of the reason that I want to continue to push myself is because, yes, I want to be successful, but I want to show that anything’s possible if you’ve got the hunger, irrespective of what you look like and where you come from. I want to be an inspiration to the next generation.”

Sports.title: Barkley and Buendía on target as Aston Villa sink Viking to maintain perfect start
Sports.content:
For a little over 20 minutes, Aston Villa could look down on the rest of Europe. They had scaled the Champions League summit on goal difference when Henrik Heggheim put through his own net and the fact was not lost on the Holte End, who reflected their position in song and perhaps allowed themselves another glimpse back to the days when their supremacy was undisputed. “We’ve conquered before, we’re prepared for more,” the pre-match tifo display had read.

Perhaps Villa really will rekindle the spirit of 1982 but the frustration here, albeit minor in the wider scheme, was that they could not maintain their bird’s-eye view over the continent. A superbly taken volley by Peter Christiansen, awarded by the video assistant referee after initially being disallowed for offside, gave Viking a consolation their second-half display deserved and meant Unai Emery’s side must make do with slumming it just behind Paris Saint-Germain.

“Collectively and individually we did a good job and some players also made a step forward in their confidence,” said Emery, who was pleased with Villa’s seriousness against opponents still finding their way in a first campaign at this level. “Each match has an objective to get better, to be consistent and be very demanding.”

The hard work had been done in an opening period whose scoreline hardly did justice to Villa’s total dominance. Viking had drawn at home with Bayern Munich in their previous game, a fact that would look more explicable when they emerged from their shell later, but were barely afforded a kick and looked vulnerable every time the ball was delivered from wide.

Nicolas Jackson, electric in the 6-0 thrashing of Fenerbahce, fluffed two free headers in the opening seven minutes and a similarly resounding win came to appear possible. Emery had made four changes but Villa, working the play smoothly from side to side, were a consistent threat and unfazed by opponents whose attacking ambition was initially minimal.

The breakthrough arrived after a spell of pressure sparked when a cross from João Gomes, the makeshift right-back, deflected on to the bar. Two corners later, an inswinger from the livewire 18-year-old Ibrahim Mbaye was met by Ross Barkley, who leapt highest to plant a firm header across Arild Østbø at the near post.

Barkley had scored twice in the previous week’s big win but the rest of the first half resembled a quest for Emiliano Buendía to put his mark on the scoresheet. Straight after the opener Buendía looped a header wide of the vacant goal after Østbø had parried from Alysson, who was a rangy threat throughout, and then he charged on to a clever John McGinn corner only to aim straight at the keeper.

View image in fullscreen Ross Barkley heads Aston Villa’s opener from Ibrahim Mbaye’s corner. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

It was third time lucky when the VAR reviewed a needless challenge by the Viking captain Zlatko Tripic on Alysson, who had run into traffic in the box, and led the referee Sebastian Gishamer to award a penalty. Buendía rolled it in, his fourth goal in consecutive European games; 37 minutes had passed and Viking had still not produced a meaningful attack.

After the restart they showed some of the intensity and verve that had ruffled Bayern, the richly promising midfielder Tobias Moi warming Zion Suzuki’s midriff and seeing a goalbound effort blocked. Suzuki also beat away a Tripic drive. But Villa could now exploit space in behind and, after flashing an angled effort just wide, Alysson got away once again to create the third. This time his attempted centre snicked off Heggheim, who was desperately trying to recover, and gave Østbø no chance.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Now Villa were, as the home choirs gleefully announced, top of the league and they received further opportunities to hammer home the point. Alejandro Garnacho saw one of them saved by Østbø after a strong run but Viking remained a threat and Christiansen’s finish, emphatically converting Kristoffer Askildsen’s deep cross, was by some distance the best of the night.

“The second half was much more like the Viking we want to be,” said Morten Jensen, who co-manages the Norwegian champions alongside Bjarte Lunde Aarsheim. “Maybe we had too much respect for them in the first half, they were all over us.”

View image in fullscreen Emiliano Buendía calmly doubles Aston Villa’s lead from the penalty spot. Photograph: Alex Livesey/AVFC/Getty Images

Nine points from nine, not to mention 12 consecutive home wins in Europe, mean Villa are flying. Sweeping Fenerbahce and Viking aside can “give us confidence and comfort for the next challenges,” Emery said. They will need plenty of it given a trip to Barcelona follows the relatively soft run presented so far. Maybe the peak is yet to come.

Sports.title: Champions League: Silva sparks Real Madrid’s demolition of Leipzig as Lask stun Sporting
Sports.content:
Real Madrid claimed a third Champions League victory in as many games by thrashing RB Leipzig 4-1 on Wednesday, with Kylian Mbappé and Yan Diomande among the goals for José Mourinho’s side.

Bernardo Silva opened the scoring for Madrid from close range towards the end of a tight first half, with Arda Guler doubling the record 15-time European champions’ advantage soon after the interval.

Mbappé bent home a third before Tidiam Gomis pulled one back for the German side and Diomande rammed a volley into the top corner to cap Madrid’s triumph late on.

“We know every point is important to get into the top eight, we know we have to win as many games as possible – we’ve won three and there are five to go,” Mbappé said. The France forward, who hopes to win the Ballon d’Or next week, has netted in each of Madrid’s Champions League matches this season and has 12 goals in 12 games.

“I’m doing well [but] I think I can do more,” he said. “I’m one of the few players who always has to demand more from himself ... right now it’s a good moment, but we have to keep going and I have to do more.”

Lask launched an impressive comeback at Sporting to earn their first Champions League win of the season. The Austrian champions went behind when Luis Suárez scored from the spot after five minutes, but equalised 10 minutes later through Christoph Lang.

The visitors then stunned the Estádio José Alvalade as Sasa Kalajdzic and Krystof Danek put them 3-1 up, the former rounding off a smart team move and the latter firing in at the near post. Suárez scored again for the hosts late on, but it was not enough.

View image in fullscreen Victor Osimhen, with Yunus Akgun on his shoulders, after rounding off Galatasaray’s 4-2 win at Lille. Photograph: Matthieu Mirville/Zuma Press Wire/Shutterstock

Galatasaray swept past Lille at the Stade Pierre-Mauroy, setting the tone with a goal after two minutes from Yunus Akgun.

Lille levelled the score via Soriba Diaoune, who then put them 2-1 up in the 39th minute. Aleksey Batrakov made it 2-2 just before half-time, however, before an own goal from Nabil Bentaleb and Victor Osimhen, in action against his former club, sealed a 4-2 victory.

Inter had Alessandro Bastoni sent off midway through the second half before Carlos Augusto’s late goal secured a 1-0 win at home to Shakhtar Donetsk, as the Italian champions got their first points of the league phase.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Bastoni was sent off for two yellow cards in as many minutes, putting Inter on the back foot. Carlos Augusto saved the day in the 77th minute, capping a lightning-fast counterattack with a low finish.

View image in fullscreen Isco wheels away after netting from 12 yards to put Real Betis 1-0 up against Feyenoord. Photograph: Antonio Pozo/PRESSINPHOTO/Shutterstock

Real Betis, who beat Feyenoord 1-0 via a penalty kick from Isco, made it three from three in the Champions League to extend their strong start to the season.

Betis had the lion’s share of the chances, but only broke the deadlock when Jeremiah St Juste was adjudged to have handled in the box. Isco stepped up and fired low into the right-hand corner for what proved to be the winner.

Club Brugge defeated Lens 3-0 at the Jan Breydel Stadium in a ruthless home performance. The Belgians went 1-0 up through Hans Vanaken in first-half stoppage time before Joaquin Seys and Carlos Forbs secured the win in the second half.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo asked for punishment ‘without mitigation’, then fought to cut it
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo successfully fought to reduce his punishment for walking out on a Portugal training camp, after saying publicly that his sanction should be imposed “without mitigating circumstances”.

After leaving the training camp in Denmark last month, Ronaldo said in a lengthy statement on social media that he should be punished as the Portuguese Football Federation saw fit and that his role as captain constituted “an aggravating factor”.

However, during the disciplinary council’s inquiry the 41-year-old put forward several arguments for cutting his punishment, including his clean disciplinary record in recent seasons and his services to football.

Ronaldo received a 30-day suspension and a €255 (£215) fine, and the document accompanying the ruling reveals he presented three arguments in mitigation: his disciplinary record this season and in the previous three seasons; his services to football including recognition for sporting merit; and his contribution to establishing the facts of the case.

To support these arguments, Ronaldo listed the club titles he has won and his achievements with the national team: the 2016 European Championship and two Nations League titles. His individual awards were also highlighted, including the fact that the Al-Nassr forward has won the Ballon d’Or five times. Beyond his achievements on the pitch, he mentioned the honours he had received from senior state officials.

The decision-makers accepted Ronaldo’s arguments concerning his achievements and services to the country, using them to halve his suspension and fine. The punishment was then halved again because Ronaldo had accepted responsibility for his actions.

Ronaldo’s suspension will be served in a period during which there are no international matches. It is unclear whether he intends to return to the national team – or whether the head coach, Jorge Jesus, will select him again.

The account of events provides a clearer picture of the circumstances surrounding Ronaldo’s departure from the training camp. After head coach Jesus held a press conference in which he reiterated that he was in charge of the team and that no player would influence his selection decisions, Ronaldo requested a vehicle from the FPF and set off for Copenhagen airport.

During the journey, he called the Portuguese federation’s president, Pedro Proença, and told him he was “not in the right frame of mind” to remain with the team.

“The defendant [Ronaldo] did not inform or provide prior justification to the federation or the men’s national team officials regarding his intention to leave the stadium and the training camp,” the ruling states. It says that between 30 September and 4 October, Ronaldo missed more than 30 team activities, including travel, training sessions and meals.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The federation says that Ronaldo’s promise on social media, after leaving the training camp, to tell his fans “the whole truth” brought further negative attention to the incident: “Given his prominence as a public figure on a global scale, the defendant could not have been unaware that his conduct, in the circumstances in which it occurred, would be subject to intense media scrutiny, as indeed it was.”

Ronaldo was therefore “expected to exercise particular caution in choosing the timing and manner in which he expressed his dissatisfaction with the manager’s decisions and conduct”. Instead, the player “further fuelled speculation and public curiosity by posting on Instagram on the very day he left Copenhagen, announcing that, ‘in due course’, he would tell ‘all Portuguese people the truth about the reasons that led to his departure from the men’s senior national team’,” the inquiry concluded.

Portugal are scheduled to play Denmark again in their next game on 14 November in Braga.
