Sports.title: David Raya makes surprise transfer admission in huge worry for Arsenal
Sports.content:
David Raya might just have set alarm bells ringing among Arsenal fans with comments about his future.

The three-time back-to-back Golden Glove-winning goalkeeper is happy with the Premier League champions – but that doesn't mean he won't be tempted by a move away at some point.

2 Raya has been integral to Arsenal's recent success, becoming regarded as one of the best goalkeepers in the world Credit: Getty

Raya dreams of Spain return

A Spain international and 2026 World Cup winner, Raya has made clear his desire to play in his homeland, having spent his entire senior career to date in England.

"I would love to play in LaLiga one day," the 31-year old told MARCA.

"Right now, I'm very happy at Arsenal, but it's true that I'd love to play in LaLiga one day. It's a very competitive league.

"I'm Spanish and I'd love to play in Spain, that's obvious."

Born in Barcelona, Raya started out with nearby club Cornella before heading to England to join Blackburn Rovers aged 16 – going on to make almost 100 first-team appearances in the Championship and League One.

His exploits for Blackburn saw him snapped up by Brentford in 2019, and he starred as the Bees won a first-ever promotion to the Premier League two years later.

Having impressed over his first two top-flight campaigns with the west London side, he made the switch across the capital to Arsenal in 2023.

Since then, Raya has established himself as one of the very best goalkeepers in world football.

Only the third 'keeper to win three successive Premier League Golden Glove awards for the most clean sheets in the division, he recorded 19 shutouts en route to the title with Arsenal last term.

Raya has kept 72 clean sheets in 176 Premier League appearances overall.

2 Raya conceded at a rate of barely 0.7 goals per Premier League game as Arsenal won the title last season Credit: Getty

He also helped Arsenal to the final of last season's Champions League.

What's next for Arsenal?

That's a trophy Mikel Arteta will be determined to deliver for the first time in the Gunners' history this time around.

They continued their European campaign with an entertaining 2-2 draw away to Bayern Munich on Wednesday, moving to seven points from their first three games in the league phase of the Champions League.

Arteta's men have also made a strong start to their Premier League title defence, winning six of their opening seven matches, trailing early leaders Manchester City by three points.

The Gunners are next in action at home to Everton on Sunday.

That's their first of five games in three competitions between now and the next international break, including a league trip to Liverpool next weekend.

Sports.title: EFL boss sacked 10 games into season despite two promotions in three years
Sports.content:
EFL boss sacked 10 games into season despite two promotions in three years

Bromley have sacked Andy Woodman after winning just two games in all competitions so far this season.

Woodman, who had been in charge since March 2021, led the club to the League One for the first time in their history last term.



2 Woodman has been sacked by Bromley after a successful five-and-a-half years in charge of the club Credit: Getty

That was their second promotion in three years, with manager Woodman taking them on a remarkable rise from non-league.

However, since reaching League One, they've hit a stumbling block, with things appearing to be too much of a challenge.

Woodman has been sacked amid a four-game losing streak in the league, with the club sitting 23rd after ten matches.



The Ravens have won just two of their opening fixtures, losing six straight in all competitions since beating Huddersfield on September 19.

They have not won any of their last four league outings, also losing to Brentford U21s and Crawley Town in the Jersey Mike's Trophy.



And Woodman's last game in charge saw his side thrashed 4-0 at home to Russell Martin's Leicester City on Tuesday night.

Across his five-and-a-half year tenure as Bromley boss, Woodman took charge of 274 games, winning 117 and losing 76.



He was the third longest serving manager in the entire EFL and Premier League combined.

Bromley sack Andy Woodman

Bromley confirmed the dismissal of their long-standing manager in a statement on Thursday morning.

Owner and Chairman Robin Stanton-Gleaves said: “I would firstly like to offer my sincere thanks to Andy for all he has achieved during his time with us.

“It’s no surprise that this club has reached new heights and Andy has been fundamental in helping us achieve that.



"I would like to reassure our supporters that we will be entering this new chapter with the same ambition and determination to keep moving this football club forward.

“On a personal note, Andy has been a pleasure to work with, and I wish him all the best for the future.”

Former player Byron Webster will be taking charge on an interim basis whilst the club appoint a permanent replacement.

Woodman, who is Liverpool goalkeeper Freddie Woodman's dad, was previously a goalkeeper coach and Head of Goalkeeping at Arsenal before being appointed as Bromley manager in 2021.



His only previous managerial role before taking over at the Ravens came with semi-pro side Whitehawk.

2 Bromley have struggled since promotion to League One and Woodman has been dismissed with just two wins in ten games Credit: Getty

'I certainly won't lie down'

Woodman's sacking comes days after he said he was up for the fight of keeping Bromley in League One after a poor start.

He had criticised his team for 'gifting' opponents goals after they were beaten by Leicester on Tuesday evening.



"We're just making rash decisions, without any pressure on us," Woodman told BBC Radio London.

"That's the bit that's frustrating me at the moment because that's not what we've been built on.

"We're trying to find the answers, we're grafting and we're putting the hours in. Maybe it's a bit of quality and confidence [we are lacking], but we've got to find the solution quickly.

"I certainly won't lie down and accept what I'm seeing."

But sadly for Woodman, he hasn't been given more time to turn things around.

Sports.title: Kyle Walker urges Marcus Rashford to adapt to new position to get in England side
Sports.content:
Kyle Walker urges Marcus Rashford to adapt to new position to get in England side

Kyle Walker has told his former England teammate Marcus Rashford to consider changing position to boost his international career.

Rashford has a total of 78 caps for the Three Lions and has played the large majority of his games for his country on the left wing.

3 Walker thinks Rashford should consider playing as a striker to get into the England team more regularly Credit: Getty

But Walker thinks a potential new focus on playing as a striker for Thomas Tuchel's side could help him get more minutes.

At the start of his career with England, Rashford played up front regularly before becoming a permanent left winger.

Across his 78 caps, he has played 23 games as a striker, but only two of those games have come in the last six years.

Of course, as Harry Kane has been so dominant on the international stage as well as at club level, any other striker playing for the Three Lions has majorly struggled for regular minutes.

However, Kane is now 33 years old and coming towards the end of his career, with doubts rising over who will be able to step into his shoes after retirement - so could Rashford capitalise on that?

Walker has praised his good friend and ex-teammate for his ability on the left, but thinks he could launch a bid to start up front.

He said on talkSPORT Drive: "I like him on the left. I think he would probably be more effective though, through the middle.

"But if Marcus thinks he should be playing off the left then that's his best position, he's still a very good player."

Walker added: "I look at England...Anthony Gordon is undroppable.

"So maybe Marcus needs to look at that and think: 'Can I add another string to my bow and adapt as a No.9 and play down the middle?'"

3 With Kane now 33, his England career is in its final days, so could Rashford capitalise and become the next No.9? Credit: Getty

What else has Walker said on Rashford?

Rashford made six appearances for England at the World Cup this summer, scoring one goal at the tournament and impressing at times, but since returning to Man United his form has dipped.

And Walker thinks confidence is all the 28-year-old needs, saying: "I spoke to some of the lads during the World Cup and they said he was so sharp in training. It was like having the old Rashford back.

"I think Marcus plays a lot off confidence. I think strikers do. You score goals and everything is going completely fine.

"He just needs a bit of a run in a team. Managers, if strikers aren't having a good time, should say: 'Listen, I'm going to give you two, three games, it doesn't matter what happens, but we'll give you a bit of confidence, give you chances and you have to take them'.

"But taking him in and out, dropping him, giving him 20 minutes here and there having to showcase what he can do...

"I think it's always difficult for strikers, they want to score goals and probably try too hard."

3 Rashford has not scored or provided as assist for Man United since his return, but Walker has reiterated his passion for the club Credit: Getty

Does Rashford have a future at Man United?

So far this season, Rashford has started four of his six Premier League appearances for Man United, but he hasn't played 90 minutes.

He's also yet to score or assist in all competitions this term.

Walker was asked whether he thinks the forward has a future at his hometown club after struggling to make an impact.

The right-back said: "I'd like to think so. I think what he's done for the club, he needs to do a little more to be up in that legendary status of Man United. But he lives, breathes and loves the club dearly.

"He needs to do a little bit more, but he's got the potential to do it definitely."

"If his heart's not in it at Man United, he may as well finish football," Walker added, praising Rashford's passion for the Red Devils.

"And I can tell you now, I saw him a week ago and he's fully invested into the club."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick told to drop ‘disgrace’ Bruno Fernandes – ‘he’s killed the manager’
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes has shamed himself as Manchester United captain, Michael Carrick should drop him from the starting XI.

That's the assessment of Gabby Agbonlahor after United suffered an embarrassing 4-1 defeat to Como that has left them winless in seven matches across all competitions.

3 United were well-beaten by Como, and captain Fernandes took issue with their tactics during a post-match interview that puts more pressure on Carrick Credit: Getty

It took just two minutes for the two-time Champions League winners to fall behind as Como played them off the park, and perhaps left feeling as though they could have scored at least eight on the night.

Similar to Lisandro Martinez after the 2-0 loss to Atletico Madrid last week, United skipper Fernandes delivered an extraordinary rant and appeared to take aim at under-fire head coach Carrick over tactics.

Fernandes, who was substituted in the 67th minute, claimed it was a decision from the coaching staff to not press man-to-man and this allowed Como to play with confidence.

"That's on the manager and staff to see, not me," he responded when asked if he hinted at Carrick making a tactical error, but Agbonlahor was highly critical when analysing his words and performance.

Fernandes is a 'disgrace'

"Don't get me started on him, he's a disgrace," he told Alan Brazil on talkSPORT Breakfast and, when reacting to Fernandes' comments, he insisted: "He's absolutely killed the manager."

"I've been saying it for years, and Manchester United fans have been like, 'Oh, shut up. I'd rather you have passion, look at the goals he's scored'," he added.

"He's showing himself when the going's got tough now at Manchester United, how is he the captain of that football club? He was a disgrace last night.

"I was watching the game and I was player-camming Bruno Fernandes. He was giving the ball away, throwing his arms up at anyone else whenever anyone tried anything.

"(Youri) Tielemans tried a cross and, because he didn't pick out Fernandes, he's thrown his arms at him, he's pointing at him. He will be the player in that changing room that the players dislike.

"When he got dragged at 60 minutes, I was like, 'Fair play to you, Michael Carrick. If you're going to go down, you're going to get the sack, you're going to go down your way.

3 Agbonlahor cannot understand how Fernandes is the United captain and called him a disgrace what he did on and off the pitch at Como Credit: Getty

"'You're going to take Bruno Fernandes off because he's deserved that for weeks'. He did nothing.

"I was watching him, and I'm like, 'You're giving the ball away, and then you're taking it out on your teammates. What a horrible teammate you are'."

Carrick should drop Fernandes

talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook believes that the defeat to Como could well be his last as the permanent head coach at United, a role he took on just five months ago.

It's understood that Former Germany and Bayern Munich boss Julian Nagelsmann has been sounded out as a potential replacement, whilst Brighton head coach Fabian Hurzeler has admirers at old Trafford.

However, Agbonlahor believes Carrick is worthy of more time in the dugout and should be in charge for the Premier League clash against Bournemouth on Sunday.

In addition, he should leave Fernandes out of the starting XI despite his captain status.

3 If Carrick remains in the job this weekend, then Agbonlahor wants to see him drop Fernandes from the team Credit: Getty

Agbonlahor explained: "I wouldn't sack him now, I would wait to see a reaction against Bournemouth.

"Let Michael Carrick drop Bruno Fernandes for the Bournemouth game. Let him play his team, who he thinks are going to run for him, are going to work hard and put in a performance.

"If he doesn't get a result against Bournemouth, then I think the inevitable will happen, but I wouldn't sack him just yet."

Sports.title: Top five Ballon d’Or winners since 2000 with no Cristiano Ronaldo
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has tarnished his legacy - he doesn't belong on the list of the best five players to have won a Ballon d'Or this millennium.

That is the explosive verdict of talkSPORT's Max Scott, who admits recent events have seen him go off the five-time Golden Ball winner.

7 talkSPORT's Mount Rushmore looks at the most influential and iconic things in sport, with presenter Max Scott selecting five (four is just not enough) in each topic Credit: Alamy

CR7's international career with Portugal was thrust into doubt after he departed the Euro 2016 champions' training camp in September.

Portuguese journalist Pedro Sepulveda told talkSPORT that Ronaldo's anger stemmed from a belief that he had been lied to about his game time by his new national team boss, Jorge Jesus.

Jesus then doubled down on his stance regarding the Manchester United legend, who has even escalated events by having a personal dig at Simon Jordan.

In the end Ronaldo, 41, was given a 30-day suspension and fined 255 euros (£215) by his country's FA.

With the 2026 edition upon us and Harry Kane, Rodri and Lamine Yamal in the running, Max has looked at the list of the best Ballon d'Or winners since the year 2000 in his weekly series, Mount Rushmore or less, to pick the best.

Lionel Messi: Eight-time winner

As talkSPORT's Scott says: Let's get the obvious one out of the way.

Messi has won a record-breaking eight Ballon d'Ors, starting in 2009 and most recently after lifting the World Cup with Argentina in 2022.

"The greatest of all time - He did what Ronaldo could never do and win the World Cup," Scott told talkSPORT.com.

"And he's quite simply the greatest ever football player to grace a football pitch.

"And that hurts me particularly after what happened in the World Cup between England and Argentina," Scott continued on Messi.

"I've still got a bee in my bonnet about the behaviour of those Argentinian players and Messi's the captain, but you cannot deny that he is the best ever player.

"I think that he's the most complete footballer as well.

"There's something special about a player who seems to have been just born with it.

"Whereas CR7 clearly grafted to become one of the greatest ever players in the gym, early mornings, routine.

"I'm sure Lionel Messi worked incredibly hard, but there's a magic about him that puts him, not just at the top of my Mount Rushmore or less, of Ballon d'Or winners, but as the greatest ever player to play the beautiful game.

7 Messi is football's Ballon d'Or king with eight wins in his career to cement his place as the greatest ever player

Kaka: 2007 winner

Once upon a time, he was the cream of the crop and the last winner before Messi and Ronaldo's domination that lasted until 2018.

"One of the most phenomenal attacking midfielders I think that we've ever seen," Scott recalled.

"And people often look at Kaká and look at the end of his career, or look at what happened at Real Madrid.

"But prime AC Milan Kaká, who won the 06/07 Champions League and Ballon d'Or, by the way, beating Ronaldo and Messi, scored 20 goals, 14 assists in 51 games that season. He was unbelievable.

"And he wasn't just one of those sort of graceful Brazilian attacking midfielders that was in pockets.

"He could pick up the ball at the edge of his own box, drive forward 30, 40 meters, and make something magic happen.

"I just think he's one of the most underrated greats of the game - the way he played football, it was similar to Patrick Vieira in the Premier League: just the power, the strength, the skill, the technique, and the goals."

7 Kaka is one of six players to have won the Ballon d'Or at Milan Credit: AFP

Ronaldinho: 2005 winner

A man was so indestructible at his peak that even some of his former Barcelona teammates struggle to choose between him and Messi.

Scott said: "Now his Brazilian counterpart, one of the greatest ever, Pele, he made famous the phrase, the beautiful game - And I feel like Ronaldinho picked up that baton and carried it on.

"Not just his achievements on the pitch, as a Barcelona player, in El Clásico, he got a standing ovation from the Bernabeu for the two goals he scored in a 3-0 El Clásico win in 2007.

"That alone tells you that he sits in a different stratosphere of football players, a different otherworldly realm of Ballon d'Or winners that you can, as a Barcelona player, get a standing ovation from Real Madrid fans.

7 In his prime, Ronaldinho was one of the best players in world football Credit: Getty

"He was absolutely unbelievable, but it was not just what he achieved on the pitch, winning the World Cup, winning the Champions League.

"It's the fact that he transcended sport. I remember his Jogo bonito campaign with Nike with those beautiful Nike boots that he had, gold and white boots.

"And I still refuse to believe that him repeatedly kicking the ball against the crossbar was CGI, because he was just that special.

"His goals against Chelsea in the Champions League were unbelievable.

"And for me, as somebody that played the game with such ease and with a smile on his face, he's like a Last Bastion of a maverick, of a player that didn't need systems and tactics and over-management.

"He partied, he got the women, he gambled, but he's still an absolute legend. Ronaldinho, hats off to you, sir."

7 In 2005 Frank Lampard finished as runner-up to Ronaldinho for both the Ballon d'Or and FIFA World Player of the Year awards Credit: Getty

Luis Figo: 2000 winner

"From a man in Ronaldinho who was absolutely adored by Barcelona to a man who is despised by them for moving from them to Real Madrid Galacticos, it's Luis Figo.

"And he's another guy who I think has almost lost a little bit in the history of European greats because he played before the Ronaldo-Messi era. Luis Figo is one of the greatest wingers we've ever seen.

"Rapid, technical ability, shooting, finishing, dribbling, but he was also incredibly powerful. Moving to Real Madrid, he won it all.

"Absolutely class, still an incredibly important figure in world football. I just think, go and watch his highlights.

"Go and look at his achievements. He's won the Ballon d'Or and he won it for a reason.

"A little bit underrated, but that era of La Liga, Revista de la Liga on Sky Sports, when we used to be able to watch it all the time, he was absolutely unbelievable."

7 Figo won the 2000 Ballon d'Or to just about to sneak into selection for this list Credit: AFP

Why Ronaldo Nazario not Cristiano?

"I know Cristiano Ronaldo has won his fair share of Ballon d'Ors, but if I'm completely honest with you, I feel that the ways he's conducted himself, whether it's going to Saudi Arabia, whether it's dragging out his Portugal career and becoming an even greater ego, I've just gone off him.

"I'm not denying how great of a player he is, but I do think that he's tarnished his legacy, whereas Ronaldo hasn't.

"I know that his career ended with injury issues and issues with his sort of, with his weight and his physicality, but in his prime in 2002, when he won the Ballon d'Or, he'd won the World Cup. He got the golden boot at the World Cup with eight goals.

"He was the greatest, and still is, the greatest ever striker in modern times.

"I'm talking greater than Erling Haaland, and this hurts to say, greater than Thierry Henry, who for me is the greatest player we've seen in the Premier League.

7 Ronaldo is a World Cup legend with 15 goals in 19 games and two winner's medals Credit: Getty

"We're talking about a player who had absolutely everything: the perfect amalgamation of that Brazilian grace and skill and technique, and then the power and the pace and the finishing ability and the dribbling ability that made him one of the greatest in Europe.

"He did it everywhere: Barcelona, Inter Milan, Real Madrid, Wimbledon, World Cup, Champions League, La Liga, Serie A. Ronaldo Nazário, for me is an absolute icon of the game.

"That dome haircut, his famous seizure that he had before a World Cup final, how he came back then afterwards to win it in 2002, the story's absolutely amazing.

"And where is he now? He's back in Brazil, living the humble lifestyle, in complete contradiction to the crazy antics we see from Cristiano Ronaldo and how he seems to think he's got complete control over the Portuguese FA.

"I think the sooner that CR7 retires, the better it is for his legacy.

"But Ronaldo Nazário is the greatest striker we've ever seen in modern times, and he has to be up there on the Mount Rushmore, or less, of Ballon d'Or winners."

Sports.title: Bournemouth owner Bill Foley makes Champions League vow and gives Alex Scott transfer update
Sports.content:
Bournemouth owner Bill Foley wants to bring Champions League football to the south coast and is relishing the visit of Milan.

The Cherries host the Italian giants at the Vitality Stadium on Thursday in only their third ever European game.

4 Foley has been Bournemouth owner since December 2022 Credit: Getty

American billionaire Foley, who has bankrolled the Cherries rise into Europe, also says they can win the Europa League this season.

Speaking exclusively to talkSPORT ahead of arguably the biggest game in Bournemouth’s history, Foley said: "Little old tin pot Bournemouth playing AC Milan," he said making a light hearted reference to their recent history that saw them climb from -17 points in League Two in 2008 to hosting the seven time Champions League winners.

"It's an honour but I don't think it would be a surprise if we win. We deserve to win and I think we can go all the way.

“I don't want to make a prediction that we will because I end up getting in trouble when I started making predictions even though they usually come true.

“I like our team. I like what we've done so far in Europa in the Europa League.

“We have a big game on Thursday, and then if we can get to 15, 16 or 17 points we believe will avoid the knockout round and then anything can happen.

“My number one ambition is to win a major trophy winner major and number two to qualify for the Champions League.



“We have to do it consistently, by being numbers seven, six, five, four in the Premier League.

“That's the goal. I haven't changed my goals.”

What will happen with Alex Scott?

One of Foley’s biggest challenges will be keeping hold of star player Scott.

Bournemouth rejected a £64m offer from Chelsea for the 23-year-old in the summer and the Blues and Liverpool retain strong interest in the England international.

talkSPORT understands Scott has rejected a new contract making him Bournemouth’s highest paid player and Foley says Cherries players earning six-figure salaries should become ‘commonplace’.

4 talkSPORT understands Scott could leave in January if the right offer arrives, but Foley believes the south coast is the right place for him Credit: Getty

He added: “I think earning that kind of number should be commonplace, and we should be prepared to meet that challenge.

“At this point, we're convinced we're the right place for Alex to be and to stay, and we'll keep on addressing the contract issues with Alex as we move through this year.



“We'd love to have Alex stay here and sign a new contract and be part of this team for the long haul.

“We haven't given up, but sometimes players get stars in their eyes, and they think that Chelsea or Manchester City is the right place to go.



“We believe, if we keep on buying infrastructure and a common thread of leadership across the team then we will start keeping more and more players.

“People will be surprised about that, and they'll be able to earn substantial wages here.

“We have to respect the fact that a lot of our players are younger, and they've come to Bournemouth with the expectation that they'll get time to play and perhaps move on to a bigger team.

“We recognise that my job is to make players feel comfortable and provide them with the infrastructure they need to understand that.

4 Bournemouth host Milan, the seven time Champions League winners, at the Vitality on Thursday night in what is sure to be the biggest match in their history so far Credit: Getty

“We're serious about what we're doing. We're in a brand new performance centre and it is as state of the art as they come.

“We're happy with where we are and we believe we'll start making progress in terms of retaining key talent.

“It may not be this year, it may not be next year in terms of everyone, but we're close.

“We have to prove to the players this is a place they want to be and that they want to stay and they don't want to move on because that's the way we really build a successful team.”

Marco Rose progress

Finally, Foley praised new manager Marco Rose after the German picked up his first Premier League win at home to Sunderland on Sunday – two matches earlier than predecessor Andoni Iraola.



Foley said: “Andoni had nine games and won the ninth game against Burnley, so we're a little ahead of schedule compared to him.

“The changes Marco is making are not like the changes Andoni made in terms of completely restructuring our offense and our defensive plans.

4 Rose replaced Andoni Iraola at the Cherries this summer Credit: Getty

“I feel like we let a few games get away and we have to be more consistent with our shots.

“We have to execute a little bit better, but the team is a really good team, and they're playing like a team, which is the most important thing to me.

“Marco is a players’ coach. He's empathetic, but he's also very demanding.

“I'm happy where we are, and now we have to get ready for the next transfer window to see what we need and what we need to add to make sure we drive on.

“The team is ready; there's no question about it.”

Bournemouth vs Milan is live on talkSPORT from 8pm on Thursday 22 October

Sports.title: Harry Kane wanted transfer to Man City and mega move was very close
Sports.content:
Harry Kane wanted transfer to Man City and mega move was very close

It's one of the biggest what-ifs in Premier League history.

In the summer of 2021, Manchester City were seriously interested in Harry Kane, who was at Tottenham.

3 Kane scored 213 Premier League goals for Spurs Credit: Getty



There were also whispers Kane struck a gentleman's agreement with then-Spurs chairman Daniel Levy a year earlier that he'd have one more season in north London before being allowed to move elsewhere.

Ultimately a transfer never came to fruition, but just how close was Kane to calling the Etihad Stadium home?

Kyle Walker lifts lid on Harry Kane's failed move to Manchester City

According to Kyle Walker, who was on City's books at the time but played with Kane at Spurs, the superstar striker was 'very close' to moving.

"I think he was just at a point in his career where he wanted to go and win trophies," Walker said on talkSPORT Drive.



"That was the one cloud over his head. He's a great player and has got all these personal accolades for himself, but he'd never won anything for a club."

Walker added that at no stage did Kane tell him he was bound for City, but was keen on the switch.



"He said, 'I want to come,' and was asking me a little bit about it," Walker continued.

"But I'm guessing the clubs couldn't reach an agreement."

After the 2021 summer window shut, former City boss Pep Guardiola revealed City made four bids to sign Kane, only for Spurs to turn all of them down.



Harry Kane gets his move to Bayern

Kane would eventually get his move to a European giant, although not until August 2023 when he joined Bayern Munich for an initial £86.4million.

3 Walker was in constant contact with Kane throughout the transfer saga but it never came to fruition Credit: Getty

The 33-year-old has gone on to establish himself as arguably Europe's most elite striker having twice won the European Golden Shoe, an award given to the leading goalscorer from the top division of a European league.

Kane's brilliance also has him as a serious contender to win this year's Ballon d'Or, which would make him the first English player to take football's most coveted individual prize since Michael Owen in 2001.



The qualities that made Harry Kane into superstar

Walker admitted he did not predict Kane would go on to enjoy such a stratospheric rise in his career when the latter was breaking into the first team at Spurs.

"He was a little bit overweight," Walker said.

"He could finish, but he wasn't very mobile."

However, it was Kane's desire to extract every little droplet of talent he possessed that made him into the lethal striker he is today.

3 Kane has scored over 150 goals for Bayern in just four seasons Credit: Getty

"There's not one training session or one stone left unturned that he doesn't try and make himself a better player," Walker added.



"I think he's a great example to every young kid coming up.

"You might not be the best at the start, but if you've got a goal and an objective you want to get, you can get there."

Sports.title: Man United fans rage after spotting one of their players wearing full-length tights in mild temperatures on night they were thrashed 4-1 by Como
Sports.content:
Man United fans rage after spotting one of their players wearing full-length tights in mild temperatures on night they were thrashed 4-1 by Como

Manchester United fans took aim at Noussair Mazraoui's bizarre decision to wear black leggings during the team's chastening defeat in Como, with some claiming the full-back's attire encapsulates the club's woes.

The Moroccan was part of the Red Devils' back four that conceded four goals on Wednesday evening as they lost 4-1 at Como in the Champions League.

The manner of the defeat was the latest abject display from Michael Carrick's side - who are now winless in their last seven matches in all competitions, dating back to a 4-0 victory over Sabah on September 10.

And while United's fan base are in disarray at how their club's season is unfolding, many were also left perplexed by Mazraoui's accessory on the pitch.

The 28-year-old was pictured wearing black leggings during the match, despite temperatures in Como being just 14 degrees Celsius.

'Mazraoui wearing tights sums it all up games gone,' wrote one Manchester United fan on X.

Noussair Mazraoui wore leggings during Man United's 4-1 Champions League loss at Como

The defeat extended the Red Devils' winless run in all competitions to seven matches

Manchester United fans took to X to air their displeasure at Mazraoui's choice of accessory

'I knew we were getting hammered when I saw Mazraoui wearing tights,' commented another on the social-media platform.

Another user wrote: 'Mazraoui is still hopping around on one leg in the away changing room of an empty stadium trying to get them tights off.'

One United fan made a light-hearted reference to Lisandro Martinez's public criticisms last week, while discussing Mazraoui.

'Mick Carrick's biggest tactical errors tonight were not putting Lisandro on media duties and allowing Mazraoui to wear leggings. Everything else is just noise.'

It's been a difficult week for Mazraoui who was also scrutinised by many for Leeds' equaliser during their 1-1 draw on Sunday when he gave away a corner cheaply which led to Dominic Calvert-Lewin's goal.

He and United will look to end their winless run on Sunday afternoon when they host Bournemouth in the Premier League.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick and Bruno Fernandes drive home at 12.30am as Man United's captain is called an 'absolute disgrace' - but boss faces the sack, says Jamie Carragher
Sports.content:
Manchester United's forlorn players and staff returned back to Manchester and drove home in the rain in the early hours of Thursday morning as the latest storm builds momentum at the club. The Red Devils were thrashed 4-1 at Como in the Champions League on Wednesday evening - in what will be the latter's greatest-ever European display. It proved a night to forget for United too as their winless run in all competitions now stretches to seven games - with their last win a 4-0 victory over Sabah on September 10. Michael Carrick and Bruno Fernandes were both pictured driving away from Manchester airport at around 12.30am with the head coach and captain at the heart of the latest difference of public opinion. Goalkeeper Senne Lammens and midfielder Mason Mount, who both started in Italy too, were also pictured driving to their homes in the damp conditions. A week after Lisandro Martinez's damning comments about the club's hierarchy, Fernandes' remarks have sharpened the focus on Carrick's tenure after he questioned his tactics in Como post-match, in particular their lack of a man-to-man press. Under-fire Michael Carrick was pictured driving home from Manchester Airport in the early hours of Thursday following their humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como Bruno Fernandes' comments about Carrick's tactics post-match have heaped pressure on the head coach and also seen the United captain come under-fire for making his views so public Reacting to Fernandes' comments, CBS Sports pundit Jamie Carragher was in shock at what he heard - brandiing 'awful attitude' Fernandes a 'disgrace' and declaring his actions as 'not what a Manchester United captain should be'. 'We said Lisandro Martínez was bang out of order last week for calling out the hierarchy above him. For Bruno Fernandes to do that is a disgrace really,' Carragher said. 'When you think about last season, he got player of the year. That was on the back of Michael Carrick becoming the manager. He wouldn't have got that award without Michael Carrick, because Michael Carrick put him back in his rightful position and he then went on to have a fantastic season because he's a talented footballer. But when you think of him as a footballer, he's a talent, but in terms of attitude and the way he goes about things, it's not right at all. 'And he's reacted like that because he's been brought off and he's been embarrassed tonight by the manager as he brought him off. And when he talks about pressing, whether it's man to man or zonal, for years, Bruno Fernandes has meant Manchester United can't press because he does things for the crowd. 'I commentate on games watching Man United and he runs all over the place like a kid in the schoolyard for the supporters. They all think he's working hard - he's not. He's killing the rest of the team doing it. 'Years ago, there was a captain called Bryan Robson, one of the greatest players to ever play for Man United because he played for the club, he didn't throw the manager or the players under the bus. 'He kept fighting for Manchester United and watching him throw his arms up every week in a game is an absolute disgrace, calling the manager out considering how he's performed this season on the pitch. 'Awful attitude and not what a Manchester United captain should be.' "For Bruno Fernandes, it's a disgrace, really." 😳@Carra23 doesn't hold back on the Manchester United captain after Bruno questioned Michael Carrick's tactics following their defeat to Como 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/7KpJR3RT9O — CBS Sports Golazo ⚽️ (@CBSSportsGolazo) October 21, 2026 CBS Sports pundit Jamie Carragher labelled Fernandes as a 'disgrace' for his comments United captain Fernandes bemoaned their lack of pressing tactics during their defeat at Como CESC FABREGAS TOLD HIS COMO PLAYERS TO STOP RUNNING AT 4-0 Cesc Fabregas revealed that he told his players to ease off Manchester United during their Champions League humiliation at the hands of Como in Italy on Wednesday night. Como were four goals up against Michael Carrick's side when Fabregas ordered his players to conserve energy ahead of Saturday's Serie A clash with Sassuolo. United scored a late consolation goal through substitute Joshua Zirkzee, and Fabregas admitted that he was angry at himself for not heaping further embarrassment on his opponents. 'I regret the last 10 minutes because I was the one who told the team to slow down the tempo because there's another match and at 4-0 we could manage things a little,' said the former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder. 'I told the players to stop running and stay in the middle and that is something I regret because I'm the first to always push them to fight until the end. Their goal hurt me because we dropped our intensity and dropped our defensive block, but it was my fault. 'I'm very happy with how the players applied everything we tried to do, not only in terms of quality, which was high, but also the way we were pressing relentlessly until the 85th minute. 'We are trying to create a culture at the club, a style of play and an identity. Tonight was another convincing moment for us.' Como celebrated the greatest result in the club's history, seven years after they were playing in the fourth tier of Italian football. 'I can't lie to you that it (beating United) wasn't pride,' added Fabregas. 'We know the history of our club, how much they have suffered over the last many years. Obviously, I hope that tomorrow all the boys and girls go to school wearing the Como shirt and feel proud. 'I always tell the lads, enjoy yourselves, fight, do everything to make the best career possible for each one of you, because it goes by quickly. 'They made me enjoy myself tonight, but not so much for the win, for the result, because they played like I like my team to play, with conviction, with quality, with a clear head, with aggressiveness, with a fierce pressing.' Como's star man was Nico Paz who tormented United with two goals and an assist to hand the Premier League club their heaviest defeat in Europe since losing 4-0 to Barcelona in 1994. 'It has been one of the most beautiful nights of my career,' said Paz. 'I'm still young, but I will never forget it. I used to dream of playing in a match like this, and tonight we've gone even further. It's a historic night for Como fans.' Chris Wheeler in Como Carragher's disdain for Fernandes' actions didn't stop there as he continued, before conceding that Carrick's days the United hotseat are very much numbered. 'Isn't it funny? How many managers has he had, Bruno Fernandes? So every single manager at Manchester United doesn't have an identity? How many managers are we on now for Bruno Fernandes? Five? They change the manager every season... Manchester United is rotten from top to bottom. 'I said earlier on, it's not about the manager. It's everything about the club. And who has got the answers? We comment on it all the time, "they might need to change the manager or do this, do that". Are we ever right really? Because no one ever seems to get it right. But listen, there's no doubt the manager needs to be changed now. Right now this can't go on for a club of the stature of Manchester United. 'But I'm glad Michael Carrick come out and just said that about Bruno Fernandes, that he don't run, because they don't run, this team. 'And what he did last season, no one's proclaiming Michael Carrick as one of the greatest managers in European football, but what he did was he come and helped his own football club last year when he was out of work himself. He's come in and he did amazing. 'And the reason Manchester United are in the Champions League is because of Carrick - he got them in there. The reason they got another 100, 150 million pounds into the club is because he got them in. No one though he was going to get into the Champions League last season. So I feel for him a little bit. He loves the club, he's a legendary figure as a player, but obviously it's not working out for him as a manager and that needs to be changed. 'But I'm delighted he brought him off, Fernandes, and I'm delighted that he had a little pop back there in the press because that's what they need some of those players.' Speaking after losing to Como, Fernandes broke ranks to question why United were so passive again. He said: 'It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence.' Asked if he meant that Carrick got his tactics wrong, Fernandes added: 'That's on the manager and staff to say, not me. 'Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable. As you saw with Como, the centre back was coming to mark me in my own half. We need to do that as a team but we were unable to. 'A team that plays through the middle with small connections, if you give them too much time and space then they can hurt you out wide.' Having conceded to Atletico after 50 seconds last week, United were behind within two minutes as Como star Nico Paz struck the first of his two goals. 'It's not the first time, we started on the wrong foot, and they scored very early,' said Fernandes. 'Not much pressure on the ball, not many good movements with the ball, not many things going our way. 'Conceding early makes us go into game with a mood of defeat, it's difficult to get out of that, trying to be brave, to have the ball and make something happen. If we are not able to do that, it is going to be very difficult to get out of this situation.' Fernandes was substituted in the second half and looked frustrated as he left the pitch Fernandes was surprisingly substituted by Carrick midway through the second half, and the United skipper shook his head in frustration as he made his way back to the dugout. When Carrick was told about Fernandes' comments, the United boss gave a pointed response by suggesting that his players weren't willing to run enough. 'We actually were half-pressed man-to-man in the second half and then conceded a goal from that,' he said. 'There's a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, but if you don't run - you don't run forward and you don't run back - you aren't going to win.' United will look to end their winless run on Sunday afternoon when they host Bournemouth in the Premier League. Sports.title: Man United's five-man shortlist to replace Michael Carrick revealed: Fabian Hurzeler admired but Brighton compensation obstacle looms, while Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are in the race for Old Trafford hotseat
Sports.content:
Man United's five-man shortlist to replace Michael Carrick revealed: Fabian Hurzeler admired but Brighton compensation obstacle looms, while Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are in the race for Old Trafford hotseat

Three days after Michael Carrick sat at Elland Road and talked about a fresh start, this felt like the end.

He left the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium looking beaten and rather bewildered after Manchester United hit a new low in Lombardy.

Losing 4-1 to Como was more than a defeat. It felt like a surrender. How apt that United played in white. Noussair Mazraoui played in tights, for goodness sake.

So here we go again. How much longer can Carrick last? Hours? Days? Beyond the international break? United have never sacked two managers in the same calendar year, but this cannot go on.

It has been a desperate season and the manner of United's capitulation in Italy was so dramatic, so shocking, that you wonder if the United hierarchy have a contingency plan in place for something like this.

They are not known for their forward-thinking and the Carrick crisis has engulfed them faster than they could ever have imagined, five months after they handed him a two-year contract in May.

Pressure is mounting Man United Michael Carrick head coach after a string of bad results

Brighton's Fabian Hurzeler has admirers as Old Trafford but any arrival wouldn't come cheap

Julian Nagelsmann has been out of a job since Germany's shock World Cup last-32 exit

Still, it would be negligent if they hadn't at least discussed possible replacements as the feelgood factor of qualifying for the Champions League has given way to utter despair amid the worst start to a league season in 40 years and the heaviest European defeat since 1994.

There are some intriguing possibilities. Brighton's Fabian Hurzeler is known to have admirers at Old Trafford, but it will not be cheap to extract the German from the Amex Stadium after he signed a new contract in June.

It cost Chelsea £20m in compensation for Graham Potter and his coaching staff in 2022. United are £1billion in debt and cannot keep paying out compensation to change managers.

Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte are both available, as well as two young British options in Eddie Howe and Kieran McKenna.

Perhaps the bigger question now, is who would want the job? United are a club locked in a death spiral, a recurring nightmare, that won't be ended by replacing one man. It has become a coach's graveyard since Sir Alex Ferguson retired.

They all find a different way to go in the end. David Moyes insisted that he had the backing of the board until the moment he realised he didn't.

Louis van Gaal left Wembley clutching the FA Cup as if he would gladly have beaten his employers over the head with it after waking up to the fact it was his last match in charge.

Jose Mourinho's demise was 'death by a thousand cuts' according to former United chief Ed Woodward, but leaving Paul Pogba on the bench at Anfield felt like a final act of self-sabotage.

Eddie Howe is out of a job after leaving Premier League rivals Newcastle United in pre-season

BOOKIES' NEXT MAN UNITED BOSS ODDS Eddie Howe -7/4 Julian Nagelsmann - 4/1 Antonio Conte - 6/1 Fabian Hurzeler - 6/1 Cesc Fabregas - 11/1 Thomas Tuchel - 14/1 Kieran McKenna - 14/1 Unai Emery - 14/1 Gareth Southgate - 16/1 Mauricio Pochettino - 25/1 Carlo Ancelotti - 25/1 Ole Gunnar Solskjaer - 25/1 Odds provided by Betfair as of 9.45am on Thursday, October 22

Like Carrick, Solskjaer's mea culpa and apologetic farewell to fans at Watford was a clear sign that the Norwegian knew he was toast. Erik ten Hag remained deluded to the last, even though Ineos had gone behind his back months earlier, and Ruben Amorim cut his own throat by taking them on in public.

Now Carrick's reign appears to be in its death throes, dragged down by performances that are an insult to this great club and increasingly loud dissent from the dressing-room.

The spotlight is back on Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers again now. On chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox. Do they act now or allow Carrick to stagger on in the belief that he can yet turn this around?

The hundreds of fans who had stood in the rain for hours in Como and left the ground long before Carrick walked over to apologise at the end have had their say. Now it's up to United.
