Sports.title: It is Michael Carrick's turn to go now, but who will be stupid enough to follow him? The top job at rotting Man United is a red cyanide pill at a club where nobody takes responsibility, writes IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
It is Michael Carrick's turn to go now, but who will be stupid enough to follow him? The top job at rotting Man United is a red cyanide pill at a club where nobody takes responsibility, writes IAN LADYMAN

So the Manchester United job has ruined Michael Carrick just like it ruined Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.

Carrick's sad, Mea culpa walk across the turf towards his club's supporters at Como's Stadio Guiseppe Sinigaglia last night bore a dismal resemblance to that made by one of his many predecessors at Vicarage Road, Watford, almost five years ago.

Solskjaer was to say goodbye to United in tears a couple of days later, a coach broken by a club so dysfunctional and a playing squad so riddled with rot that it had become impossible to manage.

And now it is Carrick's turn. Another good man on the way, another servant of the club to feel that miserable cocktail of regret, failure and resignation. Another football man with United in his veins who must look around and wonder what on earth a once great club has become.

The question now is who will be stupid enough to put their hand up to follow Carrick into a post he will surely be invited to leave before too long.

The job at Old Trafford used to be one of English football's most coveted postings. Now it merely represents a fast track to pain, suffering and failure.

Michael Carrick will surely be invited to leave the Manchester United job shortly

Only a football junkie looking for a cheap fix of glamour and status would take it. It still gives you that. Managing United will still provide a man with that quick jolt of adrenaline.

But the reality is that it is a cyanide pill coloured red. Nobody since Sir Alex Ferguson's day gets out alive. That's the reality of working at a place where if the lack of football smarts above you don't get you then the lack of heart in the dressing room surely will.

The thing about United is that the expectation will always be the same. Despite its reduced circumstances, no club expects you to win so regularly and monotonously as this one does.

The modern United is not set up to succeed. The squad is not good enough, the ownership continues to milk its revenues from within and its executive structure makes bad decisions.

Still, though, their managers are expected to win and to compete with proper, well-run football clubs like Arsenal at the top of the Premier League. It's impossible. The road back to the top of the English and European game is longer than it has ever been for a United manager but that's the remit nevertheless.

Carrick should never have been given the job last summer. The red flag comparisons with Solskjaer were so numerous, it was terrifying. But whoever succeeds him is a fool to think success can come quickly to this club in its current form.

It's a place that pays footballers who don't want to run and who talk a better game than they play. A place where even the rehabilitation of a captain like Bruno Fernandes has now been derailed by an environment where not a single person in the building bar the manager seems willing to take responsibility for failure.

To listen to Bruno Fernandes talk after last night's dismantling by Como in Italy was to be granted a snapshot of United's rotting soul. Back in the day when United did things properly on and off the field, Fernandes would have spent the following few days juggling footballs on his own in the car park. On Saturday, when United face Bournemouth, he will doubtless lead the team out wearing the captain's armband.

Eddie Howe would be a fool to go anywhere near Old Trafford in the current climate

The Premier League's latest young tyro Fabian Hurzeler of Brighton should avoid United

In terms of their future, United are known to have feelers out for replacement candidates. The former German national team and Bayern Munich coach Julian Nagelsmann is thought to be near the top of a provisional list. Antonio Conte – once of Tottenham and Chelsea – would like to be on it.

Both will back themselves to be the man to work the miracle simply because managers always do. It's the way they are made. The job would play to Conte's ego and he would come with nothing to lose. He would also fail, and do so quickly, but it hasn't stopped United making bad appointments before.

But as for men like Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe and the Premier League's latest young tyro Fabian Hurzeler of Brighton, they would be fools to go anywhere near Old Trafford.

Howe may be a future England coach. Why jeopardise your chances? Hurzeler is a former Bayern Munich B team player. They, along with the rest of the Bundesliga, will be watching the 33-year-old. Why risk a reputation on a basket case club? All three are coaches whose next posting will determine their career trajectory. They need to go somewhere that provides them with a platform to develop, grow and succeed. They need foundations. United presents only a trapdoor without a latch.

In the 13 and a half years since Sir Alex Ferguson left, seven have walked through the door thinking they had reached the top of the mountain. Seven have crawled out again on their knees.

This is what United does to people these days. There are some with Carrick's best interests at heart who feared for him when he took the job. They had seen the evidence and followed the trends.

Bruno Fernandes captains a club where not a single person bar the manager seems willing to take responsibility for failure

What will come of him is painful to consider. Once he has done the rounds of the podcasts and told his stories of an environment where self-harm has become a culture, he will look down at his feet and see a career in management lying in ruins.

He is not alone in that. Others, meanwhile, count their blessings of a lucky escape.

The England manager Thomas Tuchel, for example, spoke to United more than once when they looked to replace Erik ten Hag in the summer of 2024. He ultimately withdrew from the process.

United failed the sniff test. He didn't like the rather unpredictable nature of what he saw. And this from a bloke who once worked at Chelsea.

Sports.title: Como 4-1 Man United PLAYER RATINGS: Which stars fare worst in our most damning ratings EVER after Michael Carrick's side sink to new low?
Sports.content:
Things went from bad to worse at Manchester United as their 'fresh start' under Michael Carrick began with a disastrous 4-1 drubbing at the hands of Como.

In the pouring rain, United capitulated under the pressure put on by Cesc Fabregas' young guns and they were behind inside two minutes in what was the start of a very long evening.

Anastasios Douvikas got himself on the scoresheet, teed up by man of the match Nico Paz, who scored twice, before Jacobo Ramon compounded United's misery with a fourth.

By the time Joshua Zirkzee held his run to stay onside to score a consolation in stoppage time, there was barely a flicker of a smile on the faces of anyone wearing United white.

At that stage, United's wounded supporters had long left in their droves, furious at a performance that suggests this United group are only heading in one direction: backwards.

Daily Mail Sport's NATHAN SALT gives his verdict on a truly hapless Manchester United performance in Italy...

Manchester United have a lot of soul searching to do after a shambolic defeat to Como

Nico Paz ran United ragged with a brace and an assist as United's season gets even worse

Manchester United (4-2-3-1)

Senne Lammens – 4

What is he meant to do when those in front of him are so hopeless? The defence was about as solid as a house of cards in a gentle breeze. Genuinely hopeless and as long as that continues, Lammens is on a hiding to nothing.

Diogo Dalot – 3

Wasted a golden opportunity after a deflection fell at his feet in the box, shooting a whisker wide of the post. That proved costly when Como scored less than a minute later. Works hard and was willing at right back, where he started, and left back, where he went at half time. Some at United feel Dalot is unfairly criticised when the chips are down, but he was miles away from the required quality here.

Matthijs de Ligt – 3

His first United appearance in 325 days and there was so much hope that the Dutchman could pick up where he left off. The positive is that he came through it unscathed. By the time he went off, it was a disastrous night for United and De Ligt was far from blameless after losing sight of Douvikas before stumbling as Como made it 2-0.

Harry Maguire – 4

Made a super last-ditch, sliding challenge to deny a second goal but it all proved in vain. Maguire called out the team for not showing enough bravery away to Leeds and this as a response was disastrous.

He was the best of the back-line but that's not saying much. Looks one of very few who can actually handle the pressure and navigate the storm now.

Harry Maguire called out the bravery of this team after Leeds and it didn't have any impact

Noussair Mazraoui – 3

Ran ragged at both left back, where he started, and at right back, where he played in the second half. It was Mazraoui who was at fault for Leeds' equaliser at the weekend and his press to close out in the lead up to Como's second goal was dreadful. Looked like a rabbit in headlights by the time Kaiki, gifted the freedom of Como by Mazraoui, crossed in for the hosts' fourth.

Mason Mount – 3

Has won this competition and has plenty of experience at the level but looked way short of the necessary quality required as this youthful Como team made him look distinctly average. Constantly came out second best in duels.

Andrey Santos – 4

Found himself completely overrun in the middle of the park – he wasn't alone in that – and was hooked at half-time after a rash slide to bring down Nico Paz brought a yellow card. Never got close to the speed of the game. The fact it was only 1-0 when he went off goes in his favour.

Bryan Mbeumo – 4

Has looked best at centre forward and so, naturally, he was deployed wide off the right, a position he doesn't ever seem to thrive in. Made a couple of smart runs but chances were at a premium and he was marginalised.

Bryan Mbeumo was pushed out on to the right and it massively limited what he is good at

Youri Tielemans – 4

Keeps starting matches but this one was one where it was easy to forget he was playing. Totally anonymous.

Matheus Cunha – 3

Another who was totally anonymous. Had one touch in the Como box, didn't create a single chance, and had just one shot off target before he was hooked at half-time alongside Santos. Been in and out of the side of late and this didn't do anything to improve his odds of more starts.

Bruno Fernandes – 4

Shook his head as he was taken off just after an hour into this one-sided contest but the truth is his performances have been way below the levels he has previously shown he can reach and he could have few complaints at coming off.

This false-nine experiment they have used in the past two games isn't yielding successful results.

MANAGER: Michael Carrick – 2

Spoke about a 'fresh start' after the draw at Leeds and then saw his side get totally dominated by a quicker, hungrier and better coached team. This was alarming mostly because United never looked remotely threatening, never mind threatening to pull off a positive result.

Michael Carrick is going to be under enormous pressure now as he bids to keep his job

SUBS

Amad (for Matheus Cunha, 46min) – 6

The brightest player in a United shirt. Looked to actually make stuff happen, and it was his ball in to Zirkzee that led to the late consolation.

Carlos Baleba (for Andrey Santos, 46) – 5

Catastrophic error to concede possession to Nico Paz as he broke to score a third. Did at least add some physicality that is severely lacking in this team. United cannot start matches going forward without him.

Joshua Zirkzee (for Bruno Fernandes, 67)

Scored in what was basically the only positive on a sobering night. Ended his drought.

Harry Amass (for Matthijs de Ligt, 79)

Shea Lacey (for Bryan Mbeumo, 86)

Como (4-2-3-1)

Butez 6; Couto 7, Ramon 7, Kempf 6, Valle 6; Milla 7, Perrone 8; Da Cunha 7, Paz 9 (Ricci 80), Baturina 7 (Caqueret 64, 7); Douvikas 8

Goals: Paz (2, 57), Douvikas (49), Ramon (76)

Manager: Cesc Fabregas 8

NOW READ: Man United were insipid, lifeless and downright ugly in tame Como surrender, writes CHRIS WHEELER

Sports.title: Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal PLAYER RATINGS: Which stars left the Gunners defence exposed too often? Who pulled the strings for Mikel Arteta's men? And who had a 'quiet' night?
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal PLAYER RATINGS: Which stars left the Gunners defence exposed too often? Who pulled the strings for Mikel Arteta's men? And who had a 'quiet' night?

Declan Rice stole the limelight from Harry Kane as Arsenal hit back to snatch a thrilling 2-2 draw against Bayern Munich in a heavyweight Champions League clash at the Allianz Arena.

Gunners midfielder Rice lashed low beyond Bayern goalkeeper Manuel Neuer eight minutes from time to extend his side’s unbeaten start to this season’s competition following back-to-back wins over Napoli and Lille.

Kane was on course to claim the winner after registering his 16th goal in 23 career outings against Arsenal by converting a 61st-minute penalty following Jurrien Timber’s handball.

The England captain earlier produced a sublime assist for Alphonso Davies to cancel out Eberechi Eze’s opener.

But in their biggest test since losing last season’s final to Paris St Germain on penalties, Mikel Arteta’s Premier League champions responded well to deservedly return home with a share of the spoils.

Here ISAAN KHAN rates Arsenal's top performers on the night.

David Raya - 7

Top save to deny Dayot Upamecano from point-blank range. Impressive with his fast distribution to kickstart counter-attacks.

Jurrien Timber - 4

Out of position for Alphonso Davies’ goal and caught out throughout the match. Conceded a penalty for a handball following Harry Kane's strike.

Jurrien Timber endured a difficult night and was caught out of position for Bayern's opener

Ezri Konsa - 5

Tasked with keeping tabs on Kane, yet the England man found ways to find space. A couple of strong, important blocks, but his positioning ought to be better.

Gabriel - 6

Strong at the back and up for the fight. Stepped up when required, not deterred by the task at hand.

Riccardo Calafiori - 5

A constant threat in the final third but, like his fellow full back Timber, he left the backline exposed too often.

Martin Odegaard - 8

Pulled the strings for Arteta's side and played some classy passes, including a sublime assist for Eberechi Eze. The Norwegian is hard to stop when he’s in this mood.

Martin Odegaard delivered another impressive display as the Arsenal captain rediscovers his best form

Declan Rice - 8

Energetic in the middle of the park and covered lots of ground. His corner-kicks caused havoc in the Bayern area and struck a well-taken goal.

Bruno Guimaraes - 6

All-action display. Put in a number of crucial challenges and was a threat going forwards. Had a header well-saved by Manuel Neuer.

Bukayo Saka - 5

Pulled up with what looked like a quad injury in the opening 10 minutes, signalling to the bench that he would not be able to continue. Massive blow for Arsenal, who will be sweating over the severity of Saka's blow.

Kai Havertz - 4

A quiet night with the German unable to create openings in threatening areas.

It was a quiet night for Kai Havertz, who struggled to make an impact

Noni Madueke - 5

Direct and tried to make things happen. Thoese opportunities dwindled in the second-half as Bayern grabbed control of the tie.

Substitutions:

Eberechi Eze - 7

Deserves credit after an impressive, goalscoring cameo following recent scrutiny.

Viktor Gyokeres - 7

Myles Lewis-Skelly - 6

Manager: Mikel Arteta - 7

A good move to bring on Viktor Gyokeres, who came off the bench to assist Rice. Will be pleased to walk away with a point.

Boss Mikel Arteta will be pleased with his side's performance and the point gained in Germany

BAYERN MUNICH (4-2-3-1): Neuer 7; Laimer 6, Upamecano 7, Min-Jae 6 (Tah 6, 46mins), Stanisic 6; Pavlovic 6, Bischof 6; Gnabry 6 (Karl 68, 6), Saibari 6 (Diaz 6, 68), Davies 8; Kane 8.

Referee: Davide Massa - 6

Sports.title: Chelsea set to move for £90m-rated Alex Scott in January, as Bournemouth owner Bill Foley says 'sometimes players get stars in their eyes' and refuses to give up on keeping him
Sports.content:
Chelsea set to move for £90m-rated Alex Scott in January, as Bournemouth owner Bill Foley says 'sometimes players get stars in their eyes' and refuses to give up on keeping him

Bournemouth owner Bill Foley insists they have 'not given up' trying to convince Alex Scott to sign a new contract with them and snub his interest from Chelsea.

Per sources, Chelsea made at least three offers for the 23-year-old midfielder in the summer with their highest bid worth £68million. Bournemouth insisted throughout the last window that he was not for sale, and it is now known they value him north of £100m ahead of January.

Foley spoke openly about Scott's situation when asked. The 81-year-old American even name-checked his Stamford Bridge counterparts when conceding 'sometimes players get stars in their eyes and they think Chelsea is the right place to go'.

However, Foley believes Bournemouth are close to being in a place where they no longer have to sell their star men, and he is still trying to have Scott stay with them.

'I don't want to sell anyone at any time anywhere,' Foley said, in an interview with talkSPORT teeing up Bournemouth's Europa League home clash with AC Milan.

'Now I have to defer to Tiago (Pinto), my president of football, and he really comes to me with his ideas and his plans. At this point, we're convinced we're the right place for Alex to be, for Alex to stay. We'll keep on addressing contract issues with Alex as we move through this year.

Bournemouth value Alex Scott north of £100m in January - with Chelsea showing interest

'We'd love to have Alex stay here and sign a new contract and be a part of this team for the long haul and we're still working on it. We haven't given up.

'But sometimes, players get stars in their eyes and they think Chelsea is the right place to go, or Man City. We hated to lose (Antoine) Semenyo. What a great guy he was. But to show you his character, he didn't have to play those last two games with us. He stayed, and he played, and he scored a winning goal in the very last game.'

Scott's current contract with Bournemouth runs until 2028 and he has so far resisted signing a new deal despite the efforts of those inside the Vitality Stadium. He is currently sidelined by a quad problem picked up while representing England in the last international break.

Chelsea sources claim they have not been back for Scott since the summer despite speculation of ongoing talks over a price, but their interest in him remains, and they are expected to move for him in January. Despite Bournemouth insisting they want £100m-plus, it could take an offer worth around £90m to sign him this winter.

Foley also discussed how Bournemouth believe they are close to becoming a club that does not need to sell big names such as Scott or Semenyo, who joined City for around £65m.

'We're close,' Foley said. 'We have to respect the fact that a lot of our players are younger, they've come to Bournemouth on the expectation that they'll get time to play and perhaps move on to a bigger team and we recognise that. We're happy with where we are, and we believe we'll start making progress in terms of retaining key talent.

'It may not be this year, it may not be next year in terms of everyone, but we're close. We have to prove to the players that this is the place they want to be, and that they want to stay, and don't want to move on.'

Sports.title: How Bournemouth became favourites to beat AC Milan: From copying the Italians' famous kit to just £100,000 saving them from extinction... now the Cherries are ready to beat their idols
Sports.content:
How Bournemouth became favourites to beat AC Milan: From copying the Italians' famous kit to just £100,000 saving them from extinction... now the Cherries are ready to beat their idols

Another club might have ditched the self-deprecation by now, but Bournemouth are a conscious bunch. They know the depths from which they rose to reach this European stage and so their social media manager could not resist adding a note when advertising their next home fixture.

‘AC Milan (H)… still feels a bit mad typing that,’ the admin tweeted. While Bournemouth are now an accomplished Premier League club, they recognise their history and respect that this is a Europa League fixture at the Vitality Stadium which will carry no shortage of nods.

There is the nod to Milan themselves with Bournemouth’s red-and-black striped kit adopted in 1971. That rebrand was inspired by the Italian giants’ swashbuckling greatness, while they also added ‘AFC’ to the beginning of their name to ensure they would appear first in alphabetical lists.

There is the nod to how as recently as 2008, they were starting their season in League Two with a 17-point deduction. Bournemouth’s supporters unveiled an enormous banner before their last Europa League home game against Sturm Graz which read ‘Minus 17 to European dreams’ as the DJ pressed play on Andy Williams’s The Impossible Dream. We can expect to see more references to where they came from before this marquee showdown with Milan, a club that have seven European Cup/Champions League trophies in their cabinet.

But the biggest nod is the literal one provided by Jeff Mostyn while standing at the back of a room. As detailed by Mostyn, who wrote a memoir called The Chairman: The Man Who Saved AFC Bournemouth, he led the takeover of the club in 2007 at a time when the club was flirting with ceasing to exist.

Bournemouth’s red-and-black striped kit, adopted in 1971, was inspired by the Italian giants’ swashbuckling greatness

AC Milan (H).



Still feels a bit mad typing that. pic.twitter.com/dWjhcKidCa — AFC Bournemouth 🍒 (@afcbournemouth) October 21, 2026

Mostyn’s lawyers did their due diligence at the time, and, in his own words, advised him to get back in the car and drive as fast as he could out of Bournemouth.

Yet Mostyn saw a club in need. There was a famous moment when administrator Gerald Krasner conducted a press conference. He had warned Mostyn beforehand that at some stage, he would ask him the question whether he would fund the additional £100,000 required to save Bournemouth from liquidation. It would then be over to him to either nod, or shake his head. The room turned to Mostyn, who nodded, his heart ruling his head in that moment.

Were it not for Mostyn and that nod, Bournemouth would not be where they are today, as a Premier League club about to face Milan in a European fixture.

It is a clash worth celebrating because of that. It allows those supporters of sides lower down the pyramid to dream themselves. Yet once Marco Rose's players are on the pitch, Bournemouth should not see this as a ceremonial clash.

They have snapped out of their Premier League slumber, finally securing their first win under Rose by beating Sunderland on Sunday. Milan are unbeaten in Serie A, and managed by Ruben Amorim, formerly of Manchester United, but the bookmakers have Bournemouth as favourites to win amid all the romanticism. And then they visit a troubled United on Sunday.

They are perfectly capable of competing, and winning. Bournemouth already carry a perfect record in the Europa League, having won away at Real Sociedad and at home against Sturm Graz. Adam Smith, who first joined the club on loan in 2010 when they were in League One, set up Evanilson for their opener in that latter victory.

Fifteen years ago on this night, Bournemouth were still toiling in football's third tier, losing at home to Bury. That was during a six-game winless streak which included being beaten by Hartlepool, and drawing with Tranmere, Rochdale, MK Dons and Colchester.

Bournemouth’s mayor, Roberto Rocca, was not living here then. He moved to the town 13 years ago as a Milan-born Italian. Yet he is now backing his local club.

‘Milan by birth, Bournemouth by choice,’ Rocca said, and there is every chance that he will have bragging rights over his Milan-supporting family members come full-time. They have endured the dark days, but this will be up there with Bournemouth’s best ones.

Sports.title: Meet the double Winter Olympic champion in BBC SPOTY battle with Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham
Sports.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Meet the double Winter Olympic champion in BBC SPOTY battle with Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham

Team GB hero Matt Weston has opened up about his journey from almost quitting sport to finding himself a front runner for BBC Sports Personality of the Year after winning two gold medals at the Winter Olympics

View 5 Images Winter Olympics star Matt Weston is eyeing up the Sports Personality of the Year (Image: Getty Images)

Matt Weston has admitted it would be "insane" if he became the first Winter Olympian in more than 40 years to win the BBC Sports Personality of the Year.

‌



‌



Weston, 29, is the fourth favourite with the bookmakers to pick up the SPOTY prize after winning two gold medals at the 2026 Milano Cortina Games back in February.

‌



The Surrey-born superstar won both the individual and mixed team skeleton events, becoming only the second Team GB athlete to secure two Winter Olympic gold medals, after Lizzy Yarnold.

‌



He set four course records as he raced to his individual victory, finishing 0.88 seconds ahead of Germany's Axel Jungk. Realising his Olympic dream was an emotional and unforgettable moment, but there was more to come.

Just two days later, Weston celebrated alongside Tabitha Stoecker after clinching mixed team gold in thrilling fashion, running a final time of 1:59:36, 0.17 seconds ahead of Germany's Susanne Kreher and Jungk, and setting a new track record in the process.

It wrapped up a historic and record-breaking Winter Olympic Games for Weston and his achievements have not gone unnoticed. Indeed, as well as being given the freedom of his hometown, Crowborough, and an honorary doctor degree at the University of Kent, he is among the frontrunners to win the most prestigious honour in British sport.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Weston is, at the time of writing, priced at 11/1 with bet365 to claim the SPOTY award in December, with only Amy Hunt (5/6), Josh Kerr (10/3) and Harry Kane (7/2) ahead of him. Jude Bellingham (14/1) and Saffie Osborne (33/1) complete the top six.

‌



View 5 Images Matt Weston posing with his first gold medal at the Milano Cortina Games (Image: Getty Images)

Speaking to The Mirror about the potential of winning SPOTY, Weston said: "I think the honour for me, like you said at the start, there has been so many pinch me moments and so many people that I've met and situations that I've been in that I never thought would be possible.

‌



"I do a sport where we don't get much publicity. When you compare us to footballers and things like that, we're like the 0.1 per cent of the publicity and the time and effort that, well, the viewership that they get. And the fact that my name is up there with some huge athletics and football names, like I'm next to Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham! Just to have my name on these lists that are going out there at the moment, that's an honour in itself for me. I'm really happy with that.

"The thought of winning it? I don't know, I don't know. It would be insane. I've already had some amazing responses from the British public and the support that they have given me. I feel very honoured to be a part of that and feel very grateful. And the fact that there's a chance that the British public could do that for me as well would be honestly insane.

‌



"I'm struggling to find the words, really, of how much that would mean to me. It would mean a lot for not just myself, but my family, my friends, the team as well. The recognition would be me going up there, but actually what it would mean for my teammates, for the coaching staff, for the support staff, for everyone who's been a part of my journey getting me to this point. I think it would mean a lot to be honest."

If Weston came out on top, he would become the first Winter Olympian to win SPOTY since ice dancers Jayne Torvill and Christopher Dean, following their iconic gold-winning performance at the Sarajevo Games in 1984.

‌



While he does feel he has the support from the British public heading into SPOTY, he believes the timing of winning the gold medals won't do him "any favours".

View 5 Images Matt Weston celebrates winning gold at the Milano Cortina Games (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"I think I do a very unique sport and it was a very unique situation what happened at the Olympics and the response from the public was absolutely crazy," Weston said. "I think I am kind of in a bit of a strong point with that.

"I think the only thing that doesn't do me any favours is that the Olympics was in February and Sports Personality of the Year is in December. So I'm almost as far away as you can be from Sports Personality of the Year, from my achievements.

‌



"But the fact that my name is still up there, I think kind of shocks me sometimes at how much of an impact that might have had on the British public as well as myself. So I think we're in a good position, but like all these things, I never want to believe anything until I'm actually there experiencing it. So I'm keeping my fingers crossed and I'm just saying yes to everything and revelling in kind of what's unfolding in front of me."

Weston's double-gold medal haul in Milano Cortina was even more remarkable when just four years before, he finished 15th in the individual skeleton event at the Beijing Winter Olympics and thought about quitting the sport.

‌



But Weston bounced back to win gold at the World Championships in 2023 and 2025, as well as gold at the European Championships in 2023, giving him huge motivation and confidence to come out on top at the Winter Olympics.

"When I first came back from Beijing, I almost wanted to quit the sport," the two-time world champion added. "It was pretty gutting for me. It was really disappointing. I felt like I'd let myself down, the country down, family, team, all that sort of thing.

‌



View 5 Images Matt Weston's Milano Cortina Games was an iconic one (Image: Getty Images)

"It was, yeah, you kind of want to go to the Games and you want it to be this amazing kind of fairy tale of an experience, which kind of, in a way, it was. I actually loved my time at the Beijing Olympics, just apart from the racing side of things, which is almost the most important part.

‌



"But after I'd given myself some time to kind of decompress and accept what had happened, I kind of used that disappointment and turned it into like a fire to like go, 'this isn't the end of my Olympic journey, this isn't the end of my story within skeleton' that I want to make.

"I want to make something better of it, and I used that as kind of like a fire to give me the motivation and dedication to be able to go out there and make sure that this wasn't going to happen again and that I was going to leave no stone unturned on the way to Milano Cortina."

‌



After suffering disappointment in Beijing and a string of long-term injuries, Weston sought help from a psychologist. He had been struggling with his mental health and wanted to ensure his head was in the "right place to go and perform".

Weston admitted: "I mean, the team, there's certain members of the team that were really there for me, as well as I think in the past few years I've worked with psychologists as well. I've worked with two currently. One's a sports psych and one's a clinical psych. And when I first started working with them, especially like we worked as a team, like a three-way conversation where me as an athlete and me as a person are almost like two different people.

‌



"So we need to have the whole complete package in the best place to be able to go out and perform. It's not just focusing just on sport, it's about life as well, because that can creep into your performance. So we've worked a lot.

"It's been a pretty tough journey to get to this point, but I think a lot of my success and a lot of the consistency which I've had is a result of working with the psychologists and making sure my head is in the right place to go out there and perform. And I think that that made a big difference going into this Games, because there was obviously a lot of pressure on my shoulders going in. I've been world number one for the past three years, so I was able to handle that really well because of the work I've put in with the psychologists."

‌



Back in March, fresh after winning in Milano Cortina, Weston admitted he hasn't thought about whether he will aim for Team GB's outright gold medal record at the 2030 French Alps Games. He is level on two with retired skeleton star Yarnold, who was victorious at Sochi 2014 and PyeongChang 2018.

View 5 Images Matt Weston with Lizzy Yarnold (Image: Getty Images)

‌



But now, Weston has revealed that he does "like the idea" of becoming Team GB’s outright most successful Winter Olympian and has "thought about" it.

"A bit of both, to be honest," Weston continued, when asked if he has thought about the record going into the 2030 Games. "Obviously that's come into my mind, but my main priority this year has been enjoying it. I've put nine years of dedication, hard work and sacrifice into this. So I've missed weddings, funerals, birthdays, and so much important family time. I've really tried to, as much as I can, catch up with that and enjoy the kind of reward from winning the Olympics, which is still really weird for me to say.

‌



"But I have had a thought about, like at the moment, obviously in terms of medal tally, I'm tied with Lizzie Arnold for the overall most successful British Winter Olympian ever, which is, there's a lot of things that I'm saying that are still very crazy for me to say. That kind of doesn't feel real, but there is a lot of temptation for me to go out there and be like, well, actually, like, I quite like winning.

"So I quite like the idea of being Britain's outright most successful [Winter Olympian]. So that is something that definitely is playing on my mind, but at the moment I'm kind of focusing on getting my body fixed, as well as spending time with family, friends and my new wife as well."

Article continues below

While getting married his wife Alex, Weston has spent the last couple of months on the treatment table, having had surgeries on his shoulder and his hip. But, after recovering, he is now focused on the winter season and getting back to competing following his heroics in Milano Cortina.

Sports.title: Newbury meeting abandoned and Saturday racing threatened by Storm Austen
Sports.content:
Newbury meeting abandoned and Saturday racing threatened by Storm Austen

Friday's meeting at Newbury racecourse has been cancelled due to a waterlogged track as Storm Austen hits the country, while an inspection has already been called ahead of their high-profile meeting on Saturday

View 2 Images Racing at Newbury on Saturday under threat from Storm Austen (Image: PA)

Friday's race meeting at Newbury has been scrapped owing to a waterlogged track, while an inspection has already been scheduled ahead of their prestigious Saturday fixture.

‌



‌



With substantial rainfall predicted as Storm Austen batters large swathes of the nation, officials at the Berkshire venue initially arranged an inspection for 8am on Friday before the opening day of two consecutive racing days. However, with sections of the course already waterlogged by Thursday morning, clerk of the course George Hill took the swift decision to cancel the six-race programme.

‌



He said: "We had over 10mm of rain yesterday (Wednesday) and I probably wasn't expecting that much, and then we had another 4.6mm during the early hours of this morning up until 6am.

‌



"When you've had nearly 15mm on top of nearly 20mm the day before, that's just left one or two areas of the track suffering and waterlogged in places.

"We had an inspection this morning and while a lot of areas are raceable, there were some areas we just couldn't get around, and looking at the forecast tonight into tomorrow that is probably going to make matters worse."

Focus now turns to Newbury's final Flat meeting of the year, which is scheduled to showcase two Group 3 fixtures, the St Simon Stakes and Horris Hill Stakes.

‌



Hill has arranged an inspection for 8am on Friday and with an additional 15-30mm expected from 8pm on Thursday right through until after Saturday's racing concludes, he concedes the team are "up against it".

View 2 Images George Hill: Newbury clerk of the course (Image: Alan Crowhurst, Getty Images)

‌



"We've got a nice card planned on Saturday and we just want to give it an extra 24 hours, just to see if there is any improvement either in the track and mainly the forecast for Saturday afternoon," Hill added.

"At the moment it looks like we'll get persistent rain throughout Saturday afternoon, but we just want to give it an extra 24 hours to be double sure before making a decision on Saturday's card.

Article continues below

"When we inspect on Friday morning we'll know what rain we've had up to that point and know what state the ground is in, and we'll also have an up to date forecast to see if there is any opportunity for it to dry out.

"If that persistent rain is still set for Saturday we're likely to be up against it, but we'll see what the next 24 hours bring."

Sports.title: Former Chelsea and England star launches £87m investment bid for League One club
Sports.content:
Former Chelsea and England star launches £87m investment bid for League One club

Former England international Ryan Bertrand has joined forces with a consortium to propose a huge investment deal in an EFL club

View 2 Images Ryan Bertrand is leading a consortium looking to acquire a minority stake in AFC Wimbledon

Former Premier League star Ryan Bertrand has joined forces with a consortium seeking to secure an £87million minority stake in League One outfit AFC Wimbledon. The former England international is playing a leading role in the proposed investment alongside British technology specialist Omar Mir, who is providing the financial backing for the deal.

‌



‌



Mir is financing the takeover proposal through Sloane Street Capital (SSC), with the investment firm planning to acquire a 34 per cent shareholding in AFCW PLC, the organisation responsible for operating the football club. According to the BBC, the agreement would initially see SSC inject £16million into Wimbledon upon completion of the transaction.

‌



A further £71m would then be committed across five seasons, with the investment programme running until the conclusion of the 2030/31 campaign. Should the proposal receive the necessary approval, SSC would assume responsibility for overseeing the club's football activities, while Bertrand would take up a position as senior football advisor.

‌



Football fanatic who'd been to every single AFC Wimbledon match for 37 years dies suddenly READ MORE :

Despite his involvement in sporting decisions, the former Chelsea and Southampton defender would remain subject to the financial limits and operational procedures established by the AFCW PLC board. Discussing the potential partnership, Bertrand expressed his admiration for the club's history and the important role its supporters have played in its development.

"AFC Wimbledon's story is unique in English football and it was built by its supporters. We felt at home from our very first meetings," Bertrand admitted. "We are not here to change what this club is.

"We are here to help it go further on and off the pitch, for the men's team, the women's team and the academy. It would be an honour to join the Wimbledon family and help write the next chapter, and we look forward to meeting members and answering their questions over the coming weeks."

‌



Ensure our latest headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as your Preferred Source in your Google search settings.

Wimbledon would continue to operate under supporter control through The Dons Trust, which currently possesses 50.01 per cent of the voting rights.

‌



The proposed investment has been structured to preserve that arrangement, ensuring the supporters' organisation maintains its existing voting power.

The Dons Trust would also retain the authority to block any proposed changes affecting the freehold of the Cherry Red Records Stadium. Under the suggested governance structure, SSC would be allocated two positions on the club's 12-member board, alongside an additional non-voting observer role.

‌



View 2 Images AFC Wimbledon have had a mixed start to the League One season

Crucially, the supporters' trust would continue to have the final say on fundamental aspects of Wimbledon's identity, including the club's name, crest, traditional colours, stadium and constitution.

‌



The proposed agreement would therefore introduce substantial outside investment while maintaining the supporter-led principles that have defined AFC Wimbledon since its formation.

If SSC decided to offload its shares, the Dons Trust would be given the first opportunity to purchase them and would have the power to reject potential investors it considered unsuitable.

‌



Furthermore, any failure to meet scheduled payments would immediately freeze the growth in SSC's share of the club's value, with control reverting to AFC Wimbledon within three months.

Angus Fox, chair of the Dons Trust board, said: "The deal brings at least £87m into AFC Wimbledon over five years, while the Trust keeps a permanent majority of the votes, control of the Plough Lane freehold and a veto over everything that makes us who we are.

‌



"We have set out the factors to weigh as plainly as the opportunities. The board recommends a yes vote, but this is our members' club and our members' decision."

Bertrand brought his playing career to an end in 2023, having represented several English clubs, including Chelsea, Nottingham Forest, Aston Villa, Southampton and Leicester City. Wimbledon, meanwhile, are sat 16th in the League One table following a mixed start to the season.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta provides worrying Bukayo Saka update after Arsenal star forced off
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta provides worrying Bukayo Saka update after Arsenal star forced off

Bukayo Saka had to be subbed off with an injury just 10 minutes into Arsenal's 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League, giving Mikel Arteta a major concern

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta confirmed the nature of Bukayo Saka's injury (Image: Beanyman Sports)

Mikel Arteta has admitted Arsenal are concerned about Bukayo Saka's injury which 'does not look good at all'. Saka, 25, had to be substituted in the 10th minute of Arsenal's 2-2 draw away to Bayern Munich in the Champions League, with replacement Eberchi Eze breaking the deadlock shortly after.

‌



‌



The winger looked injured his quad while attempting a lofted pass. Post-match, Arteta was asked to provide an update.

‌



"They (medical staff) are a bit concerned," the Arsenal manager told TNT Sports. "A player that has to come off with a really sharp pain is never good news. But we have to wait and see."

‌



Arteta added in his press conference: "It does not look good at all. It's his quad."

Saka missed 10 games for club and country last season, suffering from hip and ankle problems. In late 2024, the England international had surgery on his hamstring, so Arsenal will hope that he doesn't need to go under the knife again.

Arteta was more upbeat about the Gunners' performance at the Allianz Arena. Arsenal surrendered their early lead by conceding goals either side of half-time before Declan Rice popped up with an equaliser late on.

‌



"That is one of the highest levels we played," Arteta hailed. "Two teams who wanted to press each other and wanted to attack and wanted to play. It was a fascinating game.

"We started the game incredibly well, we were so dominant. Then we had to adapt without Saka. In the second half the game was a bit even and they scored the goals and we had to react, which we did. We scored and we had the chance to win it too. That is the level."

‌



Will Arsenal win the Champions League? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

Arsenal went for Bayern both in attack and defence. Arteta deployed a man-marking strategy, with Ezri Konsa often following Harry Kane into the middle third.

Rice explained how the Gunners wanted to assert themselves. "It's what the manager has drilled into us; we aren't just going to come here and sit," the Arsenal midfielder stated.

‌



"At home, they are probably one of the best teams in Europe, so to come here tonight and give that account of ourselves was really good. We have to keep going."

Arsenal resume their Premier League campaign this Saturday at home to Everton before they travel to Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday. Their next Champions League fixture is away to Slavia Prague and that comes after a trip to face Liverpool at Anfield.

Sports.title: Arsenal leave it late vs Bayern Munich but Mikel Arteta dealt huge injury blow
Sports.content:
Arsenal leave it late vs Bayern Munich but Mikel Arteta dealt huge injury blow

BAYERN MUNICH 2-2 ARSENAL: Declan Rice's equaliser denied Harry Kane from being the match winner, as the points were shared in an entertaining Champions League clash

View 3 Images Arsenal left it late to grab a draw (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Declan Rice came to the rescue for Arsenal as they played out an entertaining 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich. The Gunners were staring down the barrel of a first Champions League defeat in normal time for 18 games, but Rice's equaliser snatched a valuable point from Harry Kane and Co.

‌



‌



Despite not being named in the starting line-up, Eberechi Eze opened the scoring with 25 minutes gone. The Arsenal star had replaced Bukayo Saka, who picked up an injury which will leave Mikel Arteta concerned.

‌



Bayern quickly replied through Alphonso Davies, but the equaliser was all about the pass from Kane, who put Bayern 2-1 up from the penalty spot following a handball from Jurrien Timber. No wonder the England captain the favourite to win the Ballon d'Or on Monday.

‌



Although Bayern manager Vincent Kompany was well enough to be on the touchline after missing his pre-match press conference through illness, his side were without several key players. Michael Olise was suspended following his red card last time out while Joshua Kimmich and Jamal Musiala were both injured.

Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



No Saka, no problem - for now

Who'd have thought that after being hooked at half-time against Nottingham Forest, Eze would be the man to put Arsenal in front? Very few, we're guessing, after the 28-year-old started on the bench.

But Eze was needed after 10 minutes when Saka injured what looked to be his quad. Arteta gave Eze a smile and a hug before he entered the fray, and quarter of an hour later, he fired Arsenal ahead.

‌



Martin Odegaard launched a wonderfully weighed pass over Bayern's defence which found the chasing Eze, who let the ball bounce before lashing it past Manuel Neuer from close range. The linesman initially raised his flag but the goal was given upon review.

Will Arsenal win the Champions League? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

‌



View 3 Images Bukayo Saka was replaced by Eberechi Eze on 10 minutes (Image: Stuart Franklin - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

Kane closes in on Champions League record

You can't move for Kane stats these days. Whether it be 24 goals and assists already this season, 156 goals in 158 games for Bayern or the fact that he's now scored in 10 successive Champions League games, the numbers speaks for themselves.

‌



It's that last stat which comes into focus on a European night. Kane's well-taken penalty following a handball by Jurrien Timber means that he's one game away from equalling Cristiano Ronaldo's record of scoring in 11 games on the trot.

Next up: Atletico Madrid away. He's never faced them before.

‌



View 3 Images Harry Kane needs to score against Atletico Madrid to equal Cristiano Ronaldo's record (Image: Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

Rice to the rescuse

May 2025 marks the last time that Arsenal lost a European fixture inside 90 minutes and the Gunners were determined not to end that run at the Allianz Arena. For all the critics of their style of play, Arsenal worked an attack beautifully in the 82nd minute to cut Bayern open before Rice produced an emphatic finish and made it 2-2.

Article continues below

The Gunners midfielder started the move by popping the ball out to Noni Madueke, who then found Viktor Gyokeres on the corner of the penalty area. The Swede held off Jonathan Tah and with a lovely touch sent Rice through on goal, and he showed great composure to slot the ball home.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick hits back at Bruno Fernandes comments in extraordinary press conference
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick hits back at Bruno Fernandes comments in extraordinary press conference

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has responded to some veiled criticism from captain Bruno Fernandes in the wake of the Red Devils' humbling by Como

View 2 Images Carrick hit back at Fernandes in an extraordinary press conference (Image: UEFA via Getty Images)

Michael Carrick hit back at captain Bruno Fernandes after the Manchester United skipper blasted a 'decision from staff' following the Red Devils' lamentable defeat at Como.

‌



‌



United were hammered 4-1 by Cesc Fabregas' side in a result that has plunged Carrick's future into doubt. His team have won just twice in 11 games so far this term.

‌



Fernandes said the coaching staff had opted not to adopt a man-to-man marking policy in the game, suggesting it contributed to the heavy defeat.

‌



"It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave a bit of space in behind and then try to get the ball in the first moment to wait for them, to give them the ball," the Portuguese captain told TNT Sports.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"But sometimes when you give too much the ball [away] to these teams, they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot which makes people get frustrated.

"And then, when we recover the ball, the legs and the brain are much more difficult to make it work."

‌



But Carrick has hit back, suggesting Fernandes' comments are not accurate. "We actually half-pressed man-to-man the second half and then conceded a goal from that," he said.

"And there's a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you ain't going to win."

‌



Carrick took aim at his side's effort, while accepting the buck stops with him.

View 2 Images Fernandes had aimed a veiled dig at Carrick

‌



"We might win, we might lose, but the way we went about it tonight, I wouldn't say everyone, but the way we went about it in some ways tonight wasn't acceptable. And I just wanted to let the fans know that I feel for them, for sure," he added.

"It wasn't just the goals, if I'm totally honest. It was the manner and the way we played at times, in the way we went about it, that was the difficult thing to watch for me.

‌



"It's not about playing for me, it's about playing for this football club. It's the responsibility that comes with being in the position; I'm responsible for the football club and the supporters.

"I'm giving my best, absolute best all the time, I care about it. My whole life's wrapped around it. I genuinely give everything that I possibly can."

Sports.title: Man City charges: Fresh investigation confirmed as EFL 'ready to agree' punishment
Sports.content:
All the latest news on Manchester City's guilty verdict ahead of their appeal hearing, with the club now expected to receive a 'huge points deduction' and a fine

At the end of September, the Premier League confirmed that City had been found guilty on all charges relating to breaches of its financial regulations between 2009/10 and 2017/18. It was revealed that City had artificially inflated revenue by more than £900million through so-called 'sham' sponsorship deals.

City, however, have vehemently denied any wrongdoing and submitted an appeal against the ruling on October 1. In an official statement, the club maintained they are "innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League" and claim they possess "a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence" to support their position.

Nevertheless, The Daily Mail have reported that the 'most likely' outcome is a three-pronged punishment for City, with the club expected to receive a 'points deduction which will guarantee relegation' and a 'huge fine'.

It's suggested that the sanction could include an additional points deduction that would virtually ensure City remain in the Championship for at least one further season, though the EFL would not be compelled to accept that penalty for one of their clubs. However, it's understood they would be prepared to agree to the points deduction.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick's reaction says it all as Como hammering leaves job hanging by a thread
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick's reaction says it all as Como hammering leaves job hanging by a thread

Manchester United's abject 4-1 loss away to Como has left Michael Carrick fighting to save his job, and his reaction when he went over to their fans after full-time spoke volumes

View 3 Images Michael Carrick fronted up to the furious Manchester United fans (Image: PIERO CRUCIATTI/AFP via Getty Images)

Michael Carrick apologised to Manchester United's sodden supporters and coldly ignored his players after their woeful 4-1 defeat against Como. The hammering has left Carrick's job hanging by a thread, as United fans call for him to be sacked.

‌



‌



And of the 700 who'd made the journey to Como, where it was lashing down with rain, most had already left the open-ended away section by the time the final whistle sounded. After shaking hands with Cesc Fabregas, Carrick marched straight over to the 100 or so supporters who remained.

‌



The beleaguered boss put one hand on his chest and raised both of his arms by way of apology before walking past his players and going down the tunnel. United have won just two of their 11 games in all competitions this season and Wednesday's performance against Como was arguably their worst of what's been a sorry campaign.

‌



Post-match, Carrick told TNT Sports: "It was more than disappointing. I think everybody has got to take responsibility for that. I 100 per cent take responsibility for the overall team and the performance - that's where it stops.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"It stops with me and I'm absolutely fine with that. I accept that totally. But as a supporter of this football club for so long, to see a performance like that is unacceptable, I have to say."

"I care an unbelievable amount about the supporters. They are the heartbeat of this football club and they always will be. For them to travel, I had to apologise for the performance. To have to watch a performance like that, I totally feel for them. There are no excuses at all. It is not acceptable."

‌



Carrick added on the topic on his future: "It's not about me. It's about digesting the game and how it went. That is the most important thing right now."

Should Manchester United sack Michael Carrick? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 3 Images Michael Carrick cut a despondent figure in Como (Image: Nderim Kaceli/BSR Agency/Getty Images)

United captain Bruno Fernandes, who was subbed off after a poor display, suggested that Carrick and his coaching staff got their tactics wrong. "It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence," Fernandes explained.

‌



"That's on the manager and staff to see, not me. Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable. As you saw with them [Como], the centre-back was coming to mark me in my own half. We need to do that as a team but we were unable to.

"A team that plays through the middle with small connections, if you give them too much time and space then they can hurt you out wide."

‌



Carrick responded to Fernandes' comments in his press conference, saying: "We actually half-pressed man-to-man the second half and then conceded a goal from that. And there's a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you ain't going to win."

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes called out Manchester United's tactics (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

‌



The 45-year-old went on to say: "We might win, we might lose, but the way we went about it tonight, I wouldn't say everyone, but the way we went about it in some ways tonight wasn't acceptable. And I just wanted to let the fans know that I feel for them, for sure.

"It wasn't just the goals, if I'm totally honest. It was the manner and the way we played at times, in the way we went about it, that was the difficult thing to watch for me.

‌



"It's not about playing for me, it's about playing for this football club. It's the responsibility that comes with being in the position; I'm responsible for the football club and the supporters. I'm giving my best, absolute best all the time, I care about it. My whole life's wrapped around it. I genuinely give everything that I possibly can."

When asked if his players were doing the same, Carrick replied: "I'd like to think so. I didn't like what I saw tonight, though."
