Sports.title: Featured Comment: Budget cap not to blame for lack of winning teams in F1 | Brief
Sports.content:
This week’s poll asks whether Formula 1 needs to rethink its budget cap as the series’ top four team have pulled further away from their rivals this year.

But reader @Skydiverian suggests it might not be realistic to expect F1 to regularly have more than four race-winning teams:

Four competitive teams has happened before but it’s still not great and the problem is as it always is, money. And I’d like to see more teams in a season have a realistic shot of winning races. It’s unfortunate that the stats are not on my side.

Pretty much since the late 80s the problem has been that the best teams could throw more money at the problem to fix it. Now, teams that are significantly behind can’t throw more money at the problem to catch-up due to the cost cap, rather than simply not having the money in the first place as was common in the 80s. (This season is interesting. It seems that Mercedes blew most of it’s cap early to get and maintain their advantage, whereas Red Bull didn’t and that’s in part why Max has had a better car the last two races. But it’s not like Williams or Aston Martin can fix their problems by spending more money to fix the deficit).

The problem is that ultimately there’s no easy fix, but spending millions to be the so-called best of the rest basically seems pointless if there is a very unlikely chance of a team outside of the top four having a realistic shot at the podium or even a win. And that’s always been a problem going back decades.

Some number crunching by looking at the history books: the 500th race was 1990 Australia, 1,100th being Vegas 2023. In those 600 races I’ve found six that were won by drivers driving for teams who finished outside the top four in the constructors championship.

That’s six of 600 races over 33 years where we had a winner driving for a team who finished outside the top 4 in that years constructors championship, 1% of all races. Seven if you count Johnny Herbert’s win at the Nurburgring which to me was a genuine surprise at the time. To me those stats aren’t good enough.

Whether that’s the fault of teams with no money, teams with too much money or teams with a cash limit so they can’t design their way out is up for debate. But my point is that I’d like to see more teams have a reasonable chance of winning. F1 has never really had that and will continue not to unless something changes (maybe by letting teams further down have a bigger budget the following season rather than just more CFD time).

I’d rather that at least 70% of drivers have a realistic chance of winning, ideally 100% of teams. It’s the reason I preferred IndyCar before Alex Palou showed up, results were unpredictable and smaller teams have a chance of getting a win or two. That’s just so rare in F1 and the current cost cap rules will continue to make unlikely.

@Skydiverian

Sports.title: Early coronation for Antonelli? Five talking points for the United States Grand Prix | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli could win the world championship this weekend in only his second year as a Formula 1 driver. Here are the talking points for the United States Grand Prix.

Will Antonelli clinch the title?

The odds are stacked heavily in favour of Mercedes’ new star clinching the title at some point, but most likely not this weekend. That said it is not beyond the realm of possibility team mate George Russell could have another poor weekend and come away point-less while Antonelli takes his ninth victory of the season, putting him over the line.

The title has been won at this track twice before, and both times it was by a Mercedes druver: Lewis Hamilton won the championship there in 2015 and 2019. But regardless of whether Antonelli does clinch the title this weekend it is clearly a matter of ‘when’ not ‘if’.

Verstappen dominating again?

The driver most likely to delay Antonelli’s championship celebrations is not his team mate but Max Verstappen. Red Bull have made a breakthrough with their RB22 and as well as winning the last two grands prix plus a sprint race, Verstappen could have taken victory in Baku as well with better luck.

He arrives at this weekend’s race looking like the driver to beat, with every indication he could dominate the final rounds of the season, setting himself up for a shot at the title next year.

McLaren’s driver headache

McLaren arrive in Austin in a curiously similar situation to last year: a clash between their drivers at the previous race in Singapore has created an obvious tension. What’s more, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri’s collision during the sprint race in Singapore was more costly than the one they had in the grand prix 12 months ago.

Norris’s radio messages during the grand prix gave the distinction impression he was looking for ways to make amends, having eventually accepted he was the one at fault for their collision. But above all the team will be anxious to avoid a repeat of the first-corner collision which wrecked their sprint race at the circuit 12 months ago. Particularly as a resurgent Red Bull are poised to relegate the reigning constructors’ champions to fourth place in the standings.

US teams’ driver decisions

Of the two teams competing in their home event this weekend, one has settled its driver plans for 2027. Haas has announced Rafael Camara as the replacement for Esteban Ocon, whose Formula 1 future is in serious doubt as few likely alternatives remain for next year.

Could Cadillac be one of them? F1’s new American team is yet to confirm its plans for next year. However its hopes IndyCar star Colton Herta would take Formula 2 by storm and make himself an obvious candidate for promotion have been dashed: he lies 19th in the standings, 181 points behind fellow rookie and championship leader Camara.

Are Colapinto’s die-hards paying attention?

Last week Franco Colapinto spoke out in criticism of the element of his fanbase which has sent vile abuse to his rival drivers, team members and FIA officials since he made his F1 debut this year. The Alpine driver told those attacking others in his name that they are not helping his cause in F1.

Will they take his words on board? We’ll get an indication the next time he is involved in any kind of incident on-track – however slight it may be.

Are you going to the United States Grand Prix?

If you’re heading to USA for this weekend’s race, we want to hear from you:

Who do you think will be the team to beat in the United States Grand Prix? Have your say below.

Sports.title: On This Day: Ralf Schumacher wins Formula Nippon title despite spinning out | Brief
Sports.content:
30 years ago today Ralf Schumacher won the Formula Nippon title despite retiring two laps into a rain-lashed race.

Schumacher arrived at the final race at Fuji Speedway just two points ahead of team mate Naoki Hattori. But Schumacher spun out two laps into the rain-hit race (see 3’50 in the video below).

That left Hattori on course for the title, which looked increasingly secure as the laps ticked down. But conditions worsened, and seven laps from home he spun out too, handing Schumacher the 1996 title. Schumacher made his F1 debut the following year for Jordan (now Aston Martin).

Katsutomo Kaneishi won ahead of future Formula 1 driver Pedro de la Rosa. Another future F1 driver, Shinji Nakano, took fourth place behind Masahiko Kageyama. Just seven of the 26 starters were running at the finish.

Sports.title: Fired On His Day Off: Bradley Shreds Shakur Stevenson Over Lost Zuffa Contract
Sports.content:
Tim Bradley pulled no punches on his channel when breaking down how Shakur Stevenson lost his Zuffa Boxing contract. According to Bradley, Shakur fumbled massive money because he failed to deliver the one matchup the promotion actually cared about: Devin Haney.

“Shakur and his team, they thought that they was going to pull off a lick,” Bradley said on Into the Storm. “They was just like, ‘Oh yeah, we got these stupid people up here. They don’t know nothing about boxing.’”

Bradley believes Shakur and his handlers completely misread the room, assuming they were dealing with naive outsiders whom they could easily manipulate. In reality, Zuffa’s willingness to spend fifteen million dollars per fight was meant strictly for marquee events, not hand-picked opposition like Gary Antuanne Russell.

“The fight that Zuffa wanted was Haney-Shakur. Period,” Bradley said.

He also mocked how readily Zuffa allowed Shakur to leave his contract, imagining the company responding, “We good.”

“How big of a damn diva you got to be to get released on your contract?” Bradley asked.

Bradley highlighted the absurdity of the split, pointing out how rare it is for a fighter to get released from a massive deal without ever stepping into the ring. He called out Shakur’s team for managing his career poorly, arguing that letting an eight-figure bag slip away was inexcusable.

While Bradley noted that prolonged weight squabbles and promotional moves damaged the negotiations on both sides, he laid the ultimate fault on Shakur’s reluctance to take real risks.

“All this was done because you afraid to lose that O,” he said. “It’s about protecting that damn O, bro.”

Now planning to launch his own promotional outfit, Shakur faces a stark reality. Finding financial backers willing to offer that caliber of purse without top-tier opponents is nearly impossible. As Bradley put it, someone has to put up the money, and Zuffa was ready to do that, but Shakur was unwilling to fight the opponent required to earn it.

When an entity like Zuffa comes into boxing with massive venture backing, they aren’t paying a fighter $15 million a fight out of altruism—they are paying for immediate, marquee box-office events to establish their footprint.

Shakur made three miscalculated moves. For starters, treating Silicon Valley/UFC money like naive marks. Bradley’s phrase that they thought they could “pull off a lick” was dead-on.

Shakur’s camp operated like they could sign the deal, dictate terms from high above, and then demand eight-figure checks to fight safe stylistic matchups like Gary Antuanne Russell. They forgot that Zuffa’s entire business model is built on rigid control, star matchups, and high returns.

Then he got dragged into prolonged posturing over weight. The nine-month negotiation saga over whether they’d fight at 144, 145, or 147 pounds drained every ounce of momentum. By letting the fight stall over a couple of pounds, and then throwing Keyshawn Davis into the mandatory picture as an artificial wedge, they gave Devin and Bill Haney the opening to outmaneuver them entirely and do their own business with DAZN.

Prioritizing the “0” over generational exposure: At 27 or 28, in the prime of his physical career, Shakur had a direct pipeline to beat Haney, fight Ryan Garcia, and cement himself as the premier American star of this era. Instead, the hyper-defensive mindset inside the ring mirrored his mindset outside of it: risk minimization at all costs.

Getting released from an eight-figure contract without ever throwing a single punch under the banner, literally getting “fired on your day off” while only doing a broadcast stint, is almost unheard of at that level of boxing.

Betting on yourself only works if the market is willing to pay what you think you’re worth. Now Shakur is left trying to build his own promotional company in a landscape where broadcast money is tightening, and network buyers aren’t handing out $15 million paydays for sparring sessions.

Sports.title: Arnold Barboza Hints At Devin Haney Title Shot
Sports.content:
Arnold Barboza Jr. dropped word on social media that a massive welterweight title opportunity just landed in his lap on short notice. While he confirmed that 147 pounds is locked in with a belt on the line, he kept the identity of his opponent quiet for now.

Speculation immediately involved Devin Haney after Haney’s anticipated matchup with Shakur Stevenson fell apart. Barboza’s remarks point to a fast-developing opening, even if ink has not officially met paper yet.

“I got some news today. It’s a blessing. I don’t know how real it is, but it sounds pretty real. It might be a big fight sooner than expected,” Barboza said on social media. “I’ll be stepping in at the last minute on some s***, but I don’t know where it’s going to be at, but it’s soon.”

The tight calendar creates the biggest hurdle. Barboza appears fully ready to sign before even knowing the host city, but world championship bouts offer zero room for entering camp cold. Securing an unexpected offer represents one hurdle; having the necessary weeks to dial in a precise tactical blueprint presents an entirely separate challenge.

If Haney ends up standing across the ring, Barboza faces an elite defensive technician. Taking on Haney demands an answer for his distance control, lead hand control, and inside tie ups. Simply tracking him across the canvas without cutting the ring effectively will turn the contest into a frustrating chase.

“A lot sooner than expected. Not no next year fight. A couple of weeks soon. Yeah, I’m fighting at 147. Yeah, it’ll be for a belt. We got to go for legacy,” Barboza said.

Teofimo Lopez also figures heavily into Barboza’s long-range calculations. Barboza sees capturing a 147-pound crown as his quickest ticket to securing a second chance against Lopez after coming up short in their junior welterweight clash.

“It’s not a rematch with Teo. Not yet. I got to win this belt to rematch him,” Barboza admitted.

Holding a world title strap provides massive leverage at the negotiating table. The immediate task requires transforming the sudden opening into an executed contract, setting up a targeted training block, and verifying the sanctioning body timeline.

Sports.title: DAZN Team May Call Canelo-Mbilli From London
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez and Christian Mbilli could fight in Riyadh on October 31, with DAZN’s broadcast team following the action from a studio in London. The potential arrangement adds another question to a card already approaching under difficult circumstances.

Dan Rafael reports that the team is likely to call the event remotely if it goes ahead. His report leaves both points conditional: the card proceeding and the commentators working outside Saudi Arabia.

“Per sources, if #CaneloMbilli goes forward Oct. 31 in Riyadh, the likelihood is that the DAZN broadcast team will not be ringside and will call the card remotely from a studio in London,” Rafael wrote on X.

DAZN’s likely move speaks for itself. Calling one of the year’s biggest fights from television monitors thousands of miles away suggests the broadcast team wants no part of the danger in Riyadh. Promotional talk about the event going ahead cannot erase the attacks on the city’s international airport.

It also creates an awkward contrast. Commentators would work from the safety of a London studio, while Canelo, Mbilli and the undercard fighters would be expected to fly to Riyadh, attend media events and fight. If the risk is enough to keep the broadcast team away, the fighters have every reason to question why they should be there.

The background explains everything. Dan Rafael reported earlier on missile strikes and drone activity aimed at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, even while noting Canelo planned to go ahead anyway. Those strikes turned travel safety and the host city into the dominant story leading up to the bout.

A London crew can watch the live monitors, but calling an event off a monitor is never the same. Commentators lose their direct line of sight between broadcast angles. They miss corner chaos, subtle crowd shifts, and whatever happens outside the camera frame, leaving them watching the exact same feed fans see on their couches.

That is a massive drop in quality for a pay-per-view centered on the sport’s biggest earner. Calling action from ringside lets commentators catch real impacts, subtle cornerman instructions, and shifts in body language that cameras and boom mics miss entirely.

Canelo is penciled in to challenge Mbilli for the WBC super middleweight title. The sanctioning body still lists October 31 in Riyadh on DAZN.

The card needs an official word on how the broadcast will work. Rafael’s reporting suggests fight week will look bizarre, even if both guys walk to the ring on schedule.

Sports.title: Jaron Ennis Calls Sebastian Fundora Too Small
Sports.content:
Jaron Ennis laughed off Sebastian Fundora’s knockout claims, calling the towering champion “too small” to back up his words. Ennis is eyeing Fundora down the line, but he’s making sure business with Josh Kelly gets handled first.

That comment flips the script on Fundora. Opponents usually spend training camp obsessing over his massive reach, but Ennis seems far more eager to exploit openings than worry about incoming fire.

“He too small. He not big enough,” Ennis said to YSM Sports Media when told about Fundora’s knockout comments. “But we focused on Josh Kelly, and that’s the main focus, main target right now. We’ll talk about him later on.”

Ennis kept a close eye on Fundora’s clash with Ermal Hadribeaj, scouting for future business rather than just watching for fun.

“Definitely watching to pick him apart,” Ennis said. “Just to see what he got, and it’s what I’ve been knew.”

Fundora didn’t dial back his confidence at the post-fight presser either. When reporters brought up potential bouts with Ennis or Vergil Ortiz Jr., he insisted he’d halt both.

“If it was those guys, I’d still knock them out,” Fundora said. “These guys can’t hurt me.”

That confidence would face a different examination against Ennis. Choosing to fight inside is one thing against Hadribeaj; giving Ennis opportunities at close range would require Fundora to account for his speed and combinations.

Ennis even took a jab at the Hadribeaj stoppage, arguing the challenger beat the count right as the bell sounded. Regardless, he made it clear he wanted Fundora looking sharp so there are zero asterisks later.

“I don’t want nobody to say nothing,” Ennis said. “No excuses.”

Kelly is the obstacle between that talk and a possible Fundora fight. Ennis described him as a “sharp” and “smart” fighter. Beating him must come before Ennis can turn his confidence against Fundora into something more substantial.

Ennis is spotting the exact same tactical flaw everyone else saw against Hadribeaj: Fundora simply cannot resist fighting like a phone booth brawler. Calling a 6’6″ fighter with an 86-inch reach “too small” sounds bizarre on the surface, but Ennis is talking about physical density and ring presence, not height.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Claims Floyd Mayweather Title Fight Agreement
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia claims he and Floyd Mayweather have agreed to fight for the WBC welterweight title, putting a championship label on a matchup that looks more like a celebrity event than serious business at 147.

The selling point is obvious: Garcia gets a chance to put the first loss on Mayweather’s professional record. Whether beating a 49-year-old version of Floyd would prove much about Ryan’s ability is another question.

“Trust me at first I thought this was bull***,” Garcia posted on X. “But it’s real Floyd and I agree to a fight.”

Garcia added: “147 for the WBC welterweight championship of the world. 50-0 vs The current champ.”

That is Garcia announcing an agreement. His post does not provide a date, venue, or broadcaster, and it does not establish that the WBC has approved Mayweather as a title challenger. Those details still need to follow before this can be treated as a confirmed championship fight.

As a commercial idea, it is easy to understand. Mayweather’s undefeated record gives the promotion something to sell beyond the usual exhibition routine. Ryan would be chasing the “0,” while Floyd would be selling the possibility that he can still beat a much younger champion.

As a title defense, it is a circus.

Mayweather’s reputation was earned against elite fighters over a long career. That reputation does not tell us what he can do at 49 against a current welterweight champion. Putting his record on the line would make the result official, but it would not turn back the clock.

Garcia would also leave himself open to an obvious criticism. Beat Floyd, and he has beaten a retired great approaching 50. Struggle with him, and the questions about Ryan become considerably louder.

There will be people willing to buy it. Two famous names and the possibility of Mayweather finally losing are enough to draw attention beyond boxing’s regular audience.

That is the appeal Garcia is selling. The WBC belt adds decoration, but the attraction is celebrity, money, and a famous unbeaten record.

Sanctioning this as an official WBC welterweight title defense would make a complete joke of the belt and freeze out actual contenders at 147. If two massive names want an unsanctioned exhibition to generate huge pay-per-view numbers, boxing fans understand the drill.

Celebrity events happen all the time now. Slapping an authentic world championship onto it crosses the line from entertainment into parody. Mayweather turns 50 next February and has not fought in a sanctioned professional bout since 2017. He is not ranked by the WBC.

Handing him an immediate shot at a real crown purely because of his fame insults every active fighter grinding through eliminators for a mandatory spot. For Garcia, putting the belt up brings zero boxing credit. If he blows out a 49-year-old retired legend, nobody takes it seriously as a legitimate championship victory.

If he looks bad or gets touched up by Floyd, critics will tear him apart. Keeping it as an exhibition protects the credibility of the sanctioning body, keeps the division moving, and lets fans enjoy the spectacle for what it really is. Turning it into an official title fight cheapens the entire sport.

Sports.title: Moses Itauma Could Fight Four Times In 2027
Sports.content:
Moses Itauma could box four times in 2027, with promoter Frank Warren targeting a January return to give the heavyweight an early start on a busy year.

Warren wants at least three appearances, though fitting in a fourth will depend on the opposition. No opponent or venue has been announced for Itauma’s next fight.

“I would like him to have a minimum of three fights, maybe four if we can fit them in, depending on the opposition as well, of course,” Warren told BoxNation.

That last qualification leaves room for the schedule to change. Four fights would give Itauma regular work, but the value of that activity will come from who Warren puts in front of him. An opponent who makes him solve different problems could provide more than another quick finish.

Warren expects to reveal the next step shortly.

“I think we’ll be sometime next week, towards the end of next week, announcing something, but he’ll be fighting very early next year, probably in January,” he said.

January remains a target rather than a confirmed booking. Still, getting Itauma out that early would leave Warren enough room to spread three more appearances across the remainder of 2027, provided the fights and recovery periods allow it.

The opponent announcement will tell us more about the ambition behind that schedule. Warren offered no names and made no commitment to a world title fight during this interview. His comments were about getting Itauma into the ring regularly.

There is also a practical balance to find. As the opposition improves, fights can require longer preparation and leave less room for a quick turnaround. Warren’s preference for three, with four possible, gives him flexibility without committing Itauma to dates before the opponents are secured.

A busy calendar is a reasonable starting point. The next question is whether those appearances move Itauma closer to the heavyweights he eventually needs to beat.

Sports.title: Dmitry Bivol vs Callum Smith Gets DAZN Confirmation
Sports.content:
DAZN has officially confirmed its coverage of Dmitry Bivol’s December 12 title defense against Callum Smith in Yekaterinburg, Russia, where the Briton will challenge for the WBA, IBF and WBO light heavyweight belts.

The fight was announced on October 12, with DAZN already identified as the broadcaster. Wednesday’s promotional post provides the platform’s own confirmation, although it adds no new date, venue or opponent.

“An unmissable world title unification between Dmitry Bivol & Callum Smith lands on DAZN,” the broadcaster posted.

Bivol will defend his three belts at the UMMC Arena against Smith, who gets an opportunity to become a two-division world champion. Winning those titles requires solving a difficult boxing puzzle on the champion’s home turf.

Smith’s power gives him a threat if he can get close enough to use it. Bivol’s footwork and quick combinations can leave opponents losing rounds while trying to get into punching position. Smith cannot afford to follow him around without producing enough offense.

His prolonged absence has also taken some of the interest out of this fight. Smith’s February 2025 victory over Joshua Buatsi gave him something to build on, but fans will have waited almost 22 months to see him fight again by December 12.

That layoff was not entirely by choice. Smith was scheduled to defend his WBO interim title against David Morrell on April 18 in Liverpool before a training camp injury forced him out less than two weeks before the event. The fight never happened.

The injury explains the canceled return, but it cannot restore the attention lost during his absence. The Buatsi victory has faded into the background, leaving Smith without a recent performance to get fans talking about his chances against Bivol.

There is a sporting cost, too. Smith must find his timing against a champion who can score and move before an opponent gets his punches off. Spending several rounds settling in could leave the challenger chasing a substantial lead.

DAZN has confirmed where fans can watch. Smith’s task is to make this competitive after spending so long out of the ring.

Sports.title: Jack Catterall Ready As Teofimo Lopez Deadline Hits Tomorrow
Sports.content:
Jack Catterall has made it known he is ready to get down to business with the October 22 deadline running out for talks on his ordered WBA welterweight title fight against Teofimo Lopez.

The British southpaw went onto social media while waiting to see if he lands his mandatory crack or gets hit with another postponement.

“READY FOR A FIGHT,” Catterall posted, tagging DAZN Boxing to make sure the network heard him loud and clear.

That puts Catterall’s stance out there in four words. He wants an official date on the calendar, yet the WBA process has not produced one.

Teofimo’s side has tried to get special permission to go after a different opponent, looking into a massive unification clash against Ryan Garcia for early 2027. Catterall stands as the main roadblock for that route because the WBA already issued the order for its super champion to face him next.

Catterall picked up the WBA regular title by beating Shakhram Giyasov back in May. Grabbing that strap put him in direct position for the bout he is trying to nail down right now. Five months have gone by, and he finds himself still stuck waiting for that mandatory pathway to deliver an actual ring return.

The deadline hits at the close of business Eastern Time on Thursday, October 22. It represents the conclusion of the official discussion window set up by the WBA, not an automatic guarantee that Teofimo gets stripped on the spot.

The pending appeal keeps Catterall hanging around for a ruling that will dictate who he faces and how quickly he gets back under the lights. He recently talked about his career being stalled out, and his latest message makes it obvious that no agreement came together behind closed doors.

There is a huge cash reason for Teofimo to chase Ryan Garcia instead. That matchup pulls in massive public interest compared to a mandatory chore against Catterall. Still, Catterall followed every single sanctioning body rule to earn his spot, and a giant commercial payday for the champion does nothing to restore the lost months Catterall spent on the shelf.

Ghana News.title: GPL 2026/27: Hearts boss Kapor wary of ‘difficult’ Holy Stars encounter
Ghana News.content:
Hearts of Oak head coach Nebojsa Kapor has cautioned his side ahead of their Ghana Premier League game against Basake Holy Stars.

The two teams face each other on matchday eight of the league, with both teams hoping to continue their winning run from last weekend.

The Phobians have won all of their last two games against Port City and Vision FC, while Holy Stars have won one and lost one in the same period, losing to Bibiani GoldStars and claiming victory over Bechem United.

Each team has claimed one win in the last four meetings between Hearts and Holy Stars, and despite two points separating the two teams on the league table, Kapor has warned his side not to be complacent.

"We are not going to say we are a better team and we will win. No, never. We are really going to approach them very deep from every single department and from every single individual player," he said.

"Every game here is very difficult. Especially from the mentality side, we have to face this game very tough."

The fixture is scheduled to take place at the University of Ghana Stadium on Friday, October 23.

Ghana News.title: State appeals Court of Appeal ruling suspending Hanan’s trial over charge sheet dispute
Ghana News.content:
The State has appealed to the Supreme Court against the Court of Appeal’s decision to suspend the criminal trial of former Buffer Stock CEO Hanan Aludiba and his wife, Faiza Seidu.

Deputy Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, Dr Justice Srem-Sai, announced the appeal in a Facebook post on Thursday, October 22, 2026, saying it was filed on Wednesday, October 21.

The appeal follows the Court of Appeal’s decision on Monday, October 19, to halt proceedings at the High Court pending the determination of Hanan Aludiba’s challenge to alleged defects in the charge sheet.

Hanan Aludiba and his wife stand trial on multiple charges, including stealing, defrauding by false pretences, wilfully causing financial loss to the Republic, using public office for profit, dishonestly receiving, and money laundering.

The High Court dismissed Hanan’s application to strike out the charge sheet in July 2026. He subsequently appealed that decision and sought a stay of proceedings, which the Court of Appeal granted on October 19.

Dr Srem-Sai argued that a criminal trial should not be suspended simply because an accused person has raised objections to charges, particularly where those objections have already been dismissed as lacking merit.

“The law does not allow a criminal trial to be suspended simply because an Accused Person has complained about some of the charges on the charge sheet, more so when those complaints were dismissed as meritless,” he stated.

The Deputy Attorney-General said the state was challenging the suspension because of its implications for the prosecution of criminal cases.

The appeal seeks to overturn the Court of Appeal’s order. The Supreme Court has not announced a date to hear the matter.

The state’s appeal is the latest development in the procedural dispute over the charges and whether the High Court trial can proceed while Hanan’s appeal is pending.

Ghanaian musician Kweku Flick has teamed up with Shatta Wale on a new single titled Sweet, which explores resilience, confidence and the pursuit of success.

Shatta Wale’s feature brings his signature energy and large fanbase to the record.

Ghana News.title: Ghana Water rewards prompt-paying customers as complaints over unreliable supply persist
Ghana News.content:
Ghana Water Limited’s Accra East Region is rewarding customers who consistently pay their water bills on time, even as some beneficiaries raise concerns about unreliable supply.

The initiative, organised as part of Customer Service Month, involves visits to selected domestic, commercial and industrial customers who are being presented with customised gifts in recognition of their prompt payments.

Chief Manager of the Accra East Region, Richard Appiah Otto, said the programme was intended to encourage payment discipline and help the company mobilise revenue to address operational challenges.

“We have extreme difficulties in getting some customers to pay their water bills,” he said.

He noted that some customers resort to illegal connections and other practices that undermine the company’s operations.

“But the customers we visited today are shining examples of customers who pay their water bills as soon as they receive the bills,” Mr Otto said.

According to him, prompt payment enables Ghana Water to generate the revenue and resources needed to improve service delivery and respond to operational challenges.

“That allows us to generate the needed revenue and the resources, and also save time to attend to all the problems that face us as a utility,” he added.

Despite the recognition, some beneficiaries say their commitment to paying their bills has not translated into consistent access to water.

At Labadi, one of the customers, William Ablorh Adjei, said he had experienced inadequate water supply for an extended period despite regularly settling his bills.

“Since last year, there has been no proper flow. Previously, we had water twice a week, but now it is zero,” he said.

His concerns highlight the expectations of customers who believe reliable water supply should accompany their efforts to meet their payment obligations.

Another beneficiary, Ernestina Sowah, stressed the importance of paying for water services, describing prompt payment as a civic responsibility.

“I know that if you enjoy potable water, you must pay for it. Those who owe should pay,” she said in Twi.

Ghana Water Limited says the reward programme will continue beyond this year as part of efforts to encourage more customers to pay their bills promptly.

The company has also warned customers with outstanding bills to settle their debts or risk disconnection.

While the initiative is intended to strengthen payment discipline and improve revenue collection, concerns raised by some beneficiaries point to the importance of reliable supply in sustaining customer confidence and encouraging timely payment.

Ghana News.title: Repatriation plans underway for 7 ‘missing but found’ Sekondi fishermen from Benin
Ghana News.content:
Efforts are underway to repatriate seven fishermen aboard the canoe Second Chance who were reported missing at sea but have since been rescued in Benin’s territorial waters.

The crew’s disappearance prompted a multi-agency search after the canoe failed to return from a fishing expedition off Axim in the Western Region.

The canoe reportedly departed Sekondi Fishing Harbour on October 9 but suffered an engine failure, leaving the fishermen drifting offshore.

The Western Regional Marine Police Command said in a statement dated October 22 that the seven men were rescued by local fishermen in Benin on October 21 at about 10 pm.

The rescued fishermen have been identified as Kofi Emmanuel, 32; Uncle Amoah, 45; Kwamena Nkum, 29; Kofi Aboagye, 36; Doboa, 35; Agya Badu, 42; and Kwamena Akyem, 40.

“The coordination is ongoing between the Marine Police Command, Ghana Navy and their counterparts in Benin and Togo to facilitate their safe repatriation to Ghana,” the statement said.

The Command added that further updates would be communicated as more information became available. The rescue brings relief to the fishermen’s families as arrangements continue for their safe return home.

Ghana News.title: Protecting Ghana’s Students: Is the Time Right to revisit the case for Comprehensive Sexuality Education in our schools?
Ghana News.content:
Michael Augustus Akagbor

By Michael Augustus Akagbor, PhD

When students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School vented their anger on campus in August this year, damaging property and forcing the school to close, many of us saw only indiscipline. Look a little closer, and a more troubling picture appears: young people who, by several accounts, had been trying for months to be heard.

At least 19 female students have accused their headmaster of sexual abuse over the past year, according to an investigation by journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni. The Ghana Education Service interdicted him on 14th October, and on 20th October, the Interior Minister told Parliament that he had been arrested and that DNA evidence was being pursued.

The headmaster has signalled legal action. The allegations are yet to be tested in court; he is entitled to due process, and I will not prejudge the outcome.

A system that did not listen

We do not need a verdict, however, to learn from how this case was handled. Teachers responsible for girl-child education and safeguarding reportedly wrote several letters and petitions, and the Municipal Education Directorate was aware of complaints.

The president of NAGRAT said 38 teachers were asked to leave the school after speaking out against the headmaster, and that concerns date back to 2025. A district inquiry reportedly heard from only nine of 26 students, and treated one girl's account of unwanted touching as merely her "definition" of assault.

The warning signs were there. The people who raised them were sidelined. Left with no channel they trusted, the students eventually took matters into their own hands. Today, newly posted first-years cannot even begin classes.

Sadly, Obuasi is not an exception. The same school saw a housemaster accused of misconduct in 2018. A national survey by the Gender Studies and Human Rights Documentation Center estimated that about one in 11 Ghanaian girls will experience sexual violence from a teacher or other school authority figure.

Another study of 490 pupils in public schools found that 11.2% had been victims of rape or defilement, with girls making up 92% of victims, and concluded that our child-protection system was ineffective. Years earlier, a UNICEF survey found that 6% of schoolgirls said teachers had threatened to lower their grades unless they agreed to sex.

The conversation we abandoned

In 2019, Ghana's attempt to introduce Comprehensive Sexuality Education (CSE) was withdrawn after a fierce backlash from religious bodies and others who feared it would bring foreign values into our classrooms. As recently as January this year, the Catholic Bishops' Conference sought assurances that CSE would not return to the curriculum.

Those concerns deserve respect. Parents have a right to shape what their children learn about morality and family life, and many sincerely believe that moral formation and abstinence teaching are the best protection a child can have.

But Obuasi forces an uncomfortable question: what has our silence protected? Not the girls who reportedly were summoned alone to a headmaster's residence. Not the students who lacked the words, or the confidence, to say clearly that what was happening to them was abuse and would be taken seriously.

What the evidence tells us

At its core, good sexuality education teaches children that their bodies belong to them, that no adult, however senior, has the right to touch them or trade favours for grades, and that telling a trusted adult is the right thing to do.

A Cochrane review of 24 trials involving 5,802 children found that school-based abuse-prevention education improved children's knowledge and protective behaviour and made them more likely to disclose abuse, with no sign that it made them anxious. That matters, because abusers depend on one thing above all else: silence.

A Ghanaian way forward

Revisiting CSE does not mean importing a foreign curriculum wholesale. It means building our own, with parents, faith leaders, teachers and young people at the table, anchored in values most Ghanaians share: dignity, respect and the protection of children. Whatever we call it, certain lessons should be non-negotiable: bodily autonomy, consent, recognising abuse of authority, and knowing how to report it. And because only about half of our adolescents reach senior high school, these lessons must begin in basic school.

Education alone is not enough. Children who speak up need adults and systems that respond. That means confidential reporting channels that do not run through the school head, such as a national toll-free line linked to the Department of Social Welfare and the Police DOVVSU.

It means real protection for teachers who blow the whistle, not transfers. It means making the GES Code of Conduct legally binding, as the Education Minister has proposed. And it means counseling, legal support and uninterrupted schooling for the Obuasi students.

So, is the time, right?

I believe it is. The real question was never whether our children will learn about sex and relationships; they will, from peers, phones and, too often, from those who would exploit them.

The question is whether they will learn from us, in a framework we design, that their bodies are their own and that adults who abuse power will be held to account.

The students of Obuasi SHTS had to protest to be heard. The next generation should not have to.

About the Writer

The writer is the Programs Manager for Human Rights and Social Inclusion at The Ghana Center for Democratic Development (CDD-Ghana).

Ghana News.title: Interdicted Obuasi SHTS head sues JoyNews’ Manasseh Azure for defamation amid sexual abuse allegations
Ghana News.content:
JoyNews Investigative Correspondent, Manasseh Azure Awuni, has confirmed that he has been sued for defamation by the interdicted headmaster of the Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), Zakaria Abdulai, over allegations of sexual abuse involving female students in the school.

Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Thursday, October 22, Mr Azure said the case was his 12th defamation suit since 2015 and that his lawyers would handle it.

“That is defamation suit number 12 since 2015, and I think my lawyers will handle that,” he said.

Manasseh Azure's investigative piece titled Inside The Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow exposed cases of alleged rape involving the headmaster, leading to his interdiction by the Ghana Education Service amid ongoing investigations.

Following the investigation, the Headmaster, who also served as Juaben Constituency Secretary for the National Democratic Congress and was seeking to contest for Constituency Chairman, withdrew from the race under pressure from his party.

It emerged from the report that some of the alleged sexual cases had been reported to the Police, but investigations were either slow or had stalled.

The report also revealed that some teachers, education authorities and political heads had failed to fulfil responsibilities expected of them, resulting in pressure and victimisation against staff members seeking justice for the affected girls.

He specifically mentioned the school’s focal person and girl-child coordinator, as well as others he said were determined to pursue justice for the students.

“There were things they were supposed to do that they didn’t do, and because of that there was a lot of pressure and victimisation against the focal person, the girl-child coordinator and those who were bent on getting justice for these girls,” he said.

Meanwhile, the Police Criminal Investigations Department has confirmed that the docket on the case had been forwarded to the Attorney General for advice.

Ghana News.title: Seven missing Ghanaian fishermen rescued in joint naval operation off Benin
Ghana News.content:
Seven Ghanaian fishers who were stranded at sea for more than a week have been rescued in a coordinated operation involving the navies of Ghana, Togo and Benin.

The Ministry of Fisheries and Aquaculture confirmed the successful rescue on Thursday, October 22, 2026, commending the three navies for their swift response and effective regional cooperation.

The operation followed a distress alert issued by the Ghana Navy and the Multinational Maritime Coordination Centre (MMCC-E) on Wednesday, October 21.

The Togolese Navy deployed its patrol vessel, OTI, which located the distressed fishing boat approximately three nautical miles off Grand-Popo in Beninese waters.

All seven crew members were rescued and provided with assistance, while the vessel was being towed towards the Ghana-Togo maritime boundary for handover to the Ghana Navy.

The rescue brings relief to the crew of Second Chance, whose disappearance had prompted a multi-agency search after the canoe failed to return from a fishing expedition off Axim in the Western Region.

The canoe departed Sekondi Fishing Harbour on October 9 but suffered an engine failure, leaving the crew drifting offshore.

One of the fishermen, Kwame Akyim, told TV3 News that strong tides had carried the canoe more than 120 nautical miles offshore. He described the crew's difficult conditions, saying they had limited food, relied on their catch for sustenance and resorted to boiling seawater for drinking.

The canoe's owner, Nana Kweku Atta, reported its disappearance to the Fishing Harbour Police Station in Sekondi on October 18, triggering a search involving the Marine Police, Ghana Navy, Ghana Maritime Authority, Fisheries Commission and fishing communities.

Western Regional Minister Joseph Nelson subsequently disclosed that contact had been established with the crew and that their location had been identified in neighbouring waters, prompting engagement with Togolese authorities to facilitate their safe return.

The Ministry of Fisheries and Aquaculture has reiterated the importance of safety at sea, urging fishers to check weather conditions before departure, wear life jackets, carry reliable communication equipment and strictly observe maritime safety advisories.

“Safety at sea is non-negotiable,” the Ministry stressed, warning that no fishing expedition was worth a human life.

It urged every fisher to take personal responsibility for safety and called for all necessary measures to ensure that those who venture out to sea return home safely.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Michigan Senate debate: Key takeaways from El-Sayed, Rogers clash
World.content:
El-Sayed and Rogers also tackle immigration in Michigan while Kansas candidates spar over Ukraine.

Share El-Sayed and Rogers clash over Trump, Iran war in Michigan Senate debate on social media

Candidates in two key United States Senate races have faced off in their final debates, less than two weeks before the November 3 midterm elections.

In Michigan, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers exchanged accusations on Wednesday regarding their political views and the US-Israel war on Iran.

In Kansas, Republican Senator Roger Marshall and his Democratic opponent, Adam Hamilton, disagreed about the rising price of diesel and President Donald Trump’s plan to import Russian fuel.

The results of both elections will influence which party ends up in control of the Senate. The Republicans currently dominate Congress’s upper chamber with 53 of its 100 seats. Democrats hold 45, and two senators are independents who caucus with the Democratic Party.

Here are some of the key takeaways from these debates:

Michigan

Rogers distances himself from Trump on some topics

Rogers questioned some of Trump’s tariffs, describing them as a “mixed bag”. While he supported taking steps to bring automobile manufacturing back to Michigan from China and Mexico, he questioned the impact of tariffs on Canada.

“I have stepped back and said maybe these Canadian tariffs were not well thought through,” Rogers said, referring to the close ties between the automobile industries of the two countries.

Michigan sits on the Canadian border and is the US state with the most car-manufacturing jobs.

Rogers insisted he would put Michigan’s interests first if elected.

“If it’s good for Michigan, I’m going to be for it. If it’s bad for Michigan, I’m going to be against it,” he said.



He pushed back against El-Sayed’s repeated references to Trump.

“The bingo game ought to be how many times can he put the word Trump in any answer that he has given in the last, whatever, 30 minutes,” he said. “It’s ridiculous.”

Iran takes centre stage

El-Sayed accused Rogers of supporting the war on Iran, which he blamed for rising fuel and food prices in the US.

He said he believed Iran had posed a threat to US national security but argued that the 2015 nuclear deal, negotiated under former President Barack Obama, had helped to contain it through diplomacy.

The Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA) was signed by Iran and several world powers, including the US. It placed restrictions on Iran’s nuclear programme, including strictly limiting uranium enrichment and compelling Iran to submit to international inspections, in exchange for sanctions relief.

Trump withdrew the US from the agreement in 2018, arguing that it failed to adequately address Iran’s nuclear ambitions and ballistic missile programme and support for armed groups in the region.

El-Sayed criticised Trump for abandoning the agreement during his first term and launching a war against Iran during his second.

El-Sayed argued that Americans have been left paying the price.

“The consequences of this war are that you are paying nearly $5 [per gallon, or 3.8 litres] in gas. You’re paying more in groceries because of the price of diesel,” he said.

According to the American Automobile Association (AAA), regular petrol in Michigan averaged $4.44 per gallon on Wednesday, up from $2.92 a year earlier. Diesel prices rose from $3.62 to $6.41 per gallon over the same period.

El-Sayed also sought to tie Rogers to Trump, who is expected to campaign in Michigan on Sunday.

“Donald Trump is on the ballot through Mike Rogers. They are hip-to-hip on this war, and you are paying the cost,” he said.

“Mike Rogers has been promoting this war since before he was in Congress. He’s got a war for everything, and he won’t back off the war now.”

Rogers calls on Democrats

Rogers appealed to Democrats who supported Haley Stevens, whom El-Sayed defeated in the Democratic primary.

“If you were a Haley Stevens voter and you came out of this and you said, ‘Man, I just can’t do it. He’s too extreme,’ well, guess what? You’ll have a home with us,” he said, and claimed that a growing number of Democrats are now backing his campaign.

One of the more contentious moments of the debate came when Rogers suggested El-Sayed had the same supporters as groups like Hamas, allegations El-Sayed pushed back against.



“You can grin and you can smile and you can talk real pretty, but I’m going to tell you what, that is a risk to our national security,” Rogers said. He told reporters after the debate that he questions whether El-Sayed could get a security clearance for senators if he’s elected.

El-Sayed called the allegations “shameful”.

El-Sayed and Rogers clash over immigration and ICE

Immigration sparked another heated exchange.

Rogers defended the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown, arguing that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) operations had helped reduce crime.

“We should continue to do that. Find those folks who are committing crimes and get them the heck out of the country,” Rogers said.

El-Sayed criticised ICE’s tactics, accusing Rogers of supporting raids on schools, workplaces and places of worship.

“He supports ICE running through your streets. They don’t have to tell you who they are. They don’t have to tell you why they’re there,” El-Sayed said.

“I believe that we don’t need ICE,” he added.

Kansas

Marshall blames Ukraine war for high diesel prices

Marshall said Russia’s war on Ukraine rather than the Iran war was responsible for soaring diesel prices during his final debate with his Democratic challenger.

The Republican’s comments echoed Trump’s recent criticism of Ukraine, including his claim that Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries have caused rising fuel costs.

Trump has agreed a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to release stocks of Russian diesel to the US and global markets to ease prices, an idea Marshall greeted with some reservations.

“It doesn’t sound like a great idea,” Marshall said. But he added: “If this brings Russia to the bargaining table and it ends the war, then I am all for it right now.”

Hamilton responded angrily: “What you said just now is you’re going to sell out our friends in Ukraine. That’s not OK.”

Diesel prices have become a key campaign issue in Kansas, where farmers depend heavily on the fuel. According to AAA, diesel averaged $6.32 a gallon this week in the state, compared with $3.62 a year earlier.

Hamilton blamed the price rises on Trump’s war on Iran and called for a temporary suspension of federal fuel taxes. Marshall has also said he wants the war to end soon but has not committed to trying to force Trump to end it.

ICE raids divide Kansas candidates

Hamilton criticised recent ICE raids while Marshall defended Trump’s border policies.

Both candidates expressed cautious support for making E-Verify, a system that allows employers to check whether workers are legally authorised to work in the US, mandatory for businesses.

“I think it’s a good idea. Of course, the devil’s in the details,” Marshall said, arguing that Republicans had secured the border and could now focus on fixing the immigration system.

Hamilton challenged Marshall, who had mentioned delivering babies for undocumented parents during his medical career.



“Did you also call ICE and ask them to be taken away? What did you do with these people?” Hamilton asked.

“You had compassion for them in delivering these children, but then you support quotas. They’re going to have people taken away. Hutchinson, Kansas, I was there. There was a preschool teacher arrested in front of her children,” he added.

Hamilton also criticised recent ICE raids in southwestern Kansas, warning that they were frightening workers and disrupting the agricultural industry.

“People are terrified when ICE shows up because they’ve been militarised, politicised, and so people don’t show up at work,” he said.

“We don’t want people terrified in our communities.”

Selling weapons to Israel

Hamilton criticised the use of US weapons in Gaza while Marshall defended Washington’s alliance with Israel.

Hamilton said he supported providing Israel with defensive weapons but opposed supplying bombs used in attacks on densely populated areas.

“When you see entire cities flattened in Gaza, now we’re not just talking about rooting out Hamas,” Hamilton said.

“They’re using our aid to buy our weapons and then dropping them on innocent civilians. That’s just not OK. It’s not decent. It’s not who we are as Americans.”

Marshall defended Israel as one of Washington’s closest allies and was asked whether there were circumstances in which he would block a weapons sale.

“I’m sure there is. I’m not sure what it would be,” Marshall said.

Marshall stressed the importance of strong military alliances but said Washington should prioritise domestic concerns.

“I want to make sure that our borders are secure. Let’s take care of things at home first,” he said.

World.title: Israeli forces kill disabled man in southern Syria raid, state media says
World.content:
Civilian with a disability shot dead by Israeli forces during raid in Jamla, in western Deraa countryside, SANA reports.

Share Israeli forces kill disabled man in southern Syria raid, state media says on social media

Israeli forces have killed a man with a disability during a raid in Syria’s southern Deraa governorate, Syria’s state news agency SANA reported.

The civilian was shot dead early on Thursday in the village of Jamla in Daraa’s western countryside, where Israeli forces had deployed snipers on rooftops, SANA reported.

The victim’s body was brought to Deraa National Hospital, the agency added.

The Israeli military did not immediately comment on the report.

Since Syria’s longtime ruler Bashar al-Assad was removed in December 2024, the Israeli army has waged hundreds of strikes in the country and routinely moved forces into Syrian territory.

Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa has condemned Israel’s “aggressions”, saying they “undermine peace and security”.

In recent days, Israeli forces have reportedly carried out raids and destroyed olive groves in Quneitra province, near Deraa.

In one raid on Thursday, in the village of Turnejeh in the Quneitra countryside, Israeli forces searched homes and detained one person, according to SANA.

Earlier in the week, Israeli forces destroyed trees in a large field by the village of Saida, the agency reported.

Syria’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Sunday condemned “the intensification of incursions by the Israeli occupation” in Quneitra and Deraa.

Israeli officials have repeatedly said they plan to keep troops in what they call a “security zone” in southern Syria.

The two countries have opened negotiations for a security agreement, but the talks have been largely stalled since the outbreak of the US-Israel war on Iran in February.

World.title: Can European leaders fix the cost-of-living crisis?
World.content:
Across Europe, an autumn of anger is taking hold.

In France, student protests over overcrowded classrooms and teacher shortages have grown into a broader public outcry.

In recent weeks, separate protests have also erupted in Belgium, Italy, Portugal, Spain and Albania.

The grievances differ, from unaffordable housing and low wages to rising fuel costs, education and political accountability.

But the frustration is increasingly shared: paying more, getting less, and struggling to afford a decent life, even with a job.

Governments face demands for relief while wrestling with high debt, rising borrowing costs and, in several countries, looming elections.
