World.title: ‘Facebook’s wrongdoing’: Why has Meta been fined $25bn in New Mexico?
World.content:
The tech giant has been accused of misleading users regarding data privacy linked to the Cambridge Analytica scandal.

Share ‘Facebook’s wrongdoing’: Why has Meta been fined $25bn in New Mexico? on social media

A judge in New Mexico has ordered Meta Platforms to pay the US state $25bn after a court found the company intentionally misled consumers about the privacy of their data.

“Facebook’s wrongdoing – over the course of years and systematically broadcast to the public – goes to ⁠the heart of Facebook’s core business practices,” Judge Francis Mathew wrote in his order, which came more than three weeks after the verdict.

The judge found that a penalty of more than $219bn was warranted based on state law, but he reduced the figure to $25bn.

New Mexico Attorney General Raul Torrez said it was one of the largest, if not the largest, single state verdict against ⁠a company in United States history.

CJ Mahoney, Meta’s chief legal officer, said the company was confident it would win on appeal.

“This ruling, and the Attorney General’s approach to this enforcement, makes it all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico,” Mahoney said in a statement. “At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech ‌to enforce new rules for what people can say online.”

What is the lawsuit about?

New Mexico’s attorney general sued Meta in 2021 following revelations that Cambridge Analytica had harvested personal data from as many as 87 million Facebook users through a third-party app.

Cambridge Analytica, a now-defunct British political consulting firm, harvested Facebook data to generate targeted political s during the 2016 election season, when it worked for Donald Trump’s successful presidential campaign.



The state accused Meta of lying to Facebook users in New Mexico about who had access to their data and its handling of hate speech ⁠and misinformation posted on the platform.

Lawyers for the state cited a 2010 Washington Post op-ed in which Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg wrote that the company did not sell user data.

They alleged the company knew third parties had broad access to users’ data and tolerated hate speech ⁠or other harmful content when it benefitted the company’s bottom line.

Torrez, New Mexico’s attorney general, said the judgement “should be a signal, an unambiguous message, to Silicon Valley”.

Is Meta facing other lawsuits?

Meta is facing thousands of lawsuits and pressure from lawmakers over the impact of Instagram and Facebook on teen mental health.

A trial brought by a coalition of state attorneys general in a California federal court began in August over claims the company engineered Facebook and Instagram to be addictive to children, which could expose the company to huge damages and force it to make sweeping changes to its platforms.

It will also address claims by 29 states that the company illegally collected and used children’s data in violation of federal law.

Six other states settled their lawsuits related to Cambridge Analytica for $459m, as part of a $17bn multistate ‌settlement Meta reached in August to resolve states’ claims that the company’s platforms had harmed teen mental health.

Earlier this year, New Mexico won $942m in two trials against Meta over claims it ⁠facilitated sexual exploitation of young people on Instagram and Facebook and misled consumers about the platforms’ safety.

The American Economic Liberties Project, a nonprofit that supports stronger policies towards corporations, said the latest fine of $25bn is “a drop in the bucket for Meta”, but demonstrates that people want accountability.

“Right now, they are rolling out Muse, an AI assistant encouraging people to trust it with everything from their bank accounts to their medical information,” the nonprofit’s Executive Director Nidhi Hegde said. “Which is why we need more enforcers with courage and laws with actual teeth to rein them in.”

World.title: Fighting rages in Yemen’s Taiz as UN warns nearly 260,000 displaced
World.content:
Share Fighting rages in Yemen’s Taiz as UN warns nearly 260,000 displaced on social media

Fighting has intensified in Yemen’s Taiz province between forces loyal to the country’s internationally recognised government and the Houthis, as the United Nations warns that thousands of civilians are being uprooted.

Government forces spokesperson Majid al-Nazili said on Wednesday that they launched 835 targeting operations against the Houthis, known as Ansar Allah, killing or injuring 285 of the armed group’s members and destroying its battle tanks and weapons stores.

He said intense clashes also took place in the strategic highlands of Jabal Han in western Taiz, which overlook areas connecting the province to the Yemeni government’s Aden base. Heavy fighting was reported in the Dhubab and al-Masrakh districts.

A source in the Yemeni government’s military told Al Jazeera that its air raids had struck Houthi gatherings and infrastructure in the Maafar directorate, south of Taiz.

Yemen’s government later threatened to expand attacks to target rallies staged by the Houthis, claiming the group uses those events to recruit children into combat.

In a statement on Thursday, the ministry of defence warned civilians in Houthi-held areas to avoid any Houthi rallies or “cultural courses”, saying the gatherings would be viewed as legitimate military targets.

Rising displacement

As fighting rages between the Saudi Arabia-backed government forces and the Iran-aligned Houthis, the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said almost 260,000 people have been displaced since August. About half of them have taken refuge in Taiz, where fighting is now concentrated, the agency said.



In a report released late on Wednesday, OCHA said the UN Human Rights Office (OHCHR) has verified 251 civilian casualties, including 57 people killed and 194 injured. Half of those killed were children.

“Despite extremely difficult conditions,” humanitarian partners have reached more than 174,000 displaced people since August, “nearly six in 10 displaced households,” providing food, hygiene kits and emergency cash in the first days after they were uprooted, OCHA said.

“Newly displaced families say that their most pressing need is shelter, followed by food and cash,” OCHA said.

Yemen’s Ministry of Education earlier announced that more than 2.5 million children are out of school because of the conflict.

Widening war

The latest reports come as Yemen’s government forces press on with their “Dawn of Yemen” counteroffensive launched earlier this month to recapture Houthi-held areas, including the capital, Sanaa, with support from the Saudi-led coalition.

The operation followed the Houthis’ declaration of a blockade on Saudi Arabia in the crucial Bab al-Mandeb strait in July, as well as lightning offensives that saw the group swiftly seize strategic areas along Yemen’s Red Sea coast.

The Houthis have also launched attacks on targets in Saudi Arabia, striking the kingdom’s airports in what analysts say is a pressure campaign to force a political resolution. Houthi forces say the strikes are in retaliation for Saudi Arabia’s longstanding restrictions on Houthi-controlled airports and seaports, including Sanaa airport.

Saudi Arabia’s Authority of Civil Aviation said on Thursday that the death toll has risen to two following a Houthi strike on the King Fahd airport in Dammam on Wednesday evening.

Meanwhile, the US State Department said on Wednesday that it ordered non-essential staff and family members at its embassy in Riyadh to leave the country, raising fears of further escalation.

The embassy was already badly damaged at the onset of the US-Israel war on Iran and had been operating on a lean rota of staff, although some had recently returned.

In a new travel alert, the State Department warned Americans that “the hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area”.

In Yemen, government forces accused the Houthis of striking the Aden and al-Rayyan airports on Wednesday. The head of the governing Presidential Leadership Council, Rashad Al-Alimi, condemned the strikes and called on the international community to proscribe the group as a “terrorist” organisation.



Yemen has been engulfed in conflict since the Houthis seized Sanaa and several other provinces in 2014, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene in March 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government.

A 2022 UN-brokered truce collapsed in July, as the Houthis announced a blockade on Saudi ports.

The Houthis control much of northern and western Yemen, while government forces and their allies hold Aden and large parts of the country’s southern and eastern provinces.

World.title: Israeli elections: Is it just right wing versus right?
World.content:
Israeli elections: Is it just right wing versus right?

NewsFeed Israeli elections: Is it just right wing versus right?

Benjamin Netanyahu’s opponents are promising to shake up Israeli politics, but how different are their policies? Is Israel’s election simply a contest between right and right? Al Jazeera’s Mohammad Saleh examines the candidates running in Israel’s 27 October elections.

World.title: How Arab parties could hold critical balance of power in Israeli election
World.content:
At rush hour in Nazareth, the largest Arab-majority city in Israel, students are handing out leaflets by the roadside urging motorists to vote in next week's closely fought, general election. Polls indicate that Arab parties could be left holding a critical balance of power.

Disaffection has often driven down past turnout among Arab Israelis - who account for about a fifth of the population and often describe themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel. But this election, there is a strong push to get rid of the most right-wing governing coalition in the country's history - an alliance between veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties.

"I see it as our duty to bring down this extremist government. They treat us as second-class," says Arkan Badran, 23, who is with the students giving out flyers. "I call on all young men and women to vote for Arab lists, which represent us, because this is our future."

World.title: Celebrity shark guided out of South Korea canal refuses to swim out to sea
World.content:
A famed dusky shark in South Korea is still lingering near a canal that it was guided out of on Wednesday.

The shark, nicknamed Bukangi, became an unlikely sensation after it was spotted swimming in a canal in the south-eastern port city of Busan last month. For weeks, rescuers tried in vain to get it back to the open sea using large nets.

On Thursday, authorities said they had reinforced barriers to prevent Bukangi from returning. But it has yet to swim out into the open sea, and has been circling back repeatedly to the mouth of the waterway.

Its rescue prompted mixed reactions in Busan, where some said the shark should stay while others felt it was better for it to go.

In a livestreamed operation on Wednesday, rescue workers took more than eight hours to delicately guide the three-metre-long (10ft) shark with a net towards open water in a harbour.

Hundreds of adoring fans gathered at the park overlooking the canal, cheering and waving goodbye to the shark.

But then, on Thursday morning, Bukangi reportedly swam back into the canal after breaking through a barrier installed by authorities.

For some time, Bukangi was trapped in a tight space between two layers of nets in the canal.

Rescuers freed it by removing the outer layer, and have since fortified the remaining layer of nets to prevent it from going back in.

Since then, authorities said, Bukangi has been swimming further out but keeps circling back.

A government official told the BBC on Thursday afternoon that rescuers had concluded their operations to free the shark.

World.title: Two killed in attack on airport in eastern Saudi Arabia, authorities say
World.content:
Two people were killed and eight others injured in an attack on an airport in Dammam, eastern Saudi Arabia on Wednesday evening, the kingdom's General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) says.

Those killed at King Fahd International Airport were a Saudi citizen and an Indian resident, while the injured were Saudi, Indian, Yemeni, Bangladeshi and Nepalese nationals.

The GACA did not say what type of attack occurred, but Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi movement has repeatedly targeted the kingdom's airports with drones and missiles.

On Wednesday morning, two people were killed by debris from a drone that was intercepted over Eastern Province, where Dammam is located, the Saudi energy ministry said.

The ministry said the drone was intercepted as it attempted to target a processing facility owned by Saudi Arabia's state oil company Aramco in the Shaybeh oil field, where a contractor's vehicle was set ablaze.

It identified the dead as residents from the Philippines and Nepal.

Another four drones were also intercepted on Wednesday night, according to the Saudi-led coalition that is supporting the Yemeni government in its war against the Houthis.

There was no immediate comment from the Houthis, but they have previously said they are attacking Saudi airports, energy facilities and military bases in retaliation for deadly Saudi air strikes on the territory they control in western Yemen.

World.title: Police investigate Married at First Sight Australia after 'inappropriate' allegations
World.content:
Married at First Sight Australia is facing fresh controversy after police launched an investigation into the hit reality TV show.

New South Wales told BBC News that inquiries had taken place "following a report of inappropriate content being shared".

Channel Nine, which broadcasts Married at First Sight Australia, confirmed that it was "aware of a police investigation" involving the show's production company.

It is the latest blow for the show, after a BBC News investigation earlier this year into MAFS Australia revealed cast members said they had not been told their partners had previous drug and violence convictions.

Those revelations led to a warning from Australia's media watchdog, which called them "serious and disturbing".

The British version of Married at First Sight, known to many as MAFS UK, was separately plunged into crisis in May after BBC Panorama reported rape allegations from two female cast members - allegations the men involved have denied.

MAFS UK is made by a different production company to the Australian version.

World.title: El Salvador's president threatens Haitian gangs over military hostages
World.content:
El Salvador's president has said he has launched a military operation to rescue four air force personnel who have been missing in Haiti since Sunday.

Nayib Bukele wrote in a post on X that Wednesday's attack was "nothing" compared with what would happen if all the hostages - who he said were not combatants - were not returned alive.

They went missing after being ambushed by "heavily armed criminal groups," El Salvador's armed forces said. The ambush occurred in Croix-des-Bouquets, an area controlled by armed groups.

They were part of the so-called Gang Suppression Force (GSF), approved by the United Nations Security Council earlier this month, to tackle escalating gang violence in Haiti.

According to Bukele, the mission consisted of pilots and technical personnel, whose primary jobs were to "carry out medical evacuations and save lives, not to wage war".

His post said the Salvadoran military operation's single objective was to bring the four men back home alive.

He added that if all four were returned alive, without being harmed, "everything will go back to how it was before the kidnapping".

Bukele added they were kidnapped "in a cowardly manner" while returning after buying food at a market in the area.

A statement released by the Armed Forces of El Salvador on Sunday said the group was ambushed while travelling back to its camp in an armoured vehicle, which caught fire after being hit by explosives.

So far, no gang has claimed responsibility for the attack.

Salvadoran helicopters were deployed to assist, with multiple attempts to make an approach by land and air hampered by fighting and local security conditions, the armed forces said.

On Wednesday, before Bukele announced the launch of the military operation, the GSF said it was searching for the four missing personnel following the attack.

It added that it had "engaged armed gang elements, with helicopter support" and that early reports had indicated that several gang members were killed.

Earlier this week, the UN warned that Haiti's armed gangs were adapting to intensified security conditions, saying that they were "stepping up reprisals against civilians and extending their reach into rural areas".

Haiti has not held elections since 2016, and two weeks ago postponed presidential and legislative elections - scheduled for 13 December - indefinitely.

The country has been wracked by economic chaos, a political vacuum and increasingly violent gang warfare since its president was assassinated in 2021.

More than 5,500 people were killed in gang-related violence in Haiti in 2024. Armed gangs currently control about 85% of the capital, Port-au-Prince.

World.title: Two European women held captive for more than a year in Niger freed in Libya
World.content:
Two women - a Swiss and an Austrian â have been freed after more than a year in captivity in Niger and handed over to authorities in the Libyan city of Benghazi.

Austrian national Eva Gretzmacher, 76, and Swiss Claudia Abbt, 69, were kidnapped separately in the northern Nigerien city of Agadez in January and April last year.

No details have been given about who was holding them or their demands, although some reports have previously linked the kidnapping to Islamic State militants. The circumstances of their release were not disclosed.

Libyan officials were reported as saying the women would be handed over to authorities in their respective countries after necessary procedures were completed.

Libya's al-Masar TV showed the two women entering what looks like an ambulance and later being attended to by a health worker.

Speaking in French, the women thanked Khalifa Haftar, military commander of eastern Libya, and his son, Saddam Haftar, for their release.

Gretzmacher was an aid worker who had lived for many years in Niger, while Abbt had spent several years living and working as a community worker in Agadez.

A plane was expected to leave Benghazi on Thursday, first stopping in Vienna to transfer Gretzmacher to Austrian authorities before continuing to Switzerland with Abbt, privately owned Air Info Agadez news outlet reported.

Libya has struggled to recover from the chaos that followed the 2011 Nato-backed uprising that toppled long-time ruler Muammar Gaddafi.

It is split between two administrations - one in the east backed by Haftar, and the other in the west in the capital Tripoli, led by Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah.

Under Gaddafi, many ethnic Tuaregs from Mali and Niger were recruited to join armed groups loyal to him in Libya. After he was killed, many went home. Analysts say this has been a major factor in the spread of instability in the Sahel region.

Niger and its neighbours have faced years of jihadist violence, including kidnappings and deadly attacks, carried out by different groups linked to al-Qaeda and Islamic State.

The country has been under military control since 2023 when Gen Abdourahmane Tchiani deposed the country's elected President, Mohamed Bazoum.

World.title: Missiles hit Kyiv after Russia agrees to US call to resume Ukraine peace talks
World.content:
Ukraine's capital has come under a new missile attack, hours after Russia said it was "ready in principle" to resume peace talks and the US president said the world was "the closest we've been" to ending the war.

Several houses were hit on Wednesday night, injuring six people, Kyiv Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said.

The attack came amid a new diplomatic push led by Donald Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Witkoff met Russia's President Vladimir Putin in the city of St Petersburg on Wednesday - a day after meeting Ukraine's leader.

Three-way talks were paused in February, after which Russia stepped up attacks as Ukraine ran out of Western-supplied interceptors to defend against missiles.

Speaking on Wednesday, Trump said: "The other day I was talking to Vladimir Putin about settling his war with Ukraine, which I think we're getting closer to, by the way, maybe now the closest we've been."

The US president has so far failed to bring the Russia-Ukraine war to an end despite his repeated comments that he would be able to achieve this.

World.title: How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?
World.content:
Current polling puts incumbent Benjamin Netanyahu in a tight race with Gadi Eisenkot, a former head of the Israel Defense Forces, to become prime minister.

Eisenkot's popularity stems partly from his military credentials and his relative newness in politics, having formed his Yashar Party only last year.

He lost his son, a soldier, in the first months of the Gaza war, and served in Israel's war cabinet under Netanyahu until resigning in 2024 over disagreements about the conflict. He has built his campaign on calls for accountability over the security failures that led to 7 October.

Other opposition leaders include former prime minister Naftali Bennett and Avigdor Lieberman - both right-wingers who take hardline positions on security and advocate permanent Israeli control over much of the occupied West Bank - and Yair Golan, a left-winger who supports Israel's withdrawal from large parts of the territory. Despite their differences, they could work with Eisenkot to form a government.

Netanyahu's current government is the most right-wing in Israel's history. In order to remain in power, he will likely have to rely on the support of some of his existing far-right coalition partners. Some hold ultra-nationalist positions, such as calling for Israel to annex the West Bank and for the "migration" of Palestinians from Gaza - which could amount to the forced displacement of civilians. Some members of Netanyahu's own Likud party have also called for Palestinian "migration" from the territory.

There are two Arab party blocs in the running too, as about one-fifth of Israel's population is Arab - many of whom describe themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel. In theory, they could prove kingmakers. But all but one of the leading Jewish parties have ruled out working with them.

World.title: Premium Times publisher, Falana, to headline DevReporting LG documentary screening
World.content:
Dapo Olorunyomi, publisher of PREMIUM TIMES and Chief Executive Officer of the Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID), will chair the public screening of “LG Billions in the Dark”, an investigative documentary examining the prolonged local government leadership crisis in Osun State.

The screening, scheduled for Thursday, 29 October, at the University of Lagos (UNILAG), will feature human rights lawyer and Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Femi Falana, as keynote speaker.

According to a statement from DevReporting, Mr Falana will speak on “Accountability, Resources and Citizen Voices: Building Local Governments that Work for the People,” focusing on local government autonomy, public resource management, citizens’ rights and accountability at the grassroots.

“Nigeria’s local governments are constitutionally recognised as the tier of government closest to citizens, with responsibilities that directly affect everyday life, including primary healthcare, basic infrastructure, sanitation and other essential services,” it noted.

“However, concerns over financial control, political interference and the capacity of councils to function independently have remained central to debates about local governance in the country.”

Panel discussion

The screening will feature a panel discussion involving public officials, civil society leaders, governance experts, academics and development practitioners.

The panellists include Osun State Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Dosu Babatunde; Executive Director of the Resource Centre for Human Rights and Civic Education (CHRICED), Zikirullahi Ibrahim; and Executive Director of Spaces for Change, Victoria Ibezim-Ohaeri.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Others are Joshua Osiyemi, Head of Tracka at BudgIT; Vera Amaechi, a lecturer in the Department of Political Science at the University of Lagos; and Bukola Adebayo, Senior Multimedia Strategist at DevReporting.

Speaking ahead of the event, DevReporting Team Lead, Mojeed Alabi, said the documentary reflects the organisation’s commitment to public-interest journalism and examining governance issues with direct consequences for citizens.

DRAF unveiling

The event will also feature the official unveiling of the Development Reporting Africa Foundation (DRAF) and a fundraising initiative to support the foundation’s public-interest development reporting work.

“DRAF is a nonprofit initiative established to strengthen development reporting, generate and communicate evidence, promote public engagement and advance accountability on issues affecting communities across Africa,” Mr Alabi said.

DevReporting is also developing a civic education and youth engagement initiative that will take the documentary to tertiary institutions across Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones.

The initiative will combine campus screenings, training, mentorship and youth-led accountability projects to deepen students’ understanding of local government administration, public finance and citizen participation.

According to DevReporting, the initiative is aimed at encouraging more young Nigerians to take an interest in how local governments are funded, how public resources are spent and how citizens can demand improved services.

The documentary was produced with support from the Royal Norwegian Embassy through CJID.

DevReporting is a media and cinematic platform focused on development issues across Nigeria and Africa. It produces investigative reports and multimedia stories and undertakes research and media capacity development to promote transparency, accountability and inclusive development.

World.title: IRGC threatens invasion of neighbours that attack Iran
World.content:
The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has threatened “to invade” any country in the Middle East that attacks Iran as tensions in the region rise.

The IRGC spokesperson, Hossein Mohebi, on Wednesday, said Iran’s security doctrine has become “offensive and asymmetrical.”

Al Jazeera reported that Mr Mohebi said Iran’s defence doctrine was previously defensive but shifted to ‘offensive and asymmetrical’ because of its realities.

“We announced that if a country attacked us, we would respond to it,” he said.

“Now, we say if a country attacks us, we will respond to it, and we will invade. Our doctrine will no longer be only offensive and will become asymmetrical. We will attack the enemy in such a way that it will understand the intensity of our action.”

The US-Iran war, now over seven months, continued to heighten tension in the Middle East, with persistent strike exchanges, negotiations, and diplomatic pressure failing to bring an end to the war.

The US and Iran remain divided over the control of the Strait of Hormuz, sanction relief and Iranian uranium enrichment.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said the country is prepared to give diplomacy another chance. But this is dependent on “strong evidence of a sincere desire by the US to build trust and reach a just solution.”

“If the US chooses war over diplomacy, it’ll certainly result in an even greater strategic failure.”

The IRGC has also threatened to attack US bases in the region if tankers continue to pass through the waterway illegally.

The armed forces said it will extend “confrontation to US bases” in the region if Washington continues to urge “vessels to pass through mined waterways illegally.”

It also declared that its navy struck four ships involved in oil transfers in the Gulf, and that three other vessels caught fire after hitting mines near the Strait of Hormuz.

“The US aggressor military must understand that, if this continues, the scope of confrontation will extend to the bases of the aggressors in the region. This is a serious warning,” it said.

Mr Mohebi also taunted the United States over the Strait of Hormuz, saying the repercussions would influence the upcoming midterm elections for President Trump’s Republican Party.

“The Strait of Hormuz has squeezed the economic and political throat of the United States,” he said

Meanwhile, Iran called the US naval blockade of Iran “a flagrant violation” of international law and the UN Charter, in a letter to UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and Security Council President Aglaia Balta.

ALSO READ: Iran urges Saudi Arabia to pursue diplomacy with Houthis

The letter, written by Iran’s ambassador to the United Nations, Gholam Hossein, asked the global organisation to urge the US to immediately cease its military aggression against Iran and lift the maritime blockade.

He asked that the UN recognise that Washington remains internationally responsible for its “internationally wrongful acts, including its military aggression” and any “continuing violations of international law, and that the obligations to cease wrongful conduct and to make full reparation remain applicable in accordance with the law of State responsibility.”

World.title: CJID launches Living Archives Initiative, honours veteran journalist Lade Bonuola (LIVE UPDATES)
World.content:
The Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID) is launching its Living Archives Initiative in Lagos, alongside a digital platform aimed at preserving Africa’s media history.

The event will also feature the unveiling of ‘Ladbone: A Life in Print,’ a collection of essays honouring veteran journalist Lade Bonuola, popularly known as Ladbone, as he marks his 80th birthday.

The initiative seeks to preserve and make accessible historical newspaper records, photographs, broadcast recordings and personal accounts documenting the lives and contributions of people who have shaped journalism across Africa.

Mr Bonuola, whose journalism career spans more than five decades, began at the Daily Times before becoming the pioneer editor and managing director of The Guardian. He also co-founded The Comet newspaper in 1999 and held senior editorial positions at other media organisations.

The book features contributions from more than 80 editors, media managers, academics, political figures and industry experts, reflecting on his career and the evolution of Nigerian journalism.

CJID said the digital platform would serve journalists, researchers, students and the public, providing access to historical records that could inform discussions on press freedom, professional standards and democratic development.

The programme will feature panel discussions, a book review and the formal unveiling of the anthology.

Follow PREMIUM TIMES for live updates of the event.

World.title: New project to scrutinise Akwa Ibom budgets for gender inequality
World.content:
A new youth-led initiative will analyse Akwa Ibom State’s budgets over three fiscal years to determine whether public spending adequately addresses the needs of women, girls and vulnerable groups, in the face of persistent concerns over the state’s fiscal transparency.

The project, Budget as Policy: Advancing Gender Justice through Fiscal Analysis, will examine allocations and expenditure in health, education, water, sanitation and hygiene, and women’s economic empowerment.

It is being implemented by Lucy Eyo, a civil society advocate and development communication specialist, with support from the Nigerian Youth Futures Fund.

According to a statement announcing the initiative, the analysis will assess spending trends, identify funding gaps in critical social sectors and determine the extent to which gender considerations are reflected in the state’s budgetary decisions.

The findings are expected to inform engagement between civil society organisations, the media and government stakeholders on how public resources are allocated and spent.

“Budgets show a government’s real priorities,” Ms Eyo said.

“This project will show where public money is going, where the gaps are, and what must change so that women, girls and communities benefit fairly from public spending.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The project was launched on 16 October at an inception meeting attended by civil society representatives and media practitioners expected to support its implementation. Participants were briefed on its objectives, planned activities and expected outcomes and expressed their willingness to support the initiative.

Government budgets determine whether health facilities receive adequate funding, schools have access to safe water and sanitation, and programmes designed to improve women’s economic opportunities and protect vulnerable groups receive the resources needed to function.

The initiative comes at a time of questions about the transparency of Akwa Ibom’s public finances under Governor Umo Eno.

PREMIUM TIMES reported in July that the state government had received at least N2.934 trillion in public revenue between May 2023 and June 2026, but its published financial records lacked detailed capital expenditure schedules needed to independently track spending on projects and programmes.

The newspaper also reported in September that the state’s second-quarter 2026 budget implementation report provided insufficient details for citizens to see how public funds had been spent.

These gaps in fiscal disclosure complicate efforts to assess whether approved allocations translate into services and infrastructure for residents, including women and children who depend heavily on publicly funded health, education, water and sanitation services.

PREMIUM TIMES has also reported that Akwa Ibom allocated N61.61 billion, representing 3.73 per cent of its N1.65 trillion budget, to education in 2025. The absence of a publicly available, comprehensive budget performance report for that year made it difficult to assess the extent to which the allocation was implemented.

The new initiative will examine the state’s budgets over three fiscal years of 2024 through 2026.

Its findings are expected to provide civil society groups and journalists with evidence to question spending priorities, advocate more equitable resource allocation and press for improved accountability in the delivery of essential public services.

The project’s stated objectives include strengthening gender-responsive planning, budgeting and expenditure in the social sector and providing a stronger evidence base for engagement with the state government.

However, the initiative’s eventual impact will depend partly on the availability of sufficiently detailed public financial records and the willingness of government institutions to respond to evidence-based recommendations.

World.title: “It’s not debatable, we can’t go back,” Mbah backs Tinubu on fuel subsidy removal
World.content:
The Governor of Enug State, Peter Mbah, has doubled down in his support for the removal of fuel subsidy by President Bola Tinubu’s administration, saying it was undebatable and inconceivable for anyone to imagine a return to the old order.

Mbah spoke at the “Meet the Candidates” town hall meeting organised by Afia TV in Enugu on Wednesday, where he also said that his administration had delivered good governance to the people of the state across all sectors.

He described it as a pathetic misconception of the country’s situation and the direction it was headed for anyone to talk about the reintroduction of fuel subsidy.

“If you reintroduce fuel subsidy today, we will lose ten times whatever we are currently trying to gain in terms of the removal of subsidy. The poverty rate that you are going to experience will be very high because the naira would be automatically devalued.

“We cannot go back to subsidy. And I do not think it is in the interest of the country for us to even debate that.

“Again, we should not even debate it because we do not want to send a signal to prospective investors that we are contemplating it. That would take us back. It is going to create panic in the system. It is going to get investors to pull back.

“Those that are coming in today to invest in that sector will become jittery. So, it is not even a subject to debate. It is something that we have moved on from, and we should be thinking about how to ensure that the natural benefits cascade to the households, create jobs and generate wealth for our people,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the nation should focus on how to further encourage private capital to flow, noting the growth the nation had experienced in the stock exchange space.

He added that Tinubu’s policies had stabilised the macro indicators, thus encouraging foreign direct investment.

“You can see quite a lot of funds coming into our country, not just portfolio investments, but also direct investments. It is also going to strengthen because the macro indicators are right,” he stated.

Mbah maintained that whereas fuel subsidy removal enables the government to target the less privileged, fuel subsidy as earlier practised benefited the rich more.

“By the way, I do not think the subsidy we practised before the President removed it was even the right one for the country because even the people we were looking at benefiting from it were only insignificantly benefiting from it. It was largely beneficial to our wealthy folks.

“But now, you can almost notice that the government is doing that in targeting the poor, using proceeds from subsidy removal. The government is aggressive on cash transfers. There is also the programme where the government is targeting 1,000 persons per ward across the entire country to be able to provide seed capital for them to become productive,” he added.

Meanwhile, on his stewardship so far, Mbah said his administration had kept faith with the people of Enugu State, delivering good governance across all sectors in line with his campaign manifesto.

He said the people of the state only needed to imagine where the state was before his inauguration as governor and where it is currently headed.

“Let us imagine the Enugu we knew four years ago. Let us just imagine an Enugu without Hotel Presidential. Let us imagine an Enugu without the International Conference Centre. Let us imagine an Enugu without Enugu Air. Let us imagine Enugu without the transport terminals, the 268 Smart Green Schools, 260 Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centres.

“You do not want them to imagine an Enugu without the International Hospital. You do not want them to imagine an Enugu without the CNG buses, the Nigergas. I think the list is endless.

“But I even think that we can stretch that imagination further because the work ahead will be more profound. Just imagine an Enugu where our children are receiving education that prepares them for the world because they have been imbued with evolving 21st-century skills. Imagine again an Enugu where you do not have any part of the city with an unpaved road.

“Also, imagine an Enugu in four years’ time that generates 660 megawatts of electricity; where we are able to provide 24-hour power supply; where you cannot come into your house and have the light off; and where people can run their businesses for a whole week without worrying about the cost of diesel. Just imagine an Enugu where you generate electricity and the people of Enugu are buying that at 120 naira because they own the coal that feeds the power plant.

“Imagine an Enugu where you now have to ride, not just on our CNG buses, but you have the monorail that can take you from point A to point B. Imagine an Enugu where you can fly from here to the United Kingdom, to the United States and other parts of the world,” he charged the electorate.

He urged the people to keep faith with the journey of greatness, growth and development, defending the gains of his first term and guaranteeing the promises of his second term by working for his re-election.

“If these imaginations capture our fancy, then we have a duty to fight for it. We do have a duty to continue to make sure that the bar does not come down and that the standard we have set in Enugu is sustained,” he concluded.

World.title: Police recover 350 ammunition rounds from commercial bus – Official
World.content:
The Police in EdoState said they have arrested suspects in separate murder, sexual abuse, armed robbery and cultism cases, including four men allegedly connected to the theft of property worth more than N400 million from a communications complex in Auchi.

The command also said it recovered 350 rounds of ammunition of different calibres and arrested two officials of a transport company after intercepting a bus on the Benin-Lagos Road.

The Commissioner of Police in Edo State, Patrick Daaor, disclosed these in a press briefing posted on the command’s Facebook page on Wednesday.

According to Mr Daaor, the arrests and recoveries resulted from intelligence-led operations, stop-and-search activities and patrols across the state.

In one of the murder cases, the police said a woman was allegedly killed, one of her breasts severed and her body dumped by the roadside. Two suspects have been arrested in connection with murder cases, although the police did not disclose their identities or provide further details about the circumstances of the woman’s death.

The command said investigations were ongoing and the suspects would be charged to court.

N400m robbery

The police said the Auchi Area Command dismantled a criminal syndicate allegedly responsible for a robbery at the Paparazzi Communication Complex in Auchi on 12 July 2026.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The robbery reportedly resulted in the death of the security guard on duty and the theft of property valued at more than N400 million.

The four suspects identified by the police are Hamisu Nuhu, 34, from Jattu, whom the command described as the alleged mastermind, and Suleiman Rabiu, Hussaini Gago and Ibrahim Haruna.

The police did not disclose the specific items allegedly stolen or state whether the stolen property had been recovered.

Ammunition recovered from bus

In a separate operation on 20 October, the command said police operatives intercepted a Toyota Ultra bus belonging to GUO Transport Company along the Benin-Lagos Road.

A search of the vehicle, with registration number AGU721ZL, reportedly led to the recovery of 100 rounds of 7.62mm AK-47 ammunition, 50 rounds of 7.65mm ammunition and 200 rounds of 9mm ammunition.

The police also said three bags containing substances suspected to be cannabis were found in the vehicle.

The driver, Godwin Emeka, 37, and Enearu Louis, 40, identified by the command as the transport company’s operational manager, were arrested.

The police did not state where the ammunition and suspected cannabis originated, their intended destination or whether the suspects had been charged.

Cultism, armed robbery

The command also reported the arrest of four suspected members of the Eiye Secret Cult Confraternity following a confrontation with police operatives along Upper Siluko Road in Benin City on 17 October.

The police said operatives of the Violent Crime Response Unit were gathering intelligence when they received information that suspected cultists were planning to initiate new members.

According to the command, a man identified as Kevwe Kokori, who claimed to belong to a vigilante group, was initially intercepted and released. The police alleged that he later returned with about 20 men on motorcycles, armed with dangerous weapons, and attempted to attack the operatives, damaging the windscreen of a police vehicle.

The officers overpowered the group and arrested four suspects: Mr Kokori, 30; Omoregbe Iguma, 38; Gabriel Kokori, 32; and Emmanuel Friday, 39.

The command said the suspects confessed to belonging to the Eiye confraternity, adding that efforts were ongoing to arrest other members who escaped.

In another operation on 2 October, police arrested Chidiebere Osazee at an uncompleted building near AY Junction in Ulegun community, off the Benin-Abraka Road.

A cut-to-size single-barrelled gun was reportedly recovered from him. The police said he confessed to belonging to the Eiye confraternity and claimed ownership of the weapon. Efforts to arrest other suspected members were continuing.

The command also announced the arrest of two suspected armed robbers accused of dispossessing motorcycle riders of their motorcycles around Amagba, Ugbor and the Government Reserved Area of Benin City.

The police said the operation followed information provided by Blessing Ezekiel, who reported that her boyfriend, Nanta James, also known as Sani, often returned home late at night with bloodstains on his clothes.

Operatives of the Violent Crime Response Unit, working with officers from Ugbor Division and members of the Edo State Security Corps, arrested Mr James, whom the police said confessed to being an armed robber who specialised in stealing motorcycles from riders.

His alleged accomplice, Sambo Bala, was subsequently arrested. The police said the stolen motorcycle was recovered.

Sexual abuse, vehicle theft

The command said three suspects were in custody over separate sexual assault and defilement cases involving minors, including a girl aged two years and nine months and a four-year-old child.

The cases are being handled by the command’s Gender and Family Unit, and the suspects are expected to be charged to court, according to the police. The statement did not provide further details about the allegations or identify the suspects.

In another case, police arrested Osakpanwan Ekuase, 30, on 31 August over the alleged theft of five vehicles from a mechanic workshop in Ogheghe community, Benin City.

The command said the suspect allegedly posed as a worker at the workshop before stealing the vehicles.

The police called on residents to remain vigilant, cooperate with security agencies and promptly report suspicious activities.

World.title: Lagos backs Abuja-to-Lagos run, 226km triathlon for drug abuse, mental health awareness
World.content:
The Lagos State Government has backed two endurance challenges aimed at raising awareness about drug abuse and mental health issues, with organisers planning campaigns across several states.

The initiatives, led by Olufemi Osinubi and Dare Akinrodoye, received support from the Lagos State Sports Commission and the Ministry of Youth and Social Development during a meeting with the organisers on Tuesday.

While Mr Osinubi is using long-distance running to campaign against drug abuse, Mr Akinrodoye is deploying endurance activities to draw attention to depression, suicide and other mental health concerns.

The Director-General of the Lagos State Sports Commission, Lekan Fatodu, said the initiatives demonstrated how sporting activities could be used to address social challenges beyond conventional competition.

“As a government, we are always committed to supporting the positive endeavours of our people. Their commitment to uplifting people and social development is tied around what they do in sports,” Mr Fatodu said.

He said the physical demands of the challenges and their broader social objectives made them important platforms for communicating messages to the public.

“They engage in extraordinary sports activities that push the limits of human strength and physicality, and that is why this is important.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“What we do in sports, as well as youth and social development, is beyond the usual competition. We know there are many ways we can communicate with society through sports,” he added.

Running against drug abuse

Mr Osinubi is leading the Race Against Drug Abuse campaign, under which he and a team of runners plan to run from Abuja to Lagos.

The proposed challenge follows his recent completion of a similar run from Ibadan to Lagos as part of efforts to raise awareness about drug abuse.

He said his advocacy through running began in 2024, adding that he planned to extend the campaign beyond Lagos in collaboration with relevant government agencies, including the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA).

The initiative aims to use endurance running to draw public attention to the dangers of drug abuse, particularly among young people.

Taking mental health advocacy across three states

Mr Akinrodoye is using endurance challenges to promote awareness of mental health concerns, drawing inspiration from his personal struggles.

In 2024, he swam the 11.8-kilometre stretch of the Third Mainland Bridge to draw attention to mental health issues.

His latest initiative, tagged Mind Over Miles, is scheduled for 15 November and will take him across Osun, Ogun and Lagos states through a triathlon.

The challenge will begin with a 3.8-kilometre swim at Owala Dam in Osogbo, Osun State, followed by a 180-kilometre cycling ride from the dam to the Sagamu Interchange in Ogun State.

The final leg will be a 42.2-kilometre run to Johnson Jakande Tinubu Park in Alausa, Ikeja, Lagos.

Mr Akinrodoye said his decision to champion mental health awareness was inspired by his personal struggles.

Government pledges support

The Commissioner for Youth and Social Development, Mobolaji Ogunlende, said the campaigns aligned with the state government’s efforts to tackle drug abuse and improve mental health awareness.

“For us as a government, we don’t just discover and leave behind; we nurture and foster a great relationship.

“We currently have an ongoing advocacy in the fight against drug abuse, and we must continue to use all avenues that we have to continue.

“Mental health is real and the awareness needs to be amplified, so that the young people who are suffering know that the government is listening,” he said.

The planned challenges will extend the organisers’ advocacy beyond Lagos, using endurance activities to draw attention to issues affecting young people and encourage wider public engagement with drug abuse prevention and mental health awareness.

World.title: Abiodun salutes new Alaperu of Iperu-Remo, seeks peace, unity, dev’t
World.content:
Ogun State Governor, Prince Dapo Abiodun, has congratulated Oba Taiwo Adenaike Ogunbona, Fibigbuwa IV, on his ascension to the throne of Alaperu of Iperu-Remo, urging him to promote peace, unity and inclusive development in the ancient kingdom.

Oba Ogunbona ascended the revered throne of his forefathers on Saturday, 17 October 2026.

In a congratulatory message issued on behalf of his family, the Ogun State Government and the people of the state, Abiodun described the monarch’s emergence as the beginning of a new chapter in the history of Iperu-Remo.

The governor said the development reflected the enduring strength of traditional institutions, the richness of the state’s cultural heritage and the collective aspirations of the people for peace, unity, progress and development.

Abiodun, who described himself as a proud son of Iperu Akesan Land, said the monarch’s ascension was a moment of pride and celebration for the community, as well as a reminder of the collective responsibility to preserve its cherished customs, traditions and cultural values.

He noted that the throne came with the responsibility of preserving the kingdom’s heritage, fostering harmony among the people and providing purposeful traditional leadership that would advance the welfare and development of the community.

The governor expressed confidence that Oba Ogunbona would bring his experience, wisdom and commitment to bear on the responsibilities of the throne, adding that his reign would strengthen unity among the people and inspire renewed efforts towards the kingdom’s growth and prosperity.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Abiodun also urged the monarch to promote peaceful coexistence, encourage inclusive development and strengthen collaboration among the traditional institution, government and the people.

He prayed for God’s guidance, wisdom, sound health and strength for the monarch, wishing him a long, peaceful and prosperous reign.

The governor expressed hope that Oba Ogunbona’s reign would usher in unprecedented development in Iperu Akesan Land and leave a lasting legacy of honour, unity and progress for generations to come.

World.title: French city of Lyon bans ‘all protests’ on Saturday
World.content:
Saint-Denis Mayor Bally Bagayoko reacts as he stands between protesters and police officers during a demonstration of high-school students, in Paris on October 6, 2026, as part of a nationwide protest movement over learning conditions. Since late September, pupils have barred the entrances to hundreds of schools, complaining of teacher absences, overloaded timetables, dilapidated classrooms and buildings ill-adapted to rising temperatures, among other grievances. (Photo by Kenzo TRIBOUILLARD / AFP)

Officials have banned “all protests” in France’s third-biggest city of Lyon on Saturday, ahead of nationwide demonstrations that day following rallies last weekend that descended into widespread street violence.

The prefecture for the Rhone region said on Thursday in a statement to media that, “given the events of October 17, the prefect has decided to ban by decree all protests in the city of Lyon this Saturday, October 24”.

Lyon, like Paris and other French cities, suffered clashes and looting when masked youths took to city centre streets on the sidelines of mass rallies protesting high inflation.

The mayor of Lyon, Gregory Doucet, has said that his city experienced hours of “chaos” during the riots, with between 150 and 200 shops looted and a tourist office torched. Police arrested some 200 people.

The organisers of the rallies, the Yellow Vest movement and unions, have called for another round of nationwide demonstrations over the cost of living on Saturday, and a general strike and demonstrations on November 5.

French officials who found themselves unable to contain last weekend’s violence this week ordered three nights of curfews in parts of Paris, Lyon and some other cities to protect shopping districts.

AFP

World.title: Ebola: Medical laboratory scientists urge virtual campaigns ahead of 2027 elections
World.content:
The Association of Medical Laboratory Scientists of Nigeria (AMLSN), Kaduna State Branch, has advised political parties to campaign virtually to minimise physical contact amid the Ebola outbreak.

Mr Turman Benjamin, Chairman of the association in Kaduna gave the advice on Thursday in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in Kaduna.

Benjamin recommended social media, text messages, telephone calls and virtual meeting platforms such as Zoom and Google Meet as alternatives to physical political rallies.

He said the approach would reduce unnecessary contact and help minimise potential exposure while health authorities worked to contain the outbreak.

Benjamin urged the Kaduna State Government to intensify public awareness, trace any contacts linked to the confirmed case and ensure adequate protective equipment for healthcare workers.

He advised residents to avoid unnecessary physical contact, including handshakes and hugs, and observe appropriate hygiene measures.

The medical laboratory scientist said Ebola could be transmitted through direct contact with the blood and other bodily fluids of infected persons.

He also urged the public to avoid handling the bodies of suspected or confirmed Ebola victims without appropriate training and protective equipment.

Benjamin said only trained and properly equipped personnel should handle such bodies to reduce the risk of infection during burial preparations.

He called on the government to provide hospitals with adequate personal protective equipment, including gloves and other appropriate protective gear.

According to him, laboratory testing is essential to confirm Ebola because its early symptoms can resemble those of other illnesses, including malaria and typhoid fever.

Benjamin further advised the public to exercise caution when handling or consuming wild animals that could carry infectious diseases.

He urged the media to intensify public education on Ebola transmission, prevention and the importance of seeking prompt medical attention when symptoms develop.

The chairman also called for vigilance among healthcare workers and members of the public, stressing the importance of early detection and effective infection prevention measures.

The NAN reports that the Federal Government has confirmed one case of Ebola disease in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, with 44 close contacts identified for monitoring to prevent further transmission.

The patient, a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda, was admitted to a private hospital in the FCT, where she received treatment for several days before the diagnosis was confirmed.

The woman has since been placed in isolation and is receiving medical care, while health authorities have commenced contact tracing to identify and monitor people who may have been exposed to the virus.(NAN)

World.title: Nigerian newspapers review: No vaccine, specific treatment for Ebola strain in Nigeria – WHO
World.content:
In today’s Nigerian newspapers review programme, Today in the News, Vanguard leads with the World Health Organization (WHO) saying there is no vaccine or specific treatment for the index Ebola virus case detected in Nigeria, which carried the Bundibugyo strain.

Another headline features the Senate Committee on Public Accounts rejecting the volume of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS) imports reported by the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) for 2022 and 2023 over significant discrepancies with figures supplied by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL).

Vanguard also reports that the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, said only 108 out of about 39,000 underage candidates who sat the 2026 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME) have survived the Federal Government’s rigorous screening for possible admission into tertiary institutions.

Moving to another newspaper, The Guardian’s lead headline states that weak oversight and fiscal plan have left over 6,000 projects abandoned across the country, with their combined value running into trillions of naira.

The Punch reports that the diplomat diagnosed with the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola in the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja, has reportedly deteriorated into multi-organ failure, as the Federal Government and state governments intensify surveillance, contact tracing and emergency preparedness to prevent the spread of the deadly disease.

Lastly, The Nation reports that Vice President Kashim Shettima challenged state governments to stop depending on the Federal Government for solutions to their electricity challenges.

Vanguard News

World.title: Troops rescue four kidnapped victims in Zamfara, Kebbi
World.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

Troops of Sector 2, Operation Fansan Yamma, have rescued four kidnapped victims during separate intelligence-led operations in Zamfara and Kebbi states as the military intensifies efforts to combat terrorism and kidnapping across the North West.

According to the Army, the victims were rescued on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, in Maru Local Government Area of Zamfara State and between Bena and Sawade in Kebbi State.

“In Zamfara, troops rescued Mansur Shehu, 25, and Kadijat Haruna, 49, following a response to a reported terrorist incident on farmland across a river in Binoni Marafa, Maru LGA.

“In Kebbi, troops conducted a search-and-rescue operation after receiving reports of suspected terrorists moving with kidnapped victims from Dupindu Village, Kanya District, Danko-Wasagu LGA.

“The operation secured the freedom of Jimoh Su-Arege, 35, and Kalahe Danjuma, 41, who were subsequently handed over to the Seriki of Dipindu.

“The military said troops have continued to intensify patrols and surveillance across affected communities to strengthen security, dominate operational areas and deny criminal elements freedom of action.

“The successful operations highlight Operation Fansan Yamma’s sustained efforts to rescue abducted persons, disrupt terrorist activities and restore peace across Zamfara and Kebbi states,” the military said.

World.title: Ogun shuts schools as over 100 pupils are hospitalised after gas emissions
World.content:
Ogun State Governor Dapo Abiodun

By James Ogunnaike Abeokuta

The Ogun State government has ordered the closure of some schools in Ijebu-Ode, Ago-Iwoye and Ijebu-Igbo following the hospitalisation of more than 100 pupils on Wednesday after suspected exposure to an offensive gaseous substance.

The affected pupils were rushed to the State Hospital, Ijebu-Ode; the General Hospital, Ijebu-Igbo; and other healthcare facilities for medical attention.

Among the schools worst affected were Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School, Anglican Girls Grammar School, Ijebu-Ode, Itamerin Comprehensive High School and some schools in Ago-Iwoye.

A video circulating on social media showed pupils reportedly fainting and being rushed to hospitals following the incident. The state government had previously identified the substance as methane, although the precise source of the recurring emissions remains under investigation.

A teacher at one of the affected schools, who spoke to our correspondent on condition of anonymity, said the incident occurred at about 10am when pupils and staff began experiencing breathing difficulties, with some collapsing.

“The pupils and staff started inhaling the gas and began to have difficulty breathing. Some of them fainted and were rushed to hospitals,” the teacher said.

According to the teacher, some schools in Ago-Iwoye were forced to close at about 11am as the situation worsened.

“The worst-hit schools include Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School and Anglican Girls Grammar School in Ijebu-Ode. Some parents who heard about the incident also came to pick up their children because nobody knew what was happening,” the teacher added.

The teacher expressed concern over the recurring emissions, which have reportedly affected schools in the area since April, warning that pupils and staff continued to face potential health risks.

“We are all anxious about our health and that of our pupils. I think it is taking the government too long to get to the root of this mysterious gas leakage. The government has to do something quickly before it gets too late,” the teacher said.

Wednesday’s incident was the fourth reported occurrence of gaseous emissions in the Ijebu area since April, raising fresh concerns about the safety of pupils, teachers and other residents.

In April, about 40 pupils were reportedly affected by the emissions, while more than 120 others were hospitalised following another incident in May. A further occurrence on June 1 reportedly left 69 pupils requiring medical attention.

Schools previously affected included Our Lady of Apostles Secondary School, Epe Garage, Ijebu-Ode; Anglican Girls Grammar School, Ijebu-Ode; and St Anthony Grammar School, Ijebu-Imusin, among others.

The latest incident has renewed calls for the state government to establish the precise source of the emissions and implement a lasting solution to prevent further exposure.

Following an earlier occurrence, Governor Dapo Abiodun said the state government was collaborating with the Ministries of Environment and Health, the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority, and the Department of Geology at Olabisi Onabanjo University to determine the cause of the emissions.

Abiodun disclosed that gas analysers had been installed in affected schools after the initial incident, while preliminary findings pointed to methane as the substance involved.

“Preliminary findings suggest there may be geological factors involved, possibly fault lines common to these locations, which could be responsible for the emissions.

“We are awaiting the final report from the professionals handling the investigation,” the governor said in June.

When contacted on Wednesday, the state Commissioner for Environment, Ola Oresanya, said the government was on top of the situation.

Also speaking, the governor’s Senior Special Assistant and General Manager of the Ogun State Environmental Agency, Kehinde Bello, who visited affected areas in Ijebu-Ode and Ijebu-Igbo, linked the latest incident to underground gas emissions previously recorded in the area.

Bello said the situation was under control, assuring residents that the government would work towards finding a lasting solution to the recurring problem.

He said the government’s investigations had indicated that the phenomenon was a natural occurrence associated with geological and tectonic fault lines, rather than sabotage or a gas pipeline leak.

Bello urged residents to remain calm, adding that the affected pupils were expected to recover after receiving medical attention.

He also advised residents exposed to the odour to cover their noses and mouths with wet handkerchiefs rather than wear nose masks.

As of the time of filing this report, medical personnel were attending to affected pupils at various hospitals.

The recurring incidents have heightened concerns over the potential health risks posed by the emissions, particularly to schoolchildren and teachers, with residents awaiting the outcome of investigations and the implementation of measures to prevent further occurrences.

World.title: Iran’s Guards threaten to hit US bases in retaliation for Hormuz escorts
World.content:
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards on Thursday threatened to strike American bases across the Middle East if the US military continues to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz.

“The US military must know that if this trend continues, the conflict will extend to its bases in the region,” the Guards, the ideological arm of Iran’s military, said in a statement on their Sepah News website.

“This is a serious warning,” they added.

Iran claims control over Hormuz, a strategic shipping route through which one-fifth of the world’s oil supplies passed before war broke out in February.

It regularly attacks ships that attempt to navigate the strait without its authorisation.

But the US military has been escorting vessels through the waterway in increasing numbers, with Iran responding by stepping up attacks.

Four ships were hit in the area overnight as they attempted to pass through the wider Gulf, Iranian forces said on Thursday.

Washington has also been maintaining a naval blockade on Iranian ports in an attempt to squeeze the country’s economy, while negotiations to end the conflict are deadlocked.

Hormuz, bordered to the north by Iran and to the south by Oman, is only about 30 kilometres (19 miles) wide at its narrowest point and is a critical route for ships carrying oil and gas from energy-rich Gulf countries.

World.title: Sowore claps back after Senator Ajibola called him ‘skit maker’
World.content:
Omoyele Sowore

The presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), Omoyele Sowore, has hit back at the National Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Ajibola Basiru, after the senator described him as a “skit maker” and “comedian”.

Sowore, in a statement posted on X, recalled his longstanding relationship with Basiru, saying they fought against military dictatorship together in the 1990s.

He also accused the APC chieftain of abandoning the democratic ideals they once defended because of the privileges of his current political position.

The exchange followed Basiru’s appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday, where he described Sowore as a skit maker.

Responding, Sowore shared a photograph of himself with Basiru taken in 1998, when he led the Congress of Progressive Youths (COPY), a pro-democracy group.

“I watched an interview on Politics Today on Channels Television, anchored by Seun Okinbaloye, in which the APC National Secretary, Ajibola Basiru, called me a ‘skit maker’ and ‘comedian’,” he wrote.

Sowore said he received Basiru at the University of Lagos after the latter was expelled from the University of Ilorin in 1992 over student activism.

He said he and other activists, including Kunle Adegoke, popularly known as K-Rad, helped Basiru secure an opportunity to return to the university and study law.

“Both eventually graduated with flying colours and went on to accomplish great things,” Sowore said, adding that their shared history made Basiru’s remarks particularly disappointing.

He argued that the struggle for democracy and human dignity should not be dismissed as entertainment, insisting that his activism remained consistent with the ideals they defended during military rule.

“The struggle for justice, democracy, freedom and the preservation of human dignity is neither skit-making nor comedy,” he said.

Sowore also faulted Basiru’s argument that opposition candidates should be ashamed of losing to President Bola Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election, which he described as deeply flawed.

He maintained that political appointments were temporary and predicted that Tinubu’s administration, like previous military regimes, would eventually leave office.

“Political appointments are temporary. Tinubu’s regime will come and go, just like the military regimes we confronted in our youth,” he said.

Sowore concluded by accusing Basiru of turning against the ideals he once championed.

“What is truly comical is watching yesterday’s beneficiaries of resistance become today’s defenders of the very oppression they once fought against,” he wrote.

World.title: Ekiti Assembly passes State Police Bill
World.content:
By Rotimi Ojomoyela

The Ekiti State House of Assembly has passed the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, seeking to provide for the establishment of State Police Services in Nigeria.

The bill scaled second and third readings during plenary on Tuesday, with all 21 members present voting in support, signalling the Assembly’s endorsement of decentralised policing.

Following its passage, the Speaker, Rt. Hon. Adeoye Stephen Aribasoye, directed the Clerk of the House to transmit the document to the National Assembly alongside observations made by the state legislature.

Speaking on the bill, Aribasoye said state police had remained at the forefront of national discourse for over two decades, noting that the Ekiti Assembly had a historic opportunity to take a position.

He stressed the need for effective and responsive security, saying Nigeria’s policing challenges required practical solutions.

“Nigerians had repeatedly expressed concerns over delayed responses to distress calls, limitations in operational reach and the distance between law enforcement agencies and the communities they were meant to protect,” he said.

The Speaker added that inadequate and poorly coordinated local policing in some areas had contributed to insecurity, threatening livelihoods, disrupting education, undermining business confidence and eroding public trust.

He said a properly structured State Police system could strengthen accountability by bringing policing leadership and oversight closer to the people and their elected representatives, subject to constitutional safeguards.

According to him, the country could not afford unnecessary delays in addressing security challenges, describing State Police as “a long-overdue practical necessity rather than a mere theoretical preference.”

In its report, the Committee of the Whole House recommended concurrence to the bill, subject to an amendment to Section 317A(5).

The committee said it considered the bill clause by clause and deliberated on the proposed constitutional framework for the establishment and operation of State Police Services.

It proposed the insertion of the words “an Act of the National Assembly or a Law of the State House of Assembly, as applicable” after the words “this Constitution” in the newly inserted Section 317A(5).

The observation, the committee noted, is intended to expressly recognise the legislative authority of the National Assembly and State Houses of Assembly, within their respective constitutional jurisdictions, in authorising relevant security arrangements.

World.title: Gov Otu Presents N987.8bn 2027 Budget
World.content:
Cross River State Governor, Bassey Otu, yesterday presented a proposed N987.8 billion budget for the 2027 fiscal year to the state House of Assembly, christening it the ‘Budget of Consolidation and Renewed Hope’, and reaffirming his administration’s commitment to sustainable development, fiscal discipline, and inclusive economic growth.

Presenting the estimates in Calabar, Otu described the budget as more than an aggregation of figures, characterising it as “a solemn and sacred pact laden with the trust, expectation and aspiration of the people for their improved livelihoods.”

He said its successful implementation would depend on prudent resource management, accountability and disciplined public expenditure, underscoring his administration’s determination to translate its social contract with the people into tangible improvements in their living conditions.

The proposed budget, valued at precisely N987,808,089,235.92, represents an increase of approximately 2.57 per cent over the 2026 budget.

Capital expenditure accounts for N708.43 billion, representing 71.72 per cent of the total provision, while recurrent expenditure stands at N279.38 billion, or 28.28 per cent. The substantial capital allocation, according to the governor, reflects the government’s determination to prioritise infrastructure, human capital development and productive investments capable of stimulating economic activity.

Otu explained that the 2027–2029 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework and Fiscal Strategy Paper provided the foundation for the estimates, adding that the budget would sustain ongoing programmes while opening new pathways for investment, employment creation and improved public services.

“The imperative of this exercise underscores our collective resolve to chart a sustainable course for the growth and development of our state,” he declared.

Addressing concerns surrounding the state’s debt profile, the governor maintained that his administration had refrained from obtaining fresh domestic and external loans since assuming office in 2023. Citing verifiable indices from the National Bureau of Statistics and the Debt Management Office, he said Cross River remained among the few states that had not contracted new loans during the period. He attributed the state’s existing debt burden to obligations inherited from previous administrations, explaining that debt servicing had constrained the pace at which available resources could be deployed to development projects.

He further clarified that the naira value of external debt had been affected by currency devaluation and foreign-exchange liberalisation.

“I cannot, and will never mortgage the future of our children with unsustainable loans,” Otu declared, pledging to strengthen internally generated revenue, maximise federal allocations and attract development assistance and private-sector investment to finance the state’s development priorities.

Reviewing the performance of the 2026 budget, the governor acknowledged the pressures of exchange-rate volatility, rising operational costs, supply-chain disruptions and inherited debt obligations. He disclosed that the administration had collaborated with the legislature to enact a supplementary budget, raising the spending framework to N963.07 billion to accommodate urgent interventions and counterpart-funding requirements.

Among the achievements highlighted was the delivery of more than 608 kilometres of interconnected road projects across the three senatorial districts, including the Nsan–Oban Road in Akamkpa, the Adiabo–Ikoneto Road in Odukpani and the Yahe–Ebo–Wanakade Road in Yala.

He also reported progress in rural electrification through solar streetlights, mini-grids and network rehabilitation, describing the interventions as essential to reopening economic corridors, improving mobility and restoring commercial activity in underserved communities.

Agriculture featured prominently in the governor’s account of the administration’s economic transformation agenda. Otu disclosed that more than 20,000 bags of fertiliser had been distributed to 8,000 farmers, while over one million improved oil-palm, cowpea and cocoa seedlings had been provided to farmers across the state. He also highlighted the establishment of a 50,000-hectare rice project and support for more than 5,300 livestock farmers, alongside loans, grants and agricultural machinery for smallholder and large-scale producers.

According to him, an N18 billion offtake arrangement had helped advance the state’s agricultural initiatives, while the cash-crop revolution was strengthening the productive capacity of farmers.

“There is no food security without agriculture,” he asserted, adding that the government intended to become Nigeria’s leading cocoa and oil-palm-producing state through expanded cultivation, mechanisation, agro-allied industries and private-sector partnerships.

On healthcare, education and public-sector welfare, Otu outlined interventions designed to improve access, strengthen institutions and enhance service delivery. He cited the renovation and rehabilitation of hospitals, the establishment of medical oxygen plants in Calabar and Ogoja in partnership with UNICEF, and the upgrading of state-owned Schools of Nursing and Midwifery to accreditation standards. He also highlighted a reported 95 per cent routine immunisation coverage, implementation of the Consolidated Medical Salary Structure for medical workers and an increase in the retirement age of health workers from 60 to 65 years.

In education, he said the state had deployed more than N17 billion in Universal Basic Education Commission intervention funds, supported classroom construction and rehabilitation, paid WAEC examination fees for 43,694 Cross River State indigenes and approved the promotion of more than 14,000 teaching and non-teaching staff.

The government, he added, was targeting a literacy rate of 98 per cent from the current estimated 80.7 per cent, while strengthening technical and vocational education to equip young people with employable and entrepreneurial skills.

The 2027 estimates also assign prominent roles to aviation, transportation, maritime development and tourism in the state’s economic diversification strategy. The governor disclosed the integration of a new Bombardier CRJ regional jet into the state’s aviation assets, bringing the fleet to five aircraft, alongside accelerated construction work at the Obudu International Passenger and Cargo Airport.
